(
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Reading and writing DIMACS ".cnf" files and converting to and from HOL.   *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* This does not rigorously enforce many of the syntactic restrictions and   *)
(* in particular it completely ignores the "p" line (or many "p" lines)      *)
(* specifying the number of variables and clauses. It also doesn't do any    *)
(* analysis of the clauses to rule out tautologies etc.                      *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Equivalents of "conjuncts" and "length o conjuncts" but tail recursive.   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let list_conjuncts =
  let rec aux acc tm =
    match tm with
      Comb(Comb(Const("/\\",_),l),t) -> aux (l::acc) t
    | _ -> tm::acc in
  fun tm -> rev(aux [] tm)
in
let rec count_conjuncts n tm =
  match tm with
    Comb(Comb(Const("/\\",_),_),t) -> count_conjuncts (n+1) t
  | _ -> n
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Parsing and processing.                                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let stripcomments s =
  match String.index_opt s 'c' with
    Some i -> String.sub s 0 i
  | None -> s
in
let process_lines f p fname =
  let fd =
    try open_in fname
    with Sys_error _ -> failwith("read_dimacs: can't open "^fname) in
  let rec suck_lines acc =
    let l = try [input_line fd] with End_of_file -> [] in
    if l = [] then rev_itlist (@) acc [] else
    let y = f(hd l) in
    suck_lines (if p y then y::acc else acc) in
  let data = suck_lines [] in
  (close_in fd; data)
in
let rec parse_clauses acc cur l =
  match l with
    ""::t -> parse_clauses  acc cur t
  | "0"::t -> parse_clauses (rev cur::acc) [] t
  | n::t -> parse_clauses acc (int_of_string n::cur) t
  | [] -> rev acc
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Reading and writing betweeen DIMACS file and int list list in OCaml       *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let read_dimacs fname =
  let l = process_lines
           (String.split_on_char ' ' o
            String.map (function '\t' -> ' ' | c -> c) o stripcomments)
           (function "p"::_ -> false | _ -> true) fname in
  parse_clauses [] [] l
in
let write_dimacs =
  let string_of_clause cl =
    itlist (fun t s -> string_of_int t ^ " " ^ s) cl "0\n" in
  fun fname cls ->
    let fd =
      try open_out fname
      with Sys_error _ -> failwith("write_dimacs: can't open "^fname) in
    let n = rev_itlist (rev_itlist (max o abs)) cls 0
    and m = rev_itlist (fun _ n -> n + 1) cls 0 in
    (output_string fd ("p cnf "^string_of_int n^" "^string_of_int m^"\n");
     do_list (output_string fd o string_of_clause) cls;
     close_out fd)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Translation between HOL terms and int list list, with variable mappings.  *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let clauses_of_term vmap tm =
  let cnf_of_literal t =
    match t with
      Comb(Const("~",_),s) -> -(vmap s)
    | _ -> vmap t in
  map (map cnf_of_literal o disjuncts) (list_conjuncts tm)
in
let term_of_literal amap n =
   if n < 0 then mk_neg(amap (-n)) else amap n
in
let term_of_clause =
  let false_tm = `F` in
  fun amap ->
    let rec aux tm l =
      match l with
        h::t -> aux (mk_disj(term_of_literal amap h,tm)) t
      | [] -> tm in
    fun l ->
      match rev l with
        [] -> false_tm
      | h::t -> aux (term_of_literal amap h) t
in
let term_of_clauses =
  let true_tm = `T` in
  fun amap ->
    let rec aux tm l =
      match l with
        h::t -> aux (mk_conj(term_of_clause amap h,tm)) t
      | [] -> tm in
    fun l ->
      match rev l with
        [] -> true_tm
      | h::t -> aux (term_of_clause amap h) t
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Composite function not directly creating the int list list and picking a  *)
(* default numbering of the atoms from the call to "atoms".                  *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let dimacs_of_hol fname tm =
  let m = count_conjuncts 1 tm in
  let ats = atoms tm in
  let n = length ats in
  let _,vmap =
    rev_itlist (fun a (n,f) -> (n+1,(a |-> n) f)) ats (1,undefined) in
  let cnf_of_literal t =
    match t with
      Comb(Const("~",_),s) -> -(apply vmap s)
    | _ -> apply vmap t in
  let string_of_clause cl =
   itlist (fun t s -> string_of_int(cnf_of_literal t) ^ " " ^ s)
          (disjuncts cl) "0\n" in
  let fd =
    try open_out fname
    with Sys_error _ -> failwith("dimacs_of_hol: can't open "^fname) in
  (output_string fd ("p cnf "^string_of_int n^" "^string_of_int m^"\n");
   do_list (output_string fd o string_of_clause) (list_conjuncts tm);
   close_out fd)
in
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Tools to put formulas in definitional (Tseitin) CNF form for SAT solvers. *)
(* The temporary variables are implicit for actual proof reconstruction; all *)
(* steps simply use the corresponding expansion directly.                    *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

let exploit_conjunctive_structure = ref true
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Split up a theorem according to conjuncts, in a general sense.            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let GCONJUNCTS =
  let [pth_ni1; pth_ni2; pth_no1; pth_no2; pth_an1; pth_an2; pth_nn] =
    (map UNDISCH_ALL o CONJUNCTS o TAUT)
    `(~(p ==> q) ==> p) /\
     (~(p ==> q) ==> ~q) /\
     (~(p \/ q) ==> ~p) /\
     (~(p \/ q) ==> ~q) /\
     (p /\ q ==> p) /\
     (p /\ q ==> q) /\
     (~ ~p ==> p)` in
  let p_tm = concl pth_an1 and q_tm = concl pth_an2 in
  let rec GCONJUNCTS th acc =
    match (concl th) with
      Comb(Const("~",_),Comb(Comb(Const("==>",_),p),q)) ->
       GCONJUNCTS (PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth_ni1))
                  (GCONJUNCTS (PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth_ni2))
                              acc)
    | Comb(Const("~",_),Comb(Comb(Const("\\/",_),p),q)) ->
       GCONJUNCTS (PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth_no1))
                  (GCONJUNCTS (PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth_no2))
                              acc)
    | Comb(Comb(Const("/\\",_),p),q) ->
       GCONJUNCTS (PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth_an1))
                  (GCONJUNCTS (PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth_an2))
                              acc)
    | Comb(Const("~",_),Comb(Const("~",_),p)) ->
          GCONJUNCTS (PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm] pth_nn)) acc
    | _ -> th::acc in
  fun th -> GCONJUNCTS th []
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Generate fresh variable names (could just use genvars).                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let propvar i = mk_var("x"^string_of_int i,bool_ty)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Set up the basic definitional arrangement.                                *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let rec localdefs tm (n,defs,lfn) =
  if is_neg tm then
    let n1,v1,defs1,lfn1 = localdefs (rand tm) (n,defs,lfn) in
    let tm' = mk_neg v1 in
    try (n1,apply defs1 tm',defs1,lfn1) with Failure _ ->
    let n2 = n1 + 1 in
    let v2 = propvar n2 in
    n2,v2,(tm' |-> v2) defs1,(v2 |-> tm) lfn1
  else if is_conj tm || is_disj tm || is_imp tm || is_iff tm then
    let n1,v1,defs1,lfn1 = localdefs (lhand tm) (n,defs,lfn) in
    let n2,v2,defs2,lfn2 = localdefs (rand tm) (n1,defs1,lfn1) in
    let tm' = mk_comb(mk_comb(rator(rator tm),v1),v2) in
    try (n2,apply defs2 tm',defs2,lfn2) with Failure _ ->
    let n3 = n2 + 1 in
    let v3 = propvar n3 in
    n3,v3,(tm' |-> v3) defs2,(v3 |-> tm) lfn2
  else try (n,apply defs tm,defs,lfn) with Failure _ ->
       let n1 = n + 1 in
       let v1 = propvar n1 in
       n1,v1,(tm |-> v1) defs,(v1 |-> tm) lfn
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Just translate to fresh variables, but otherwise leave unchanged.         *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let rec transvar (n,tm,vdefs,lfn) =
  if is_neg tm then
    let n1,tm1,vdefs1,lfn1 = transvar (n,rand tm,vdefs,lfn) in
    n1,mk_comb(rator tm,tm1),vdefs1,lfn1
  else if is_conj tm || is_disj tm || is_imp tm || is_iff tm then
    let n1,tm1,vdefs1,lfn1 = transvar (n,lhand tm,vdefs,lfn) in
    let n2,tm2,vdefs2,lfn2 = transvar (n1,rand tm,vdefs1,lfn1) in
    n2,mk_comb(mk_comb(rator(rator tm),tm1),tm2),vdefs2,lfn2
  else try n,apply vdefs tm,vdefs,lfn with Failure _ ->
       let n1 = n + 1 in
       let v1 = propvar n1 in
       n1,v1,(tm |-> v1) vdefs,(v1 |-> tm) lfn
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Determine if a term is (strictly) clausal, i.e. is a conjunction of       *)
(* disjunctions of literals, all of which are right-associated.              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let is_atom tm =
  match tm with
    Comb(Comb(Const("/\\",_),l),r)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("\\/",_),l),r)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("==>",_),l),r)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("=",Tyapp("fun",[Tyapp("bool",[]);_])),l),r)
        -> false
  | Comb(Const("~",_),l) -> false
  | _ -> true
in
let is_literal tm =
  match tm with
    Comb(Const("~",_),t) -> is_atom t
  | _ -> is_atom tm
in
let rec is_clausal tm =
  match tm with
    Comb(Comb(Const("\\/",_),l),r) -> is_literal l && is_clausal r
  | _ -> is_literal tm
in
let rec is_strictcnf tm =
  match tm with
    Comb(Comb(Const("/\\",_),l),r) -> is_clausal l && is_strictcnf r
  | _ -> is_clausal tm
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Now do the definitional arrangement but not wastefully at the top.        *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let definitionalize =
  let transform_imp =
    let pth = TAUT `(p ==> q) <=> ~p \/ q` in
    let ptm = rand(concl pth) in
    let p_tm = rand(lhand ptm) and q_tm = rand ptm in
    fun th -> let ip,q = dest_comb(concl th) in
              let p = rand ip in
              EQ_MP (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth) th
  and transform_iff_1 =
    let pth = UNDISCH(TAUT `(p <=> q) ==> (p \/ ~q)`) in
    let ptm = concl pth in
    let p_tm = lhand ptm and q_tm = rand(rand ptm) in
    fun th -> let ip,q = dest_comb(concl th) in
              let p = rand ip in
              PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth)
  and transform_iff_2 =
    let pth = UNDISCH(TAUT `(p <=> q) ==> (~p \/ q)`) in
    let ptm = concl pth in
    let p_tm = rand(lhand ptm) and q_tm = rand ptm in
    fun th -> let ip,q = dest_comb(concl th) in
              let p = rand ip in
              PROVE_HYP th (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth) in
  let definitionalize th (n,tops,defs,lfn) =
    let t = concl th in
    if is_clausal t then
      let n',v,defs',lfn' = transvar (n,t,defs,lfn) in
      (n',(v,th)::tops,defs',lfn')
    else if is_neg t then
       let n1,v1,defs1,lfn1 = localdefs (rand t) (n,defs,lfn) in
       (n1,(mk_neg v1,th)::tops,defs1,lfn1)
    else if is_disj t then
      let n1,v1,defs1,lfn1 = localdefs (lhand t) (n,defs,lfn) in
      let n2,v2,defs2,lfn2 = localdefs (rand t) (n1,defs1,lfn1) in
      (n2,(mk_disj(v1,v2),th)::tops,defs2,lfn2)
    else if is_imp t then
      let n1,v1,defs1,lfn1 = localdefs (lhand t) (n,defs,lfn) in
      let n2,v2,defs2,lfn2 = localdefs (rand t) (n1,defs1,lfn1) in
      (n2,(mk_disj(mk_neg v1,v2),transform_imp th)::tops,defs2,lfn2)
    else if is_iff t then
      let n1,v1,defs1,lfn1 = localdefs (lhand t) (n,defs,lfn) in
      let n2,v2,defs2,lfn2 = localdefs (rand t) (n1,defs1,lfn1) in
      (n2,(mk_disj(v1,mk_neg v2),transform_iff_1 th)::
          (mk_disj(mk_neg v1,v2),transform_iff_2 th)::tops,defs2,lfn2)
    else
      let n',v,defs',lfn' = localdefs t (n,defs,lfn) in
      (n',(v,th)::tops,defs',lfn') in
  definitionalize
in
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* Translate .lrat proof file into HOL inferences and prove a .cnf formula.  *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* This is designed for the .lrat proofs produced by Cadical; those do not   *)
(* use proper RAT lemmas, and have a particularly clean and simple syntax.   *)
(* This might not work for the .lrat files produced by other provers.        *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The first argument "amap" is the mapping from .cnf variable numbers to    *)
(* HOL propositions, e.g. 123 |-> `p123:bool`.                               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* For the _GEN functions there are two filename arguments, one for the CNF  *)
(* problem file and the other for the corresponding LRAT proof file. For the *)
(* non-GEN forms there is a single argument that is the root "filename"      *)
(* for the corresponding CNF file "filename.cnf" and LRAT "filename.lrat".   *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* In all cases, non-absolute filenames are interpreted relative to the      *)
(* directory pointed at by the reference "problem_dir".                      *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

let problem_dir = ref "/tmp"
in
let LRAT_PROVE_GEN =
  let ptm = `p:bool` and qtm = `q:bool` in
  let orth = REFL(rator(rator(mk_disj(ptm,ptm)))) in
  let number_clauses =
    let rec aux f n (cl,th) =
      match cl with
        [c] -> (n |-> (c,th)) f
      | c::cs ->
          let th1,th2 = CONJ_PAIR th in
          aux ((n |-> (c,th1)) f) (n + 1) (cs,th2)
      | _ -> failwith "number_clauses: there are no clauses" in
    aux undefined 1 in
  let DEDRUP_RULE =
    let pth = SPEC ptm (TAUT `!p. (~p ==> F) <=> p`) in
    fun th -> EQ_MP (INST [rand(lhand(concl th)),ptm] pth) th in
  let ORIFY (c,th) uths = (-c |-> (th,MK_COMB(orth,th))) uths in
  let EQUIFY =
    let nth = SPEC ptm (TAUT `!p. ~p <=> (p <=> F)`)
    and pth = SPEC ptm (TAUT `!p. p <=> (~p <=> F)`) in
    fun (c,th) uths ->
      let tm = concl th in
      let th' =
        if c < 0 then EQ_MP (INST [rand tm,ptm] nth) th
        else EQ_MP (INST [tm,ptm] pth) th in
      let th'' = MK_COMB(orth,th') in
      (-c |-> (th',th'')) uths in
    let upth_l = SPEC ptm (TAUT `!p. F \/ p <=> p`)
    and upth_r = SPEC ptm (TAUT `!p. p \/ F <=> p`)
    and upth_b = TAUT `F \/ F <=> F` in
  fun amap cnfname lratname ->
    let adjust s =
      if Filename.is_relative s
      then Filename.concat (!problem_dir) s else s in
    let probfile = adjust cnfname and lratfile = adjust lratname in
    let prb = read_dimacs probfile in
    let ctm = term_of_clauses amap prb in
    let nvars = rev_itlist (rev_itlist (max o abs)) prb 0 in
    let upth_l_pos = Array.init (nvars+1)
      (fun v -> if v = 0 then upth_b else INST [amap v,ptm] upth_l)
    and upth_l_neg = Array.init (nvars+1)
      (fun v -> if v = 0 then upth_b else INST [mk_neg(amap v),ptm] upth_l)
    and upth_r_pos = Array.init (nvars+1)
      (fun v -> if v = 0 then upth_b else INST [amap v,ptm] upth_r)
    and upth_r_neg = Array.init (nvars+1)
      (fun v -> if v = 0 then upth_b else INST [mk_neg(amap v),ptm] upth_r) in
    let upth_t_pos = Array.init (nvars+1)
        (fun v -> REFL(rator(lhand(concl(Array.get upth_r_pos v)))))
    and upth_t_neg = Array.init (nvars+1)
        (fun v -> REFL(rator(lhand(concl(Array.get upth_r_neg v))))) in
    let UNITPROP =
      fun uths ->
        let rec conv (cl,tm) =
            match (cl,tm) with
              [c],_ -> (try 0,fst(apply uths c) with Failure _ -> c,REFL tm)
            | (c::cs,Comb(Comb(_,l),r)) ->
                (let rl,rth = conv(cs,r) in
                 try let lth,lth' = apply uths c in
                     let th = MK_COMB(lth',rth) in
                     rl,TRANS th (if rl < 0 then Array.get upth_l_neg (-rl)
                                  else Array.get upth_l_pos rl)
                 with Failure _ ->
                   c,
                (if c < 0 then
                   TRANS (MK_COMB(Array.get upth_t_neg (-c),rth))
                         (Array.get upth_r_neg (-c))
                 else
                   TRANS (MK_COMB(Array.get upth_t_pos c,rth))
                         (Array.get upth_r_pos c)))
            | _ -> failwith "UNITPROP: Sanity check" in
      fun (cl,th) -> let d,th' = conv(cl,concl th) in d,EQ_MP th' th in
    let UNITPROPS cls =
      let rec rule uths pf =
        match pf with
          c::ops -> let p,th = UNITPROP uths (apply cls c) in
                    if p = 0 then th else rule (EQUIFY (p,th) uths) ops
        | [] -> failwith "UNITPROPS: did not reach a contradiction" in
      fun dths -> rule (rev_itlist ORIFY dths undefined) in
    let NEGATE_CLAUSE =
      let pth_lor = UNDISCH(SPECL[ptm;qtm]
       (TAUT `!p q. ~(p \/ q) ==> (p <=> F)`))
      and pth_ror = UNDISCH(SPECL[ptm;qtm] (TAUT `!p q. ~(p \/ q) ==> ~q`))
      and pth_ide = SPEC ptm (TAUT `!p. ~p <=> (p <=> F)`) in
      let nrule (c,th) =
        let Comb(_,t) = concl th in
        -c,EQ_MP (INST [t,ptm] pth_ide) th in
      let rec rule (cl,th) =
        match (cl,concl th) with
          [c],_ -> [nrule(c,th)]
        | (c::cs,Comb(_,Comb(Comb(_,l),r))) ->
            let iptho = INST [l,ptm; r,qtm] in
            let th1 = EQ_MP (DEDUCT_ANTISYM_RULE th (iptho pth_lor)) th
            and th2 = EQ_MP (DEDUCT_ANTISYM_RULE th (iptho pth_ror)) th in
            (-c,th1)::rule (cs,th2)
        | [],_ -> []
        | _ -> failwith "NEGATE_CLAUSE: sanity check" in
      rule in
      let LRAT_ADD (n,cl,pf) cls =
        let ctm = term_of_clause amap cl in
        let ctm' = mk_neg ctm in
        let dths = NEGATE_CLAUSE (cl,ASSUME ctm') in
        let fth = UNITPROPS cls dths pf in
        let th = DEDRUP_RULE(DISCH ctm' fth) in
        (n |-> (cl,th)) cls in
      let rec PROCESS_LRAT fd m cls =
        match (try Some(input_line fd) with End_of_file -> None) with
         Some s ->
           (match String.split_on_char ' ' s with
             ns::"d"::dnums ->
                  let n = int_of_string ns
                  and cls' = rev_itlist (undefine o int_of_string) dnums cls in
                  PROCESS_LRAT fd n cls'
            | ns::clap ->
                  let n = int_of_string ns
                  and clans = map int_of_string clap in
                  let i = index 0 clans in
                  let c,u = chop_list i clans in
                  let cls' = LRAT_ADD (n,c,butlast(tl u)) cls in
                  PROCESS_LRAT fd n cls'
            | _ -> failwith "PROCESS_LRAT: Can't parse input line")
        | None -> apply cls m in
    let cls = number_clauses(prb,ASSUME ctm) in
    let fd =
      try open_in lratfile
      with Sys_error _ -> failwith("LRAT_PROVE: can't open "^lratfile) in
    let _,fth = PROCESS_LRAT fd 0 cls in
    let _ = close_in fd in
    NOT_INTRO(DISCH ctm fth)
in
let LRAT_PROVE amap basename =
  LRAT_PROVE_GEN amap (basename^".cnf") (basename^".lrat")
in
let LRAT_REFUTE_GEN amap cnfname lratname =
    UNDISCH(NOT_ELIM(LRAT_PROVE_GEN amap cnfname lratname))
in
let LRAT_REFUTE amap basename =
   LRAT_REFUTE_GEN amap (basename^".cnf") (basename^".lrat")
in
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* csat_lib.ml -- certified-SAT close for HOL Light word goals.               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Connects the missing BITBLAST_THEN -> CADICAL_PROVE edge.  The pinned     *)
(* Examples/bitblast.ml defines BITBLAST_CADICAL only inside a (**** ...     *)
(* ****) block, so it is never loaded.  This file supplies it.               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Kernel trust: every SAT refutation is replayed by LRAT_REFUTE_GEN inside  *)
(* the HOL Light kernel (Cadical/ldrup.ml).  No solver certificate is trusted *)
(* and no compiler enters the trusted base.                                  *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* CaDiCaL 2.1.2 emits LRAT text directly with --no-binary --lrat; the       *)
(* lrat-trim post-pass used by Cadical/cadical.ml is therefore optional.     *)
(* CSAT_PROVE is CADICAL_PROVE with that native-LRAT refuter substituted.    *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* Unix (wall-clock) is loaded by the driver before this file is loadt-ed. *)
let csat_now () = Unix.gettimeofday ()
in
let csat_debug = ref false
in
(* --- backward-closure LRAT trim (IX.63) ---------------------------------- *)
(*
   Between the solver writing its LRAT and the kernel replaying it, keep only
   the additions the empty clause depends on through positive RUP hints, in
   the original file order, and drop every deletion line.  A kept clause may
   still be hinted by a kept clause, so the replay is the same kernel code on
   a smaller file.

   Conservative by construction.  If any hint in the file is negative (RAT),
   or the last addition does not assert the empty clause, or the file is not
   understood (blank/duplicate ids/malformed line/IO error), the file is left
   untouched and `CSAT_TRIM skipped=<reason>` is printed.  There is no
   fallback on replay failure: a wrong closure makes LRAT_REFUTE_GEN fail,
   which is the intended behaviour.

   This block is delimited by BEGIN/END CSAT_TRIM_STANDALONE so that
   tests/csat_trim_selftest.sh can exercise exactly the shipped text outside
   HOL Light.  Keep it free of HOL Light names and of structure items other
   than `let` (the emitted answer inlines each phrase as a nested binding). *)
(* BEGIN CSAT_TRIM_STANDALONE *)
let csat_lrat_tokens s =
  let n = String.length s and out = ref [] and buf = Buffer.create 24 in
  let flush () =
    if Buffer.length buf > 0 then
      (out := Buffer.contents buf :: !out; Buffer.clear buf) in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    match s.[i] with
    | ' ' | '\t' | '\r' -> flush ()
    | c -> Buffer.add_char buf c
  done;
  flush ();
  List.rev !out
in
let csat_lrat_parse raw toks =
  let all_nonneg ts =
    List.for_all
      (fun t -> try int_of_string t >= 0 with _ -> false) ts in
  match toks with
  | id_s :: "d" :: rest ->
      (try
         if int_of_string id_s = 0 || not (all_nonneg rest) then None
         else Some (int_of_string id_s, None, raw)
       with _ -> None)
  | id_s :: rest ->
      (try
         let id = int_of_string id_s in
         if id = 0 then None else
         let rec first_zero acc = function
           | [] -> None
           | "0" :: tl -> Some (List.rev acc, tl)
           | t :: tl -> first_zero (t :: acc) tl in
         match first_zero [] rest with
         | None -> None
         | Some (lits, tail) ->
             List.iter (fun t -> ignore (int_of_string t)) lits;
             let hs = List.fold_left
               (fun acc t ->
                  let v = int_of_string t in
                  if v = 0 then acc else v :: acc)
               [] tail in
             Some (id, Some (Array.of_list (List.rev hs)), raw)
       with _ -> None)
  | [] -> None
in
(* (id, hints option, raw) for every non-blank line, plus the file size. *)
let csat_lrat_read path =
  try
    let ic = open_in_bin path in
    let n = in_channel_length ic in
    let text = really_input_string ic n in
    close_in ic;
    let parsed = ref [] and start = ref 0 and bad = ref None in
    let add_line stop =
      let raw = String.sub text !start (stop - !start) in
      let toks = csat_lrat_tokens raw in
      if toks <> [] then
        (match csat_lrat_parse raw toks with
         | None -> bad := Some "malformed"
         | Some p -> parsed := p :: !parsed) in
    for i = 0 to n - 1 do
      if text.[i] = '\n' then (add_line i; start := i + 1)
    done;
    if !start < n then add_line n;
    match !bad with
    | Some r -> Error r
    | None -> Ok (Array.of_list (List.rev !parsed), n)
  with _ -> Error "io_error"
in
let csat_trim_lrat path =
  let skipped reason =
    Printf.printf "CSAT_TRIM skipped=%s\n%!" reason in
  match csat_lrat_read path with
  | Error reason -> skipped reason
  | Ok (parsed, before_bytes) ->
      let m = Array.length parsed in
      if m = 0 then skipped "empty_lrat" else
      let ids = Array.init m (fun i -> let (x,_,_) = parsed.(i) in x)
      and hints = Array.init m (fun i -> let (_,x,_) = parsed.(i) in x)
      and raws = Array.init m (fun i -> let (_,_,x) = parsed.(i) in x) in
      let additions = ref 0 and last = ref (-1) in
      for i = 0 to m - 1 do
        if hints.(i) <> None then (incr additions; last := i)
      done;
      if !additions = 0 then skipped "no_additions" else
      let root = !last in
      let root_lits =
        match csat_lrat_tokens raws.(root) with
        | _ :: rest ->
            let rec count = function
              | "0" :: _ -> 0
              | _ :: tl -> 1 + count tl
              | [] -> 0 in
            count rest
        | [] -> 0 in
      if root_lits <> 0 then skipped "no_empty_clause" else
      let has_negative =
        let found = ref false in
        Array.iter
          (function
            | None -> ()
            | Some hs -> Array.iter (fun v -> if v < 0 then found := true) hs)
          hints;
        !found in
      if has_negative then skipped "negative_hint" else
      let index = Hashtbl.create (2 * !additions + 1) in
      let dup = ref false in
      for i = 0 to m - 1 do
        if hints.(i) <> None then
          (if Hashtbl.mem index ids.(i) then dup := true;
           Hashtbl.replace index ids.(i) i)
      done;
      if !dup then skipped "duplicate_id" else
      let keep = Array.make m false in
      let steps_after = ref 0 in
      let stack = ref [root] in
      while !stack <> [] do
        match !stack with
        | [] -> ()
        | pos :: rest ->
            stack := rest;
            if not keep.(pos) then
              (keep.(pos) <- true;
               incr steps_after;
               match hints.(pos) with
               | None -> ()
               | Some hs ->
                   Array.iter
                     (fun h ->
                        if h > 0 then
                          try
                            let j = Hashtbl.find index h in
                            if not keep.(j) then stack := j :: !stack
                          with Not_found -> ())
                     hs)
      done;
      let buf = Buffer.create (before_bytes / 2 + 1) in
      for i = 0 to m - 1 do
        if keep.(i) then
          (Buffer.add_string buf raws.(i); Buffer.add_char buf '\n')
      done;
      let out = Buffer.contents buf in
      (try
         let tmp = path ^ ".trim" in
         let oc = open_out_bin tmp in
         output_string oc out;
         close_out oc;
         Sys.rename tmp path;
         Printf.printf
           "CSAT_TRIM before=%d after=%d steps_before=%d steps_after=%d\n%!"
           before_bytes (String.length out) !additions !steps_after
       with _ ->
         (try Sys.remove (path ^ ".trim") with _ -> ());
         skipped "write_error")
in
(* END CSAT_TRIM_STANDALONE *)

(* Disabled only by a controlled comparison run (T4), never by the emitter. *)
let csat_trim_enabled = ref true
in
(* --- phase markers (IX.65; measurement mode only) -------------------------
   `csat_mark label` is the identity on the goal.  A measurement answer is
   emitted with
     `csat_mark_reader := inference_count; csat_mark_enabled := true;`
   in front of the tactic; each marker then prints
     `PHASE_MARK <label> <primitive inferences at this point>`
   A normal answer never enables them, so nothing is printed and no inference
   is added anywhere.  `csat_mark_reader` defaults to a function that raises,
   so enabling a marker without a reader fails loudly instead of reporting a
   fabricated count.

   `CSAT_REFUTE_GEN` also brackets `LRAT_REFUTE_GEN` with two markers when
   measurement mode is on, so the bridge block can be split into the certified
   replay and the bridge's own rewriting.  The bracket is inert in every normal
   answer.  This block adds phrases to every inlined answer, exactly as the
   IX.63 trimmer did; see that receipt for why byte identity with the Python-era
   answers is already retired. *)

let csat_mark_enabled = ref false
in
let csat_mark_reader : (unit -> int) ref =
  ref (fun () -> failwith "csat_mark: no inference reader set")
in
let csat_mark (label : string) : tactic =
  fun g ->
    if !csat_mark_enabled then
      Printf.printf "PHASE_MARK %s %d\n%!" label (!csat_mark_reader ());
    ALL_TAC g
in
(* --- native-LRAT refuter ------------------------------------------------- *)

let CSAT_REFUTE_GEN amap tm =
  let cnfname = Filename.temp_file "csathol" ".cnf"
  and lratname = Filename.temp_file "csathol" ".lrat"
  and logname = Filename.temp_file "csathol" ".log" in
  let _ = dimacs_of_hol cnfname tm in
  let command =
    "(cadical --no-binary --lrat "^cnfname^" "^lratname^") >"^logname in
  let rc = Sys.command command in
  if rc <> 20 then
    (ignore (Sys.command ("rm -f "^cnfname^" "^lratname^" "^logname));
     failwith ("CSAT: cadical did not report UNSAT, exit "^string_of_int rc));
  let _ = if !csat_trim_enabled then csat_trim_lrat lratname in
  let _ = if !csat_mark_enabled then
            Printf.printf "PHASE_MARK bridge:pre-replay %d\n%!"
              (!csat_mark_reader ()) in
  let res = LRAT_REFUTE_GEN amap cnfname lratname in
  let _ = if !csat_mark_enabled then
            Printf.printf "PHASE_MARK bridge:post-replay %d\n%!"
              (!csat_mark_reader ()) in
  let _ = if !csat_debug then ()
          else ignore (Sys.command
                 ("rm -f "^cnfname^" "^lratname^" "^logname)) in
  res
in
let CSAT_REFUTE =
  let false_tm = `F` in
  fun tm ->
    let aar = Array.of_list (false_tm::atoms tm) in
    let th = CSAT_REFUTE_GEN (Array.get aar) tm in
    if hyp th = [tm] && concl th = false_tm then th
    else failwith "CSAT_REFUTE: Sanity check failure"
in
(* --- definitional-CNF prover (mirrors CADICAL_PROVE) --------------------- *)

let CSAT_PROVE =
  let false_tm = `F`
  and p_tm = `p:bool` and q_tm = `q:bool`
  and pth_triv = TAUT `(~p <=> F) <=> p`
  and pth_main = UNDISCH_ALL(TAUT `(~p <=> q) ==> (q ==> F) ==> p`) in
  let presimp_conv = GEN_REWRITE_CONV DEPTH_CONV
    [NOT_CLAUSES; AND_CLAUSES; OR_CLAUSES; IMP_CLAUSES; EQ_CLAUSES]
  and triv_rule p th = EQ_MP(INST [p,p_tm] pth_triv) th
  and main_rule p q sth th =
    itlist PROVE_HYP [sth; DISCH_ALL th] (INST [p,p_tm; q,q_tm] pth_main) in
  fun tm ->
    if is_neg tm && is_strictcnf (rand tm) then
      NOT_INTRO(DISCH_ALL(CSAT_REFUTE(rand tm)))
    else if is_imp tm && rand tm = false_tm && is_strictcnf (lhand tm) then
      DISCH_ALL(CSAT_REFUTE(lhand tm))
    else
      let sth = presimp_conv(mk_neg tm) in
      let stm = rand(concl sth) in
      if stm = false_tm then triv_rule tm sth else
      let th = ASSUME stm in
      let ths = if !exploit_conjunctive_structure then GCONJUNCTS th
                else [th] in
      let n,tops,defs,lfn =
        itlist definitionalize ths (-1,[],undefined,undefined) in
      let defg = foldl (fun a t nv -> (t,nv)::a) [] defs in
      let mdefs = filter (fun (r,_) -> not (is_atom r)) defg in
      let eqs = map (fun (r,l) -> mk_iff(l,r)) mdefs in
      let clausify eq cls =
        let fvs = frees eq and eth = (NNFC_CONV THENC CNF_CONV) eq in
        let tth = INST (map (fun v -> apply lfn v,v) fvs) eth in
        let xth = ADD_ASSUM stm (EQ_MP tth (REFL(apply lfn (lhand eq)))) in
        zip (conjuncts(rand(concl eth))) (CONJUNCTS xth) @ cls in
      let all_clauses = itlist clausify eqs tops in
      let ntdcnf = list_mk_conj (map fst all_clauses) in
      let expat = map (apply lfn) (atoms ntdcnf) in
      let rar = Array.of_list(false_tm::expat) in
      let cth = CSAT_REFUTE_GEN (Array.get rar) ntdcnf in
      let dth = PROVE_HYP (end_itlist CONJ (map snd all_clauses)) cth in
      let fth = main_rule tm stm sth dth in
      if concl fth = tm && hyp fth = [] then fth
      else failwith "CSAT_PROVE: Sanity check"
in
let CSAT_TAC = BITBLAST_THEN (CONV_TAC o K CSAT_PROVE)
in
(* --- attempt a goal and report ------------------------------------------- *)

(* A goal (asl,w) becomes the theorem |- asl ==> w, closed with the
   certified-SAT tactic.  Returns (closed, seconds, message, theorem-term). *)
let csat_list_mk_imp (l,t) = itlist (fun a b -> mk_imp(a,b)) l t
in
let csat_attempt_goal (asl,w) =
  let tm = if asl = [] then w else
    csat_list_mk_imp (map (fun (_,th) -> concl th) asl, w) in
  let t0 = csat_now () in
  let closed,msg =
    try
      let th = prove(tm, REPEAT STRIP_TAC THEN CSAT_TAC) in
      (hyp th = [] && concl th = tm, "")
    with Failure s -> (false, s)
       | _ -> (false, "unknown exception") in
  (closed, csat_now () -. t0, msg, tm)
in
let report_attempt tag (closed,dt,msg,_) =
  if closed then
    Printf.printf "CSAT_RESULT %s closed=1 seconds=%.3f\n" tag dt
  else
    let s = String.concat " " (String.split_on_char '\n' msg) in
    Printf.printf "CSAT_RESULT %s closed=0 seconds=%.3f reason=%s\n" tag dt s
in
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* bridge.ml -- generic bridge lemmas from a num/MOD (or int/rem, real/&)    *)
(* specification to a word-level circuit statement that certified SAT can    *)
(* discharge.                                                                *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Parameterisation: the modulus `p` is an argument of every lemma, the limb *)
(* width (64) enters only through the numerals that appear in the shifts,    *)
(* and the number of limbs enters only through the nesting depth of the      *)
(* joins.  There is no P-256 constant, no P-256 limb list and no transposed  *)
(* human tactic fragment in this file: the arithmetic below is the general   *)
(* statement that `(m + n) MOD p`, `(&m - &n) rem &p` and `(p - n) MOD p`    *)
(* are what the machine's written residue is, for any `p`.                   *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Provenance of the mathematics used:                                       *)
(*   MOD_ADD_CASES / MOD_LT / MOD_REFL / EXP_ADD / LT_MULT_LCANCEL  (arith)  *)
(*   INT_REM_UNIQ / INT_OF_NUM_* / INT_POW_ADD / INT_*_DISTRIB      (int)    *)
(*   VAL_WORD_JOIN_SIMPLE / VAL_WORD_0 / VAL_BOUND / VAL_WORD_BITVAL (words) *)
(*   MOD_UNIQ / SUB_ADD / VAL_WORD_ADD / VAL_WORD_SUB               (arith)  *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The reference route: `ref_add' is the modular specification in one word    *)
(* operation, and ADD_REF_VAL is the only lemma that carries MOD.  SAT       *)
(* instances built on it are pure word statements.                          *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Conversion note: INT_SHIFT_TO_JOIN_CONV accepts a *numeral* operand, not   *)
(* only `&(val x)' and `&(bitval b)'.  The case split substitutes a carry    *)
(* by the literal 0 or 1, so `&2 pow 64 * &0' must still become a join; if   *)
(* it does not, the accumulator equation is left as an opaque int atom and   *)
(* the flag it constrains is free.                                          *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Kernel trust: every SAT refutation is replayed by the LCF kernel inside   *)
(* CSAT_REFUTE (csat_lib.ml); no solver certificate is trusted and no         *)
(* compiler enters the trusted base.                                         *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* DEVELOPMENT_ONLY (not lemmas; recorded so they cannot hide):             *)
(*   BRIDGE_ADD_TAC / BRIDGE_SUB_TAC / BRIDGE_NEG_TAC are *shape dispatch*.  *)
(*   They inspect the postcondition shape (sum MOD p, difference rem p,      *)
(*   complement MOD p), split at the single conditional that shape admits,   *)
(*   and call the generic lemmas above.  The old human tail (DECARRY_RULE,   *)
(*   DESUM_RULE, BOUNDER_TAC, EQUAL_FROM_CONGRUENT_MOD_MOD,                 *)
(*   REAL_INTEGER_TAC) is not used anywhere in this file.                    *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 1. The modular specification, split at its single conditional correction. *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Each lemma states the spec side in terms of the value the machine writes, *)
(* so the machine-side obligation that reaches SAT is a pure *sum* identity: *)
(* no MOD, no rem, no subtraction.                                           *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* add: (m + n) MOD p, at most one correction because m < p and n < p. *)
let ADD_MOD_LT = prove
 (`!p m n. m < p /\ n < p /\ m + n < p ==> (m + n) MOD p = m + n`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(m + n) MOD p = (if m + n < p then m + n else (m + n) - p)`
    (fun th -> REWRITE_TAC[th]) THENL
   [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_ADD_CASES THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]])
in
let ADD_MOD_GE = prove
 (`!p m n. m < p /\ n < p /\ p <= m + n ==> (m + n) MOD p = (m + n) - p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(m + n) MOD p = (if m + n < p then m + n else (m + n) - p)`
    (fun th -> REWRITE_TAC[th]) THENL
   [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_ADD_CASES THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    SUBGOAL_THEN `~(m + n < p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
    ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]])
in
(* `t = (m + n) - p' in sum form, so that the residue has no subtraction *)
let ADD_GE_SUM = prove
 (`!p m n t. p <= m + n ==> ((t = (m + n) - p) <=> (t + p = m + n))`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN DISCH_TAC THEN
  MP_TAC(ISPECL [`m + n:num`; `p:num`] SUB_ADD) THEN
  ANTS_TAC THENL [ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; DISCH_TAC] THEN
  EQ_TAC THENL
   [DISCH_THEN SUBST1_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    DISCH_TAC THEN UNDISCH_TAC `((m + n) - p) + p = m + n` THEN
    ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
(* the same bridge, stated once in the shape a caller applies *)
let ADD_MOD_SPLIT = prove
 (`!p m n s t.
       0 < p /\ m < p /\ n < p /\
       (m + n < p ==> s = m + n) /\
       (p <= m + n ==> t + p = m + n)
       ==> (m + n) MOD p = (if m + n < p then s else t)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `m + n < p` THENL
   [ASM_SIMP_TAC[ADD_MOD_LT] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC;
    SUBGOAL_THEN `p <= m + n` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
    ASM_SIMP_TAC[ADD_MOD_GE] THEN CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN
    ASM_SIMP_TAC[ADD_GE_SUM] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
(* sub: (&m - &n) rem &p, split at the borrow. *)
let SUB_REM_LT = prove
 (`!p m n. 0 < p /\ m < p /\ n < p /\ m < n
           ==> ((&m:int) - &n) rem (&p) = &((m + p) - n)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `n <= m + p` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `&((m + p) - n):int = (&m + &p) - &n` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [ASM_SIMP_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_SUB; INT_OF_NUM_ADD]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  MATCH_MP_TAC INT_REM_UNIQ THEN EXISTS_TAC `--(&1):int` THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[INT_ABS_NUM] THEN REPEAT CONJ_TAC THENL
   [UNDISCH_TAC `&((m + p) - n):int = (&m + &p) - &n` THEN CONV_TAC INT_ARITH;
    REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LE] THEN ARITH_TAC;
    REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LT] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let SUB_REM_GE = prove
 (`!p m n. 0 < p /\ m < p /\ n < p /\ ~(m < n)
           ==> ((&m:int) - &n) rem (&p) = &(m - n)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `n <= m` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `&(m - n):int = &m - &n` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [ASM_SIMP_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_SUB]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  MATCH_MP_TAC INT_REM_UNIQ THEN EXISTS_TAC `(&0):int` THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[INT_ABS_NUM] THEN REPEAT CONJ_TAC THENL
   [UNDISCH_TAC `&(m - n):int = &m - &n` THEN CONV_TAC INT_ARITH;
    REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LE] THEN ARITH_TAC;
    REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LT] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let SUB_LT_SUM = prove
 (`!p m n t. n < p /\ m < n ==> ((t = (m + p) - n) <=> (t + n = m + p))`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `n <= m + p` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  MP_TAC(ISPECL [`m + p:num`; `n:num`] SUB_ADD) THEN
  ANTS_TAC THENL [ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; DISCH_TAC] THEN
  EQ_TAC THENL
   [DISCH_THEN SUBST1_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    DISCH_TAC THEN UNDISCH_TAC `((m + p) - n) + n = m + p` THEN
    ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let SUB_GE_SUM = prove
 (`!m n t. ~(m < n) ==> ((t = m - n) <=> (t + n = m))`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN DISCH_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `n <= m` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  MP_TAC(ISPECL [`m:num`; `n:num`] SUB_ADD) THEN
  ANTS_TAC THENL [ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; DISCH_TAC] THEN
  EQ_TAC THENL
   [DISCH_THEN SUBST1_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    DISCH_TAC THEN UNDISCH_TAC `(m - n) + n = m` THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let SUB_REM_SPLIT = prove
 (`!p m n s.
       0 < p /\ m < p /\ n < p /\
       (m < n ==> s + n = m + p) /\
       (~(m < n) ==> s + n = m)
       ==> ((&m:int) - &n) rem (&p) = &s`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `m < n` THENL
   [ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_REM_LT] THEN REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_EQ] THEN
    CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_LT_SUM];
    ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_REM_GE] THEN REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_EQ] THEN
    CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_GE_SUM]])
in
(* neg: (p - n) MOD p, split at n = 0. *)
let NEG_MOD_ZERO = prove
 (`!p n. 0 < p /\ n = 0 ==> (p - n) MOD p = 0`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[SUB_0; MOD_REFL])
in
let NEG_MOD_NZ = prove
 (`!p n. 0 < p /\ n <= p /\ ~(n = 0) ==> (p - n) MOD p = (p - n)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC)
in
let NEG_NZ_SUM = prove
 (`!p n t. n <= p ==> ((t = p - n) <=> (t + n = p))`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN DISCH_TAC THEN
  MP_TAC(ISPECL [`p:num`; `n:num`] SUB_ADD) THEN
  ANTS_TAC THENL [ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; DISCH_TAC] THEN
  EQ_TAC THENL
   [DISCH_THEN SUBST1_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    DISCH_TAC THEN UNDISCH_TAC `(p - n) + n = p` THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let NEG_MOD_SPLIT = prove
 (`!p n s.
       0 < p /\ n <= p /\
       (n = 0 ==> s = 0) /\
       (~(n = 0) ==> s + n = p)
       ==> (p - n) MOD p = s`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `n = 0` THENL
   [ASM_SIMP_TAC[NEG_MOD_ZERO] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC;
    ASM_SIMP_TAC[NEG_MOD_NZ] THEN CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN
    ASM_SIMP_TAC[NEG_NZ_SUM] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let BRIDGE_SPEC_LEMMAS =
  [ADD_MOD_LT; ADD_MOD_GE; ADD_GE_SUM; ADD_MOD_SPLIT;
   SUB_REM_LT; SUB_REM_GE; SUB_LT_SUM; SUB_GE_SUM; SUB_REM_SPLIT;
   NEG_MOD_ZERO; NEG_MOD_NZ; NEG_NZ_SUM; NEG_MOD_SPLIT]
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 1b. The reference function.                                               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* `ref_add pw x y' is the whole modular specification of addition in one     *)
(* word operation: add, and subtract pw once if the sum overflowed or        *)
(* reached pw.  There is no curve constant here and no MOD: the single       *)
(* generic lemma ADD_REF_VAL carries the MOD, so every per-curve SAT         *)
(* instance is a pure word statement (`output = ref_add (word p) x y`) with  *)
(* `x < p' and `y < p' as bit-level hypotheses.                              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let ref_add = new_definition
 `ref_add (pw:W word) (x:W word) (y:W word) =
    let s = word_add x y in
    if word_ult s x \/ word_ule pw s then word_sub s pw else s`
in
let MOD_SUB_ONE = prove
 (`!s q:num. q <= s /\ s < 2 * q ==> s MOD q = (s - q)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_UNIQ THEN EXISTS_TAC `1` THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[MULT_CLAUSES] THEN CONJ_TAC THENL
   [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let SUB_MOD = prove
 (`!s q m:num. q <= s /\ s < m ==> ((s + (m - q)) MOD m) = (s - q)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_UNIQ THEN EXISTS_TAC `1` THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[MULT_CLAUSES] THEN CONJ_TAC THENL
   [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
(* Case: the sum overflowed or reached pw, so the machine subtracts. *)
let MOD_SUB_REF_A1 = prove
 (`!p a b m:num.
      0 < p /\ p < m /\ a < p /\ b < p /\ ((a + b) MOD m) < a
      ==> ((((a + b) MOD m) + (m - p)) MOD m) = (a + b) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) < (2 * p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `(a + b) < m` THENL
   [ SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD m = (a + b)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) < a` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MP_TAC (ASSUME `((a + b) MOD m) < a`) THEN
       ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_ARITH_TAC;
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD m = ((a + b) - m)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_ONE THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `((((a + b) - m) + (m - p)) = ((a + b) - p))`
       ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(((a + b) - p) MOD m) = ((a + b) - p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD p = ((a + b) - p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_ONE THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] ])
in
let MOD_SUB_REF_A2 = prove
 (`!p a b m:num.
      0 < p /\ p < m /\ a < p /\ b < p /\ p <= ((a + b) MOD m)
      ==> ((((a + b) MOD m) + (m - p)) MOD m) = (a + b) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) < (2 * p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `(a + b) < m` THENL
   [ SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD m = (a + b)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `p <= (a + b)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MP_TAC (ASSUME `p <= ((a + b) MOD m)`) THEN
       ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(((a + b) + (m - p)) MOD m) = ((a + b) - p)`
       ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC SUB_MOD THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD p = ((a + b) - p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_ONE THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD m = ((a + b) - m)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_ONE THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `((((a + b) - m) + (m - p)) = ((a + b) - p))`
       ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(((a + b) - p) MOD m) = ((a + b) - p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD p = ((a + b) - p)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_ONE THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] ])
in
(* Case: neither, so the machine keeps the sum. *)
let MOD_KEEP_REF = prove
 (`!p a b m:num.
      0 < p /\ p < m /\ a < p /\ b < p /\
      ~(((a + b) MOD m) < a) /\ ~(p <= ((a + b) MOD m))
      ==> (a + b) MOD m = (a + b) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `(a + b) < m` THENL
   [ SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD m = (a + b)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) < p` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MP_TAC (ASSUME `~(p <= ((a + b) MOD m))`) THEN
       ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD p = (a + b)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
     SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + b) MOD m = ((a + b) - m)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_ONE THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `((a + b) MOD m) < a` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     UNDISCH_TAC `~(((a + b) MOD m) < a)` THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] ])
in
(* The one lemma that carries MOD; proved for every width and every pw. *)
let ADD_REF_VAL = prove
 (`!(pw:W word) (x:W word) (y:W word).
       0 < val pw /\ val x < val pw /\ val y < val pw
       ==> val(ref_add pw x y) = (val x + val y) MOD val pw`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `0 < 2 EXP dimindex(:W)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [REWRITE_TAC[EXP_LT_0; ARITH]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN
   `val(pw:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\
    val(x:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\
    val(y:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W)`
    STRIP_ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [REWRITE_TAC[VAL_BOUND]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[ref_add; LET_DEF; LET_END_DEF] THEN BETA_TAC THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[WORD_ULT; WORD_ULE; VAL_WORD_ADD] THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC
   `((val(x:W word) + val(y:W word)) MOD (2 EXP dimindex(:W))) < val(x:W word)`
   THENL
   [ ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN
     REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD_SUB; VAL_WORD_ADD] THEN
     MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_REF_A1 THEN REPEAT CONJ_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
     ASM_CASES_TAC
      `val(pw:W word) <=
       ((val(x:W word) + val(y:W word)) MOD (2 EXP dimindex(:W)))`
      THENL
      [ ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN
        REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD_SUB; VAL_WORD_ADD] THEN
        MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_SUB_REF_A2 THEN REPEAT CONJ_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
        ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN
        REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD_ADD] THEN
        MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_KEEP_REF THEN REPEAT CONJ_TAC THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] ] ])
in
(* the same statement for a modulus supplied as a numeral *)
let ADD_REF_VAL_WORD = prove
 (`!p (x:W word) (y:W word).
       0 < p /\ p < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\ val x < p /\ val y < p
       ==> val(ref_add (word p : W word) x y) = (val x + val y) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `val(word p : W word) = p` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD] THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    ALL_TAC] THEN
  (* instantiate ADD_REF_VAL at pw = word p, then rewrite val(word p) = p in
     the theorem so its conclusion is syntactically the goal. *)
  FIRST_ASSUM(fun th ->
    MATCH_MP_TAC (REWRITE_RULE[th]
      (SPECL [`(word p : W word)`; `(x:W word)`; `(y:W word)`] ADD_REF_VAL))) THEN
  ASM_REWRITE_TAC[])
in
let BRIDGE_REF_LEMMAS = [ADD_REF_VAL; ADD_REF_VAL_WORD]
in
let BRIDGE_SPEC_LEMMAS = BRIDGE_SPEC_LEMMAS @ BRIDGE_REF_LEMMAS
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 2. Power-of-two scaling as a word join.                                   *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* `word_join' is free under bit-blasting (BIT_WORD_JOIN); a product by a    *)
(* power of two is instead expanded by WORDIFY_CONV into a full multiplier,  *)
(* which dominates the SAT cost.  Rewriting the shifts to joins is what      *)
(* makes the residue cheap, and it is also what removes the unconstrained-   *)
(* width problem: `word_join' has a free result type, so the width must be   *)
(* supplied here (`mk_word_ty').                                            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let EXP2_NZ = prove
 (`!j:num. ~(2 EXP j = 0)`,
  GEN_TAC THEN REWRITE_TAC[EXP_EQ_0] THEN ARITH_TAC)
in
let LT_EXP_MULT = prove
 (`!x j k:num. x < 2 EXP k ==> 2 EXP j * x < 2 EXP (j + k)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN DISCH_TAC THEN REWRITE_TAC[EXP_ADD] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[LT_MULT_LCANCEL] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[EXP_EQ_0; ARITH] THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[])
in
(* val(join x 0) = 2^w * val x, i.e. shifting left by a zero word. *)
let VAL_JOIN_ZERO = prove
 (`!x:M word. dimindex(:M) + dimindex(:N) = dimindex(:P)
              ==> val((word_join:M word->N word->P word) x (word 0)) =
                  2 EXP dimindex(:N) * val x`,
  REPEAT STRIP_TAC THEN
  ASM_SIMP_TAC[VAL_WORD_JOIN_SIMPLE; VAL_WORD_0; ADD_0])
in
(* the same statement one type level up, in the shape the residue has *)
let INT_JOIN_ZERO = prove
 (`!x:M word. dimindex(:M) + dimindex(:N) = dimindex(:P)
              ==> (&2:int) pow dimindex(:N) * &(val x) =
                  &(val((word_join:M word->N word->P word) x (word 0)))`,
  REPEAT STRIP_TAC THEN
  ASM_SIMP_TAC[VAL_JOIN_ZERO; GSYM INT_OF_NUM_MUL; INT_OF_NUM_POW])
in
let BITVAL_AS_VAL = prove
 (`!b. bitval b = val(word(bitval b):1 word)`,
  GEN_TAC THEN CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN
  MATCH_ACCEPT_TAC (INST_TYPE [`:1`, `:N`] VAL_WORD_BITVAL))
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 3. Conversions.                                                           *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* real equation over integer-valued atoms -> integer equation *)
let REAL_TO_INT_CONV =
  GEN_REWRITE_CONV DEPTH_CONV
   [GSYM int_of_num_th; GSYM int_neg_th; GSYM int_add_th; GSYM int_sub_th;
    GSYM int_mul_th; GSYM int_pow_th; GSYM int_eq]
in
(* num equation -> int equation, with `&' pushed inside sum/product/power.    *)
(* INT_OF_NUM_ADD/MUL/POW are stated with `&' *outside* (`&m + &n = &(m + n)`), *)
(* so they must be used in the GSYM direction here; using them forwards folds  *)
(* the whole bignum back into a single `&(...)', which the shift-to-join       *)
(* conversion cannot see (measured: every post-simulation stage stayed SAT).   *)
let NUM_TO_INT_CONV =
  GEN_REWRITE_CONV TOP_DEPTH_CONV
   [GSYM INT_OF_NUM_EQ; GSYM INT_OF_NUM_LT; GSYM INT_OF_NUM_LE;
    GSYM INT_OF_NUM_ADD; GSYM INT_OF_NUM_MUL; GSYM INT_OF_NUM_POW]
in
(* (a + b) * c = a * c + b * c, needed because bignum_of_wordlist nests     *)
(* its shifts around a sum, not around a single digit.                       *)
let INT_DISTRIB_CONV =
  GEN_REWRITE_CONV TOP_DEPTH_CONV [INT_ADD_LDISTRIB; INT_ADD_RDISTRIB]
in
(* (&2) pow k * &(val x) -> &(val(join x 0)) at the width this x forces.     *)
(* Bottom-up application gives 2^(64*(j+1)) for j nested shifts for free.     *)
let INT_JOIN_ZERO_TH x k =
  (* `dest_word_ty' is shadowed by Library/bitmatch.ml once the ARM base is
     loaded, so the width is read off the type constructor directly. *)
  let m = Num.int_of_num
    (dest_finty(match type_of x with
                | Tyapp("word",[n]) -> n
                | _ -> failwith "INT_JOIN_ZERO_TH: not a word")) in
  let inst = INST_TYPE
    [mk_finty(Num.num_of_int m), `:M`;
     mk_finty(Num.num_of_int k), `:N`;
     mk_finty(Num.num_of_int(m + k)), `:P`] INT_JOIN_ZERO in
  let th1 = SPEC x inst in
  let cond = lhand(concl th1) in
  let side =
    prove(cond,
      CONV_TAC(LAND_CONV(BINOP_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_ADD_CONV) THENC
               RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_EQ_CONV)) in
  (* reduce dimindex(:N) on the left so the rule is syntactically applicable.  *)
  (* The left side of the equation is `&2 pow dimindex(:N) * &(val x)'; the     *)
  (* exponent is the *left* operand of that product, so the path is            *)
  (* LAND (LAND (RAND DIMINDEX)).  The old single LAND reached `&(val x)' and  *)
  (* raised DIMINDEX_CONV, which DEPTH_CONV silently swallowed, leaving every  *)
  (* shift unconverted and every SAT call SATISFIABLE.                        *)
  CONV_RULE (LAND_CONV(LAND_CONV(RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV))) (MP th1 side)
in
(* smallest b with n < 2^b, at least 1; used to place a literal operand in a
   word narrow enough that `val(word n)' is exact. *)
let bits_of_num n =
  let two = Num.num_of_int 2 and one = Num.num_of_int 1 in
  let rec go b m = if Num.le_num m n then go (b + 1) (Num.mult_num two m) else b in
  let b = go 0 one in
  Num.num_of_int (if b < 1 then 1 else b)
in
let INT_SHIFT_TO_JOIN_CONV : conv =
  (* the second operand is `&(val x)', `&(bitval b)', or a *numeral*.  The
     numeral case matters: BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_TAC substitutes a carry by
     the literal 0 or 1, turning `&2 pow 64 * &(bitval c)' into
     `&2 pow 64 * &0'.  Without this case that equation could not be wordified
     at all, BITBLAST left it opaque, and the selected limb was free. *)
  let operand q =
    match q with
      Comb(Const("int_of_num",_),Comb(Const("val",_),x)) -> (x, REFL q)
    | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_),Comb(Const("bitval",_),_)) ->
        let bth = RAND_CONV (GEN_REWRITE_CONV I [BITVAL_AS_VAL]) q in
        (rand(rand(rand(concl bth))), bth)
    | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_),n) when is_numeral n ->
        let bits = bits_of_num (dest_numeral n) in
        let w = mk_comb(mk_const("word",[mk_finty bits, `:N`]), n)
        and v = mk_comb(mk_const("val",[mk_finty bits, `:N`]),
                        mk_comb(mk_const("word",[mk_finty bits, `:N`]), n)) in
        let val_th = prove(mk_eq(v,n),
          REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD] THEN
          CONV_TAC(LAND_CONV(RAND_CONV(RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV))) THEN
          MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN
          CONV_TAC(RAND_CONV NUM_EXP_CONV THENC NUM_LT_CONV)) in
        (w, AP_TERM `int_of_num:num->int` (SYM val_th))
    | _ -> failwith "INT_SHIFT_TO_JOIN_CONV: operand" in
  let pow2 tm =
    match tm with
      Comb(Comb(Const("int_pow",_),two),n)
        when aconv two `(&2):int` && is_numeral n -> dest_small_numeral n
    | _ -> failwith "INT_SHIFT_TO_JOIN_CONV: multiplier" in
  let mul_left p th =
    AP_TERM (mk_comb(`int_mul:int->int->int`, p)) th in
  let conv tm =
    match tm with
      Comb(Comb(Const("int_mul",_),p),q) when type_of tm = `:int` ->
        (match p with
           Comb(Comb(Const("int_pow",_),_),_) ->
             let k = pow2 p in
             let (x,bth) = operand q in
             TRANS (mul_left p bth) (INT_JOIN_ZERO_TH x k)
         | Comb(Const("int_neg",_),pt) ->
             (* accumulator equations carry the shifted flag negatively       *)
             let k = pow2 pt in
             let (x,bth) = operand q in
             let q' = rand(concl bth) in
             let bth2 = mul_left p bth in
             let negth = AP_TERM `(int_neg):int->int` (INT_JOIN_ZERO_TH x k) in
             TRANS bth2 (TRANS (SPECL [pt; q'] INT_MUL_LNEG) negth)
         | _ -> failwith "INT_SHIFT_TO_JOIN_CONV: multiplier") 
    | _ -> failwith "INT_SHIFT_TO_JOIN_CONV" in
  conv
in
let BRIDGE_SHIFTS_TO_JOINS_CONV = DEPTH_CONV INT_SHIFT_TO_JOIN_CONV
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 2b. A bignum digit sum as one word.                                       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* `bignum_of_wordlist' and BIGNUM_DIGITIZE both hand back a flat sum        *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   val w0 + 2^k * val w1 + 2^(2k) * val w2 + ... + 2^(k*(n-1)) * val w{n-1} *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* over words w0..w{n-1} of one limb width k.  The reference lemmas are      *)
(* stated about ONE word, so the sum has to become a word.  Folding the      *)
(* digits from the most significant end through `word_join' does that:       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   val(w1)                  = val w1                                        *)
(*   val(join(acc) w0)        = 2^k * val acc + val w0                       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* by VAL_WORD_JOIN_SIMPLE, whose only side condition is the dimindex one.   *)
(* The limb width k is read off the words and the limb count from the sum,   *)
(* so nothing here assumes 64 bits or four limbs.                            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_word_width ty =
  match ty with
  | Tyapp("word",[n]) -> Num.int_of_num (dest_finty n)
  | _ -> failwith "bridge_word_width: not a word type"
in
let bridge_finty k = mk_finty (Num.num_of_int k)
in
(* word_join with the result width made explicit: it is a type argument, not  *)
(* something HOL infers, so it must be supplied (the same reason             *)
(* INT_JOIN_ZERO_TH supplies `:P').                                          *)
let BRIDGE_WJOIN (x:term) (y:term) =
  let mx = bridge_word_width (type_of x)
  and my = bridge_word_width (type_of y) in
  mk_comb(mk_comb(mk_const("word_join",
      [bridge_finty mx, `:M`; bridge_finty my, `:N`;
       bridge_finty (mx + my), `:P`]), x), y)
in
(* |- val(join x y) = 2 EXP k * val x + val y, with k = width of y reduced  *)
let BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_STEP (x:term) (y:term) =
  let mx = bridge_word_width (type_of x)
  and my = bridge_word_width (type_of y) in
  let inst = INST_TYPE [bridge_finty mx, `:M`; bridge_finty my, `:N`;
                        bridge_finty (mx + my), `:P`] VAL_WORD_JOIN_SIMPLE in
  let th = SPECL [x; y] inst in
  let side = prove(lhand (concl th),
      CONV_TAC(LAND_CONV(BINOP_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_ADD_CONV) THENC
               RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_EQ_CONV)) in
  CONV_RULE (RAND_CONV(LAND_CONV(LAND_CONV(RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV))))
            (MP th side)
in
(* the little-endian word list of a flat digit sum, in either associativity  *)
let BRIDGE_DIGIT_TERMS tm =
  let rec addends t =
    match t with
    | Comb(Comb(Const("+",_),_),_) -> addends (lhand t) @ addends (rand t)
    | _ -> [t] in
  let dest_val t =
    match t with
    | Comb(Const("val",_),w) -> w
    | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_DIGIT_TERMS: not `val w'" in
  let dest_pow t =
    match t with
    | Comb(Comb(Const("EXP",_),two),n) when aconv two `2` ->
        (ignore (dest_small_numeral n); ())
    | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_DIGIT_TERMS: not `2 EXP k'" in
  match addends tm with
  | [] -> failwith "BRIDGE_DIGIT_TERMS: empty"
  | first :: rest ->
      let w0 = dest_val first in
      let ws = map (fun t ->
          match t with
          | Comb(Comb(Const("*",_),p),v) -> (dest_pow p; dest_val v)
          | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_DIGIT_TERMS: not `2^k * val w'") rest in
      w0 :: ws
in
let bridge_join_of_words ws =
  match List.rev ws with
  | [] -> failwith "bridge_join_of_words: empty"
  | last :: rest ->
      List.fold_left (fun acc w -> BRIDGE_WJOIN acc w) last rest
in
(* |- val(join of ws) = flat                                                      *)
let BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_FOLD (ws:term list) (flat:term) =
  let j = bridge_join_of_words ws in
  let rec steps = function
    | [] | [_] -> []
    | w :: (_ :: _ as rest) ->
        BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_STEP (bridge_join_of_words rest) w :: steps rest in
  let sts = steps ws in
  prove(mk_eq(mk_comb(mk_const("val",
      [bridge_finty (bridge_word_width (type_of j)), `:N`]), j), flat),
    REWRITE_TAC sts THEN CONV_TAC NUM_REDUCE_CONV THEN ARITH_TAC)
in
(* (the word, |- val word = flat sum)                                            *)
let BRIDGE_WORD_OF_DIGITS tm =
  let ws = BRIDGE_DIGIT_TERMS tm in
  (bridge_join_of_words ws, BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_FOLD ws tm)
in
(* whole-term conversion from any of the three spec types to a word residue *)
let BRIDGE_TO_WORD_CONV =
  REAL_TO_INT_CONV THENC NUM_TO_INT_CONV THENC INT_DISTRIB_CONV THENC
  BRIDGE_SHIFTS_TO_JOINS_CONV
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 4. Case splitting on the conditionals the simulator leaves behind.        *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The conditions may sit in the goal (the selected limb of the written      *)
(* value) or in an accumulator equation (a selected mask word).  Both are    *)
(* reduced by the same recursive split, and the condition itself stays as a *)
(* bit-blastable hypothesis, so SAT can see that the branch is consistent.   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_conditions tm =
  map (fun t -> rand(rator(rator t))) (find_terms is_cond tm)
in
let rec BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_TAC (asl,w) =
  let conds = bridge_conditions w @
              List.concat (map (fun (_,th) -> bridge_conditions(concl th)) asl) in
  match conds with
  | [] -> ALL_TAC (asl,w)
  | c::_ ->
      let truerule = ASSUME c
      and falserule = EQF_INTRO (ASSUME (mk_neg c)) in
      let close rule =
        RULE_ASSUM_TAC(REWRITE_RULE[rule; COND_CLAUSES; BITVAL_CLAUSES]) THEN
        CONV_TAC(REWRITE_CONV[rule; COND_CLAUSES; BITVAL_CLAUSES]) THEN
        BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_TAC in
      (ASM_CASES_TAC c THENL [close truerule; close falserule]) (asl,w)
in
(* The same split, but the branch condition is *retained* as a hypothesis.
   REWRITE_RULE reads a non-equational theorem `|- c' as the rule `c -> T', so
   the version above rewrites the case hypothesis itself to `true' and the
   branch information is lost from the assumptions (it survives only where a
   lemma restates it arithmetically, as ADD_MOD_LT / SUB_LT_SUM do).  A route
   that carries the condition in the word goal -- the reference route's
   `ref_add' conditional -- needs the fact itself in the SAT instance. *)
let rec BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_KEEP_TAC (asl,w) =
  let conds = bridge_conditions w @
              List.concat (map (fun (_,th) -> bridge_conditions(concl th)) asl) in
  match conds with
  | [] -> ALL_TAC (asl,w)
  | c::_ ->
      let close rule fact =
        RULE_ASSUM_TAC(REWRITE_RULE[rule; COND_CLAUSES; BITVAL_CLAUSES]) THEN
        CONV_TAC(REWRITE_CONV[rule; COND_CLAUSES; BITVAL_CLAUSES]) THEN
        ASSUME_TAC fact THEN
        BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_KEEP_TAC in
      (ASM_CASES_TAC c THENL
        [close (ASSUME c) (ASSUME c);
         close (EQF_INTRO (ASSUME (mk_neg c))) (ASSUME (mk_neg c))])
      (asl,w)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 5. Eliminate the specification variables from their digit expansions.     *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let BRIDGE_HAS_VAL tm =
  mem "val" (map (fst o dest_const)
    (find_terms (fun t -> can (fst o dest_const) t) tm))
in
let rec ELIM_DIGIT_EQS_TAC (asl,w) =
  let pick = ref None in
  do_list (fun (_,th) ->
    let tm = concl th in
    if is_eq tm && type_of (lhand tm) = `:num` && not (is_var tm) then
      let (l,r) = dest_eq tm in
      if is_var l && free_in l w && not (free_in l r) then pick := Some th
      else if is_var r && free_in r w && not (free_in r l) then
        pick := Some (SYM th)) asl;
  match !pick with
  | None -> ALL_TAC (asl,w)
  | Some th -> (SUBST_ALL_TAC th THEN ELIM_DIGIT_EQS_TAC) (asl,w)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6. Certified-SAT close of the word residue.                               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* BITBLAST_THEN consumes only word-level content; any atom it cannot expand *)
(* becomes a free proposition and the residue comes back SAT, so everything  *)
(* that is not word-level must be gone before the call.  The residue is      *)
(* presented as one closed implication so that no hypothesis is lost.        *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6a. Hypothesis-cone slicing before the blast (XV.B).                      *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The certified close pays ~28 primitive inferences per bit-blasted         *)
(* subterm, and the blasted term is built from the *hypotheses*, not from    *)
(* the goal (IX.66: the word goal has 51 subterms at the bridge entry, the   *)
(* bit-blasted term ~1.99M).  So the cost is governed by the hypothesis set. *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Slicing keeps the connected component of the goal under "shares a free    *)
(* variable with", transitively, seeded by the goal's free variables.  A     *)
(* hypothesis outside that component shares no variable, transitively, with  *)
(* the conclusion; proving `(conj S) ==> w` for S subset of the hypotheses   *)
(* and applying MP only to S still yields `|- w` with the same conclusion.   *)
(* A smaller hypothesis set makes the obligation *stronger*, never weaker,   *)
(* so dropping hypotheses cannot produce a false theorem -- it can only fail  *)
(* to close.  That is why the fallback below is mandatory for a              *)
(* *mathematical* failure and why an incompleteness result is a legitimate    *)
(* outcome, not a bug.  XVI.D classifies the failure first: a resource-      *)
(* exhausted attempt (out of memory, stack overflow, timeout, signal) is      *)
(* reported and re-raised, never retried against the larger full set.        *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The criterion is syntactic (free-variable sharing), not semantic.  It is  *)
(* sound and deterministic; it is not complete, and it may keep hypotheses   *)
(* that are mathematically irrelevant.  It never drops one it cannot         *)
(* justify structurally, which is why a failure is a fallback.               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* `TEKMERION_SLICE_CONTROL' exists only for the S3/XV.B3 refutation and for   *)
(* the class diagnostics: `keep-none' removes every hypothesis, `drop-largest' *)
(* removes the largest kept one, `drop-non-eq' keeps only equations, `drop-one' *)
(* removes the last kept one, and `only-true'/`drop-true'/`drop-nonoverlap'    *)
(* isolate one syntactic class on the full set.  Every one of them makes the  *)
(* obligation stronger and can only turn a success into a fallback; none can  *)
(* weaken what is proved.  Unset, the criterion is the one above.             *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let rec bridge_term_size tm =
  (match tm with
   | Comb(s,t) -> 1 + bridge_term_size s + bridge_term_size t
   | Abs(_,b) -> 1 + bridge_term_size b
   | _ -> 1)
in
let bridge_slice_control =
  try Sys.getenv "TEKMERION_SLICE_CONTROL" with Not_found -> ""
in
let bridge_slice_debug =
  try Sys.getenv "TEKMERION_SLICE_DEBUG" = "1" with Not_found -> false
in
(* `--mode phase' sets this, so a SLICE line names its task.  It is inert and  *)
(* unread in a normal answer, which prints no measurement lines at all.       *)
let bridge_slice_task = ref "unknown"
in
let bridge_slice_note fmt =
  Printf.ksprintf
    (fun s ->
       if !csat_mark_enabled then (print_string s; print_newline (); flush stdout))
    fmt
in
(* The connected component of the goal under "shares a free variable with",
   transitively, in the original order of `asl'.  Terms are compared
   structurally; `frees' returns the free `Var' nodes of a conclusion. *)
let bridge_slice_hyps hths w =
  let hs = Array.of_list hths in
  let n = Array.length hs in
  let fv = Array.map (fun th -> frees (concl th)) hs in
  let reach = ref (frees w) in
  let in_reach v = List.exists (fun x -> x = v) !reach in
  let kept = Array.make n false in
  let changed = ref true in
  while !changed do
    changed := false;
    for i = 0 to n - 1 do
      if not kept.(i) && List.exists in_reach fv.(i) then begin
        kept.(i) <- true;
        List.iter (fun v -> if not (in_reach v) then reach := v :: !reach) fv.(i);
        changed := true
      end
    done
  done;
  let out = ref [] in
  Array.iteri (fun i th -> if kept.(i) then out := th :: !out) hs;
  List.rev !out
in
(* The S3 control: one deliberate over-slice.  A no-op unless the environment
   asked for it.  `only-true', `drop-true', `drop-nonoverlap' and
   `drop-largest' are diagnostics: they apply to the full set (or, for
   `drop-largest', to one kept hypothesis), so the effect of one syntactic class
   can be isolated.  `full' disables the slice entirely; it exists only to
   re-measure the pre-slice (IX.63) baseline, which is the full obligation the
   SAT close had before IX.69, not a weakened one. *)
let bridge_has_nonoverlap th =
  List.exists
    (fun t -> try fst (dest_const t) = "nonoverlapping_modulo" with _ -> false)
    (find_terms (fun _ -> true) (concl th))
in
let bridge_slice_forced hths kept =
  match bridge_slice_control with
  | "full" -> hths
  | "keep-none" -> []
  | "drop-one" ->
      (match List.rev kept with [] -> [] | _ :: rest -> List.rev rest)
  | "drop-non-eq" -> List.filter (fun th -> is_eq (concl th)) kept
  | "drop-largest" ->
      (match kept with
       | [] -> []
       | h :: tl ->
           let sz th = bridge_term_size (concl th) in
           let big = List.fold_left (fun a b -> if sz b > sz a then b else a) h tl in
           List.filter (fun th -> not (th == big)) kept)
  | "only-true" -> List.filter (fun th -> concl th = `T`) hths
  | "drop-true" -> List.filter (fun th -> not (concl th = `T`)) hths
  | "drop-nonoverlap" -> List.filter (fun th -> not (bridge_has_nonoverlap th)) hths
  | _ -> kept
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6a'. Failure taxonomy for the sliced attempt (XVI.D).                     *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* A failed slice has one of five outcomes.  Only one of them may retry the   *)
(* full hypothesis set:                                                       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   closed        the attempt returned a theorem; nothing to report.         *)
(*   mathematical  the slice was too small, and the failure carries a shape *)
(*                 on the explicit allow-list below (a SAT report or the     *)
(*                 named slice-too-strong marker); retry the full set.       *)
(*   unsupported   the input is outside the close's shape; report and stop.  *)
(*   resource      out of memory, stack overflow, timeout, or a signal       *)
(*                 death (exit >= 128, or 124 from a timeout wrapper);       *)
(*                 report and stop.  Retrying at a larger budget is a       *)
(*                 decision recorded elsewhere, never an automatic retry.     *)
(*   internal      a kernel/procedure sanity failure, a Failure whose text    *)
(*                 is not on the allow-list (a broken rewrite, a missing     *)
(*                 lemma, a violated invariant all look like this), or an    *)
(*                 unknown exception; report and re-raise.                    *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* A generic `Failure' is *not* evidence of a mathematical failure.  Only a   *)
(* message matching a recognised mathematical shape retries; everything else *)
(* is internal and propagates.                                               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Classification is a separate, pure function so it can be tested outside   *)
(* HOL Light: `tests/bridge_failure_selftest.sh` extracts the block between  *)
(* the markers below and runs it with plain OCaml.                           *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* BEGIN BRIDGE_FAILURE_STANDALONE *)
let bridge_failure_has_prefix p s =
  let lp = String.length p in
  String.length s >= lp && String.sub s 0 lp = p
in
let bridge_failure_contains needle s =
  let ln = String.length needle and n = String.length s in
  let rec go i =
    if i + ln > n then false
    else if String.sub s i ln = needle then true
    else go (i + 1) in
  ln = 0 || go 0
in
(* The *allow-list* of recognised mathematical failure shapes.  A failure    *)
(* retries the full hypothesis set only when its message matches one of      *)
(* these; `None' means "not a recognised mathematical failure".              *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   solver-sat        cadical reported SATISFIABLE (exit 10): the slice was *)
(*                     too strong to prove, which is a mathematical outcome. *)
(*   slice-too-strong  an explicit marker that a slice obligation was a     *)
(*                     strictly stronger instance of the goal.              *)
let bridge_math_failure_shape s =
  if bridge_failure_has_prefix "CSAT: cadical did not report UNSAT, exit 10" s
  then Some "solver-sat"
  else if bridge_failure_contains "SATISFIABLE" s then Some "solver-sat"
  else if bridge_failure_has_prefix "SLICE_TOO_STRONG" s then
    Some "slice-too-strong"
  else None
in
(* [IX.78] The classifier returns a portable triple `(kind, detail, limit)'
   with `kind' one of "mathematical", "unsupported", "resource", "internal".
   It used polymorphic variants, which cannot live in this file: the emitted
   answer is preprocessed by HOL Light's camlp5r (revised syntax), where a
   backtick starts a term quotation, so a variant constructor is a parse error
   rather than a value.  The same block is also compiled by plain OCaml in
   `tests/bridge_failure_selftest.sh'.  A string-tagged tuple is the only
   representation that both readers accept.  (Taken from
   `wip/xvi-f2-carry-range' and verified by building an answer, not assumed.) *)
let bridge_failure_class ?(timeout=false) (e:exn) =
  let has_prefix = bridge_failure_has_prefix in
  let exit_code s =
    let needle = "exit " and n = String.length s in
    let ln = String.length needle in
    let rec find i =
      if i + ln > n then None
      else if String.sub s i ln = needle then Some (i + ln)
      else find (i + 1) in
    match find 0 with
    | None -> None
    | Some j ->
        let rec digits k =
          if k < n && s.[k] >= '0' && s.[k] <= '9' then digits (k + 1) else k in
        let k = digits j in
        if k = j then None
        else (try Some (int_of_string (String.sub s j (k - j))) with _ -> None) in
  let classify e =
    match e with
    | Out_of_memory -> ("resource", "memory", "address space (RLIMIT_AS)")
    | Stack_overflow -> ("resource", "stack", "OCaml stack limit")
    | Sys.Break -> ("resource", "interrupt", "Sys.Break")
    | Invalid_argument s -> ("unsupported", s, "")
    | Failure s ->
        let unsupported = "unsupported:" in
        if has_prefix unsupported s then
          ("unsupported",
           String.sub s (String.length unsupported)
             (String.length s - String.length unsupported), "")
        else if has_prefix "CSAT_PROVE: Sanity check" s ||
                has_prefix "CSAT_REFUTE: Sanity check failure" s then
          ("internal", s, "")
        else
          (match exit_code s with
           | Some 124 -> ("resource", "timeout", "exit 124")
           | Some rc when rc >= 128 ->
               ("resource", "signal", "exit " ^ string_of_int rc)
           | _ ->
               (match bridge_math_failure_shape s with
                | Some _ -> ("mathematical", s, "")
                | None -> ("internal", "unrecognised Failure: " ^ s, "")))
    | e -> ("internal", Printexc.to_string e, "") in
