  if timeout then ("resource", "timeout", "wall-clock budget")
  else classify e
in
(* The fallback counter is part of the tested surface: a resource exhaustion
   must leave it at zero. *)
let bridge_fallback_count = ref 0
in
let bridge_slice_retry ~task ~kept ~total ~attempt ~fallback ~note =
  try attempt ()
  with e ->
    (match bridge_failure_class e with
     | ("mathematical", _, _) ->
         note (Printf.sprintf "SLICE fallback=%s reason=mathematical kept=%d/%d"
                 task kept total);
         incr bridge_fallback_count;
         fallback ()
     | ("unsupported", what, _) ->
         note (Printf.sprintf "CSAT unsupported=%s kept=%d/%d" what kept total);
         raise e
     | ("resource", which, limit) ->
         note (Printf.sprintf "CSAT capped=%s limit=%s kept=%d/%d"
                 which limit kept total);
         raise e
     | ("internal", why, _) ->
         note (Printf.sprintf "CSAT internal=%s" why);
         raise e
     | (_, _, _) -> raise e)
in
(* END BRIDGE_FAILURE_STANDALONE *)

let BRIDGE_CSAT_TAC : tactic =
  fun (asl,w) ->
    let hths = map snd asl in
    let total = List.length hths in
    let component = bridge_slice_hyps hths w in
    if bridge_slice_debug then
      List.iteri
        (fun i th ->
           let tm = concl th in
           let s = string_of_term tm in
           let s = if String.length s > 240 then String.sub s 0 240 ^ "..." else s in
           bridge_slice_note "SLICE_HYP %d/%d kept=%d size=%d frees=%d %s"
             (i + 1) total (if List.memq th component then 1 else 0)
             (bridge_term_size tm) (List.length (frees tm)) s)
        hths;
    let kept = bridge_slice_forced hths component in
    let keptn = List.length kept in
    bridge_slice_note "SLICE kept=%d/%d task=%s" keptn total !bridge_slice_task;
    (* The old tail was `MP_TAC th THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]'.  That rewrites the
       antecedents away but leaves `w` itself as the goal, so the tactic
       reported success while never closing anything (measured: the four SAT
       refutations all succeeded and four goals remained).  Chaining MP with
       the produced assumption theorems yields `|- w` directly. *)
    let close hs =
      let imp = itlist (fun a b -> mk_imp(a,b)) (map concl hs) w in
      let th = prove(imp, CSAT_TAC) in
      List.fold_left (fun acc hth -> MP acc hth) th hs in
    let th' =
      if keptn = total then close hths
      else
        bridge_slice_retry
          ~task:(!bridge_slice_task) ~kept:keptn ~total
          ~attempt:(fun () -> close kept)
          ~fallback:(fun () -> close hths)
          ~note:(fun s -> bridge_slice_note "%s" s) in
    ACCEPT_TAC th' (asl,w)
in
(* everything that precedes the SAT call, on the goal *)
let BRIDGE_PREPARE_TAC (expand:tactic) : tactic =
  fun g ->
    (BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_TAC THEN
     expand THEN
     RULE_ASSUM_TAC (CONV_RULE BRIDGE_TO_WORD_CONV) THEN
     CONV_TAC BRIDGE_TO_WORD_CONV) g
in
let BRIDGE_FINISH_TAC expand : tactic =
  fun g -> (BRIDGE_PREPARE_TAC expand THEN BRIDGE_CSAT_TAC) g
in
(* the same, keeping every branch condition as a hypothesis *)
let BRIDGE_FINISH_KEEP_TAC expand : tactic =
  fun g ->
    (BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_KEEP_TAC THEN
     expand THEN
     RULE_ASSUM_TAC (CONV_RULE BRIDGE_TO_WORD_CONV) THEN
     CONV_TAC BRIDGE_TO_WORD_CONV THEN
     BRIDGE_CSAT_TAC) g
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6b. The algebraic close (IX.70, recovering the IX.67 WIP of 0336cb2).     *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* STATUS (IX.70): EXPERIMENTAL, OPT-IN, DOES NOT CLOSE.  Recovered and      *)
(* repaired, this route still fails on `arm/add_p25519' (Stack_overflow in   *)
(* `ASM_INT_ARITH_TAC' on the first residual; the verbatim goal and          *)
(* hypotheses are in `research/receipts/ix70-algebraic-close.md').  The      *)
(* mathematics below is sound (rewrites and a proof-producing decision       *)
(* procedure only; no new axioms, no CHEAT_TAC), and the same linear system  *)
(* *is* closed by `INT_ARITH' when the top carry's integrality is supplied   *)
(* as a disjunction (receipt, probe `close1_full_c8', 0.48 s).  The blocker   *)
(* is the procedure/encoding at this size, not a missing identity.  The      *)
(* emitter therefore selects this entry point only when                 *)
(* `TEKMERION_ALG_CLOSE=<task id>' is set; default answers are unchanged.    *)
(* The generic fix is the carry-conservation lemma of XV.E1, not a bigger    *)
(* call to `INT_ARITH' (XV.D1).                                             *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The residue `BRIDGE_CSAT_TAC' decides is a *value-level* identity: every   *)
(* fact it needs is a library lemma about `val', plus linear arithmetic over  *)
(* the limb values.  Bit-blasting is not required.  The obligation is         *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   &(val (word_add M N)) = &(val W)                  (no correction),      *)
(*   &(val (word_sub (word_add M N) (word p))) = &(val W)  (correction),     *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* where `M', `N' and `W' are word_join nestings of the limb words, together  *)
(* with the accumulator's per-limb equations and the input range conditions.  *)
(* The route is: expand the joins into weighted `val' sums, expand the        *)
(* machine add/sub through `INT_VAL_WORD_ADD_CASES'/                        *)
(* `INT_VAL_WORD_SUB_CASES' (which state the wrap as a conditional), split    *)
(* the conditionals, read the branch's boolean carry flags into their         *)
(* `bitval' values, add the word-domain bounds `0 <= val w < 2^dimindex', and  *)
(* hand the result to integer arithmetic -- which is where it stops.          *)
(* Nothing depends on the limb width or the number of limbs: the recursion is *)
(* the join nesting and the coefficients come out of the goal.  Only the      *)
(* modulus numeral is supplied by the caller, exactly as in the SAT path.     *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Differences from the unverified IX.67 WIP are marked [IX.70]; each was     *)
(* needed to make the route *reach* the arithmetic and each is a generic      *)
(* step, not a p25519 special case.                                          *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* |- val(join x y) = 2 EXP k * val x + val y, unconditionally, at the width
   the join actually has.  BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_STEP already discharges the
   dimindex side condition.  TOP_DEPTH: the rewrite produces new `val ...'
   subterms on its right-hand side, so a nested join only unfolds completely
   if the result is visited again. *)
let rec BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_CONV (tm:term) : thm =
  match tm with
  | Comb(Const("val",_), Comb(Comb(Const("word_join",_),a),b)) ->
      CONV_RULE (RAND_CONV (TRY_CONV BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_CONV) THENC
                 LAND_CONV (RAND_CONV (TRY_CONV BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_CONV)))
                (BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_STEP a b)
  | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_CONV"
in
let BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_DEPTH_CONV : conv = DEPTH_CONV BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_CONV
in
(* |- val(word n) = n for a numeral n that fits the word, at that word's
   width.  VAL_WORD_EQ is the library lemma; only its side condition is
   discharged here, numerically. *)
let BRIDGE_VAL_WORD_CONV : conv =
  let one tm =
    match tm with
    | Comb(Const("val",_), (Comb(Const("word",_), n) as w)) when is_numeral n ->
        let bits = bridge_word_width (type_of w) in
        let th0 = ISPEC n (INST_TYPE [bridge_finty bits, `:N`] VAL_WORD_EQ) in
        let side = prove(lhand (concl th0),
          CONV_TAC(RAND_CONV(RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV) THENC NUM_REDUCE_CONV)) in
        MP th0 side
    | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_VAL_WORD_CONV" in
  DEPTH_CONV one
in
(* `bit (w-1) x' (the x86 correction tests the top bit) as a bound on `val x'.
   `MSB_VAL' states the index as `dimindex(:N) - 1', which does not match the
   reduced numeral in the goal, so the instance is built at the word's own type
   and reduced; the reduction is on the *num* form (`MSB_VAL'), because
   `DEPTH_CONV' over `MSB_INT_VAL''s `&2 pow k' recurses without bound
   (measured: stack overflow). *)
let BRIDGE_BIT_MSB_CONV : conv =
  let one tm =
    match tm with
    | Comb(Comb(Const("bit",_), k), w) when is_numeral k ->
        let bits = bridge_word_width (type_of w) in
        if not (bits >= 1 && Num.eq_num (dest_numeral k) (Num.num_of_int (bits - 1)))
        then failwith "BRIDGE_BIT_MSB_CONV: not the top bit" else
        let th = CONV_RULE (DEPTH_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV)
                   (SPEC w (INST_TYPE [bridge_finty bits, `:N`] MSB_VAL)) in
        let e1 = NUM_REDUCE_CONV
                   (mk_binop `(-):num->num->num`
                      (mk_numeral (Num.num_of_int bits))
                      (mk_numeral (Num.num_of_int 1))) in
        let th = REWRITE_RULE[e1] th in
        let e2 = NUM_REDUCE_CONV
                   (mk_binop `(EXP):num->num->num` `2`
                      (mk_numeral (Num.num_of_int (bits - 1)))) in
        REWRITE_RULE[e2] th
    | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_BIT_MSB_CONV" in
  DEPTH_CONV one
in
(* [IX.70] The WIP normalised the assumptions only through the shifts and
   never rewrote the machine add/sub or the unsigned comparisons.  Two
   consequences, both measured on arm/add_p25519:
     - `word_ult s x \/ word_ule pw s' (the correction condition) stayed a
       word-level disjunction and the arithmetic could not use it;
     - the goal kept `&(val (word_add ...))' opaque, so the wrap-around case of
       `INT_VAL_WORD_ADD_CASES' was never available to the procedure.
   The normalisation below is generic: it is a confluence-free rewrite to the
   integer fragment, run on the goal and every assumption. *)
let BRIDGE_ALG_NORM_ASSUM (th:thm) : thm =
  let th = REWRITE_RULE[WORD_ULT; WORD_ULE; VAL_WORD_0; VAL_WORD_BITVAL;
                        GSYM VAL_EQ_0] th in
  let th = CONV_RULE BRIDGE_BIT_MSB_CONV th in
  let th = CONV_RULE NUM_TO_INT_CONV th in
  let th = CONV_RULE BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_DEPTH_CONV th in
  let th = CONV_RULE BRIDGE_VAL_WORD_CONV th in
  let th = REWRITE_RULE[INT_VAL_WORD_ADD_CASES; INT_VAL_WORD_SUB_CASES] th in
  let th = CONV_RULE BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_DEPTH_CONV th in
  let th = REWRITE_RULE[VAL_WORD_0; VAL_WORD_BITVAL] th in
  let th = CONV_RULE BRIDGE_VAL_WORD_CONV th in
  let th = CONV_RULE (DEPTH_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV) th in
  let th = CONV_RULE NUM_TO_INT_CONV th in
  CONV_RULE INT_REDUCE_CONV th
in
let BRIDGE_ALG_NORM_TAC : tactic =
  fun g ->
    (RULE_ASSUM_TAC BRIDGE_ALG_NORM_ASSUM THEN
     REWRITE_TAC[WORD_ULT; WORD_ULE; VAL_WORD_0; VAL_WORD_BITVAL;
                 GSYM VAL_EQ_0] THEN
     CONV_TAC NUM_TO_INT_CONV THEN
     CONV_TAC BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_DEPTH_CONV THEN
     CONV_TAC BRIDGE_VAL_WORD_CONV THEN
     REWRITE_TAC[INT_VAL_WORD_ADD_CASES; INT_VAL_WORD_SUB_CASES] THEN
     CONV_TAC BRIDGE_VAL_JOIN_DEPTH_CONV THEN
     REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD_0; VAL_WORD_BITVAL] THEN
     CONV_TAC BRIDGE_VAL_WORD_CONV THEN
     CONV_TAC (DEPTH_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV) THEN
     CONV_TAC NUM_TO_INT_CONV THEN
     CONV_TAC INT_REDUCE_CONV) g
in
(* [IX.70] A branch condition kept as a boolean fact (for example
   `carry_s13') also fixes the value of `bitval carry_s13'.  The WIP left the
   two unrelated, so an impossible branch such as "the select took the
   corrected word but ref_add did not correct" was not refutable.  The rewrite
   uses the branch fact *as an assumption* (not via `prove', which would have
   to discharge it), so it is contextual and always available here. *)
let BRIDGE_BITVAL_ATOMS tm =
  find_terms (fun t -> match t with
    | Comb(Const("bitval",_),_) -> true
    | _ -> false) tm
in
let BRIDGE_DECIDE_BITVALS_TAC : tactic =
  fun (asl,w) ->
    let atoms = setify
      (BRIDGE_BITVAL_ATOMS w @
       List.concat (map (fun (_,th) -> BRIDGE_BITVAL_ATOMS (concl th)) asl)) in
    let rules = List.fold_right (fun t acc ->
      match t with
      | Comb(_,b) ->
          (match List.find_opt (fun (_,th) -> concl th = b) asl with
           | Some(_,th) -> th :: acc
           | None ->
               (match List.find_opt (fun (_,th) -> concl th = mk_neg b) asl with
                | Some(_,th) -> EQF_INTRO th :: acc
                | None -> acc))
      | _ -> acc) atoms [] in
    if rules = [] then ALL_TAC (asl,w)
    else
      let rs = rules @ [BITVAL_CLAUSES] in
      (RULE_ASSUM_TAC (REWRITE_RULE rs) THEN REWRITE_TAC rs) (asl,w)
in
(* [IX.70] INT_ARITH/ARITH_RULE reason over the *reals* (the error text is
   `linear_ineqs: no contradiction'): `0 <= c <= 1' does not make a carry
   integral, so the procedure cannot conclude `c = 0' even though the chain
   forces it.  The fix is to case-split the one carry whose integrality is
   load-bearing -- the carry *out of the most significant limb's addition*,
   i.e. the carry with the limb weight 2^k on the side of the hypothesis that
   also contains the highest-weighted input atom.  In every branch here the
   corrected carry (the selection flag) is already decided by a branch fact, so
   only the raw add's top carry remains.  The rule is structural: no limb
   width and no numeral is named.  Splitting every undecided bitval instead is
   exponential in the number of carries and was measured to exhaust memory on
   this obligation. *)
let BRIDGE_NUM_OF_COEF t =
  try Some(dest_numeral t) with _ -> None
in
(* weight of `atom' in `tm', counting numerals as multipliers: the nested form
   2^k*(2^k*(2^k*a+b)+c)+d gives a the weight 2^(3k). *)
let rec BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT atom tm =
  if aconv tm atom then Num.num_of_int 1
  else match tm with
    | Comb(Comb(Const("int_add",_), a), b) ->
        Num.add_num (BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT atom a) (BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT atom b)
    | Comb(Comb(Const("int_mul",_), a), b) ->
        (match BRIDGE_NUM_OF_COEF (rand a) with
         | Some k -> Num.mult_num k (BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT atom b)
         | None -> BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT atom b)
    | Comb(_, x) -> BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT atom x
    | Abs(_, x) -> BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT atom x
    | _ -> Num.num_of_int 0
in
let BRIDGE_VAL_ATOMS tm =
  find_terms (fun t -> match t with
    | Comb(Const("val",_),_) -> true
    | _ -> false) tm
in
let BRIDGE_BITVAL_COEF_PAIRS tm =
  let prods = find_terms (fun t -> match t with
    | Comb(Comb(Const("int_mul",_), Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), n)),
           Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("bitval",_),_)))
        when is_numeral n -> true
    | _ -> false) tm in
  let bare = find_terms (fun t -> match t with
    | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("bitval",_),_)) -> true
    | _ -> false) tm in
  List.fold_right (fun t acc ->
    match BRIDGE_NUM_OF_COEF (rand(rand(rator t))) with
    | Some k -> (rand(rand(rand t)), k) :: acc
    | None -> acc) prods
   (List.map (fun t -> (rand(rand t), Num.num_of_int 1)) bare)
in
let BRIDGE_MAX_COEF pairs =
  let better ((_,k) as a) ((_,k') as b) = if Num.le_num k k' then b else a in
  match pairs with [] -> None | h :: tl -> Some(List.fold_left better h tl)
in
let BRIDGE_DECIDED_BITVAL asl b =
  List.exists (fun (_,th) -> concl th = b || concl th = mk_neg b) asl
in
(* [IX.70] `ASM_INT_ARITH_TAC' quantifies over *every* assumption.  The
   non-arithmetic ones (`nonoverlapping_modulo ...', which mentions `val z',
   and the bare branch booleans already consumed by the bitval step) are not
   needed and were measured to push the procedure into a stack overflow.
   Dropping an assumption can only strengthen the goal. *)
let BRIDGE_HAS_INT tm =
  List.exists (fun s -> match s with
    | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_),_) -> true
    | _ -> false) (find_terms (fun _ -> true) tm)
in
let BRIDGE_DISCARD_IRRELEVANT_TAC : tactic =
  let irrelevant th =
    let t = concl th in
    t = `T` || not (BRIDGE_HAS_INT t) in
  fun (asl,w) ->
    ALL_TAC (List.filter (fun (_,th) -> not (irrelevant th)) asl, w)
in
let BRIDGE_INT_REDUCE_TAC : tactic =
  fun g ->
    (RULE_ASSUM_TAC (CONV_RULE INT_REDUCE_CONV) THEN
     CONV_TAC INT_REDUCE_CONV) g
in
let BRIDGE_SPLIT_TOP_CARRY_TAC : tactic =
  fun (asl,w) ->
    let hyps = List.map (fun (_,th) -> concl th) asl in
    let atoms = setify (List.concat (List.map BRIDGE_VAL_ATOMS hyps)) in
    let maxabs x =
      List.fold_left (fun a t ->
        let k = BRIDGE_TERM_WEIGHT x t in if Num.le_num a k then k else a)
        (Num.num_of_int 0) hyps in
    let scored = List.map (fun x -> (x, maxabs x)) atoms in
    (match BRIDGE_MAX_COEF scored with
     | None -> ALL_TAC (asl,w)
     | Some(msatom, _) ->
        let carriers = List.concat (List.map (fun t ->
          if List.exists (fun s -> aconv s msatom) (BRIDGE_VAL_ATOMS t)
          then BRIDGE_BITVAL_COEF_PAIRS t else []) hyps) in
        let carriers = List.filter
          (fun (b,_) -> not (BRIDGE_DECIDED_BITVAL asl b)) carriers in
        (match BRIDGE_MAX_COEF carriers with
         | None -> ALL_TAC (asl,w)
         | Some(b, _) ->
             (ASM_CASES_TAC b THENL
               [BRIDGE_DECIDE_BITVALS_TAC THEN BRIDGE_INT_REDUCE_TAC THEN ALL_TAC;
                BRIDGE_DECIDE_BITVALS_TAC THEN BRIDGE_INT_REDUCE_TAC THEN ALL_TAC]) (asl,w)))
in
(* The linear decision procedure sees `&(val w)' and `&(bitval b)' as atoms of
   unknown sign.  They are not: a `val' is in [0, 2^dimindex) and a `bitval' is
   0 or 1.  The WIP supplied only the lower bound of `val' and the two bitval
   bounds; without `val w < 2^dimindex' the carries of the accumulator chain
   are not pinned, and the overflow branches of the add cannot be refuted
   (measured: `linear_ineqs: no contradiction'). *)
let BRIDGE_INT_ATOMS tm =
  find_terms (fun t -> match t with
    | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("val",_),_)) -> true
    | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("bitval",_),_)) -> true
    | _ -> false) tm
in
let BRIDGE_INT_LE a b = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<=):int->int->bool`, a), b)
in
let BRIDGE_INT_LT a b = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):int->int->bool`, a), b)
in
let BRIDGE_BOUND_NONNEG t =
  prove(BRIDGE_INT_LE `(&0):int` t,
        REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LE] THEN ARITH_TAC)
in
let BRIDGE_BOUND_BITVAL_HI t =
  prove(BRIDGE_INT_LE t `(&1):int`,
        REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LE] THEN REWRITE_TAC[bitval] THEN
        TRY COND_CASES_TAC THEN ARITH_TAC)
in
(* &(val w) < &2 pow dimindex at the width `w' actually has: the library's
   INT_VAL_BOUND, instantiated and reduced to a numeral (dimindex(:64) left
   unreduced makes the atom opaque to the integer procedure). *)
let BRIDGE_BOUND_VAL_HI w =
  let bits = bridge_word_width (type_of w) in
  CONV_RULE (DEPTH_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC INT_REDUCE_CONV)
    (ISPEC w (INST_TYPE [bridge_finty bits, `:N`] INT_VAL_BOUND))
in
let BRIDGE_ATOM_BOUNDS_TAC : tactic =
  fun (asl,w) ->
    let atoms = setify
      (BRIDGE_INT_ATOMS w @
       List.concat (map (fun (_,th) -> BRIDGE_INT_ATOMS (concl th)) asl)) in
    let facts = List.fold_right (fun t acc ->
      match t with
      | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("bitval",_),_)) ->
          BRIDGE_BOUND_BITVAL_HI t :: BRIDGE_BOUND_NONNEG t :: acc
      | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("val",_),w0)) ->
          BRIDGE_BOUND_VAL_HI w0 :: BRIDGE_BOUND_NONNEG t :: acc
      | _ -> acc) atoms [] in
    if facts = [] then ALL_TAC (asl,w)
    else (MP_TAC (end_itlist CONJ facts) THEN STRIP_TAC) (asl,w)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.2b The top-bit mask (IX.83).                                           *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* `sub_p25519' and `neg_p25519' end with `AND x (2 EXP 255 - 1)' at the word *)
(* level, which is `val(word_and x (word(2^(w-1)-1)))'.  As an integer atom  *)
(* that is `val x MOD 2^(w-1)', and the linear prover has no MOD: the       *)
(* aggregate close cannot relate it to `val x'.  It does not have to: for a  *)
(* `w'-bit word `val x < 2^w = 2 * 2^(w-1)', so the top bit is either clear *)
(* (the truncated value is `val x') or set (it is `val x - 2^(w-1)').  Both  *)
(* directions are proved from `VAL_WORD_AND_MASK_WORD' and `MOD_CASES'; the  *)
(* tactic below case-splits on `val x < 2^(w-1)' and assumes the matching    *)
(* *equation*, not a disjunction: an added disjunction would be re-found by  *)
(* `BRIDGE_SPLIT_INT_DISJ_TAC' (which leaves the hypothesis in place) and    *)
(* split forever.  Nothing here names a curve or an instruction.             *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let BRIDGE_EXP_STEP = prove
 (`!k:num. 2 EXP (k + 1) = 2 * 2 EXP k`,
  GEN_TAC THEN REWRITE_TAC[EXP_ADD; EXP_1; MULT_AC])
in
let BRIDGE_VAL_TOP_MASK_BOUND = prove
 (`!(x:N word). val x < 2 * 2 EXP (dimindex(:N) - 1)`,
  GEN_TAC THEN REWRITE_TAC[GSYM BRIDGE_EXP_STEP] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `1 <= dimindex(:N)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [REWRITE_TAC[DIMINDEX_GE_1]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `dimindex(:N) - 1 + 1 = dimindex(:N)` SUBST1_TAC THENL
   [ASM_ARITH_TAC; REWRITE_TAC[VAL_BOUND]])
in
let BRIDGE_AND_TOP_MASK_LOW = prove
 (`!(x:N word).
     val x < 2 EXP (dimindex(:N) - 1)
     ==> int_of_num(val(word_and x (word(2 EXP (dimindex(:N) - 1) - 1)))) =
         int_of_num(val x)`,
  REPEAT STRIP_TAC THEN
  MP_TAC(ISPECL [`x:N word`; `dimindex(:N) - 1`] VAL_WORD_AND_MASK_WORD) THEN
  DISCH_THEN SUBST1_TAC THEN
  AP_TERM_TAC THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[])
in
let BRIDGE_AND_TOP_MASK_HIGH = prove
 (`!(x:N word).
     ~(val x < 2 EXP (dimindex(:N) - 1))
     ==> int_of_num(val(word_and x (word(2 EXP (dimindex(:N) - 1) - 1)))) +
         int_of_num(2 EXP (dimindex(:N) - 1)) = int_of_num(val x)`,
  REPEAT STRIP_TAC THEN
  MP_TAC(ISPECL [`x:N word`; `dimindex(:N) - 1`] VAL_WORD_AND_MASK_WORD) THEN
  DISCH_THEN SUBST1_TAC THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_ADD] THEN AP_TERM_TAC THEN
  MP_TAC(ISPECL [`val(x:N word)`; `2 EXP (dimindex(:N) - 1)`] MOD_CASES) THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[BRIDGE_VAL_TOP_MASK_BOUND] THEN
  DISCH_THEN SUBST1_TAC THEN
  ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC)
in
(* the `val(word_and x (word m))' atom and its argument, when the numeral    *)
(* mask is the low `w-1' bits of a `w'-bit word.  Any other mask is left     *)
(* alone (it is not a top-bit truncation).                                   *)
let bridge_top_mask_atom t =
  match t with
  | Comb((Const("val",_) as v), Comb(Comb(Const("word_and",_), x),
                                      Comb(Const("word",_), n)))
    when is_numeral n ->
      (try
         let bits = bridge_word_width (type_of x) in
         let rec pow2 k = if k <= 0 then num_1
           else Num.mult_num (Num.num_of_int 2) (pow2 (k - 1)) in
         let mask = Num.sub_num (pow2 (bits - 1)) num_1 in
         if bits >= 1 && Num.eq_num (dest_numeral n) mask
         then Some (t, v, x) else None
       with _ -> None)
  | _ -> None
in
let bridge_mask_atoms tm =
  List.fold_left (fun acc u ->
      match bridge_top_mask_atom u with
      | Some (t,v,x) when not (List.exists (fun (_,_,y) -> aconv x y) acc) ->
          acc @ [(t,v,x)]
      | _ -> acc) [] (find_terms (fun _ -> true) tm)
in
let bridge_has_top_mask tm =
  bridge_mask_atoms tm <> []
in
(* case-split the top bit of every masked limb and assume the equation it    *)
(* determines, so the linear close sees `val(mask)' as an affine function of *)
(* `val x' in each branch.                                                    *)
let BRIDGE_AND_MASK_FACTS_TAC : tactic =
  fun (asl,w) ->
    let atoms =
      List.fold_left (fun acc tm ->
          List.fold_left (fun a (t,v,x) ->
              if List.exists (fun (_,_,y) -> aconv x y) a then a
              else a @ [(t,v,x)])
            acc (bridge_mask_atoms tm))
        [] (w :: List.map (fun (_,th) -> concl th) asl) in
    bridge_slice_note "MASK atoms=%d [%s]" (List.length atoms)
      (String.concat "," (List.map (fun (_,_,x) -> string_of_term x) atoms));
    let one (mt,v,x) : tactic =
      let bits = bridge_word_width (type_of x) in
      let rec pow2 k = if k <= 0 then num_1
        else Num.mult_num (Num.num_of_int 2) (pow2 (k - 1)) in
      let top = pow2 (bits - 1) in
      let topn = mk_numeral top in
      let y = mk_comb(v, x) in
      let iy = mk_comb(`int_of_num:num->int`, y)
      and im = mk_comb(`int_of_num:num->int`, mt)
      and ie = mk_comb(`int_of_num:num->int`, topn) in
      let cond = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):num->num->bool`, y), topn) in
      let cond_int = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):int->int->bool`, iy), ie) in
      let cond_int_ge = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<=):int->int->bool`, ie), iy) in
      let low = CONV_RULE (DEPTH_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_REDUCE_CONV)
                  (ISPEC x (INST_TYPE [bridge_finty bits, `:N`] BRIDGE_AND_TOP_MASK_LOW))
      and high = CONV_RULE (DEPTH_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_REDUCE_CONV)
                  (ISPEC x (INST_TYPE [bridge_finty bits, `:N`] BRIDGE_AND_TOP_MASK_HIGH)) in
      (* the boolean case becomes an *integer* bound as well, so the close can
         bound the written word by `2^(w-1)' in the low case and `2^(w-1)'
         from below in the high case. *)
      ASM_CASES_TAC cond THENL
       [SUBGOAL_THEN cond_int ASSUME_TAC THENL
         [REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LT] THEN FIRST_ASSUM ACCEPT_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
        SUBGOAL_THEN (mk_eq(im, iy)) ASSUME_TAC THENL
         [MATCH_MP_TAC low THEN FIRST_ASSUM ACCEPT_TAC; ALL_TAC];
        SUBGOAL_THEN cond_int_ge ASSUME_TAC THENL
         [REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_LE] THEN
          MATCH_MP_TAC(ARITH_RULE `~(a:num < b) ==> b <= a`) THEN
          FIRST_ASSUM ACCEPT_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
        SUBGOAL_THEN (mk_eq(mk_binop `(+):int->int->int` im ie, iy)) ASSUME_TAC THENL
         [MATCH_MP_TAC high THEN FIRST_ASSUM ACCEPT_TAC; ALL_TAC]] in
    EVERY (List.map one atoms) (asl,w)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c. The oracle close (IX.78).                                             *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* IX.70 handed the whole residue to `ASM_INT_ARITH_TAC' and it exhausted the   *)
(* stack.  The receipt isolated the reason: the procedure is a *rational*     *)
(* linear prover, the accumulator carries are integers bounded by 0 and 1,    *)
(* and nothing in the 60-hypothesis encoding lets it use that.  The human     *)
(* s2n-bignum proof does three things instead (see                            *)
(* `.bench/human-baseline/arm/proofs/bignum_add_p25519.ml'): it identifies    *)
(* the top carry as a *flag* over the specification's own comparison         *)
(* (`FLAG_FROM_CARRY_LE'), it collapses the limb equations with a            *)
(* carry-conservation rule (`GEN_DECARRY_RULE'), and only then calls a        *)
(* linear prover.                                                            *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* This section does the same, without naming a curve, a width or a limb      *)
(* count:                                                                    *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   1. Linearise every integer hypothesis into an exact rational form        *)
(*      `sum (k_i * atom_i) + c = 0' (or `<=`/`<`), atoms being the opaque     *)
(*      terms `&(val w)' and `&(bitval b)'.  Anything non-linear is dropped.  *)
(*   2. Eliminate the atoms that do *not* occur in the goal, by exact          *)
(*      Gauss-Jordan.  What is left are the *aggregate* identities -- the      *)
(*      carry-conservation lemmas of `XV.E1' for this instance -- and the      *)
(*      definitions of the eliminated atoms in terms of the goal's atoms.      *)
(*      The elimination multiplies rows by each other's pivot coefficient, so  *)
(*      every coefficient stays an integer: no division is introduced.         *)
(*   3. The oracle: for each carry atom that survives, ask the *linear          *)
(*      relaxation* (the same rational procedure `INT_ARITH' runs, but on the   *)
(*      reduced system and only the hypotheses whose atoms it mentions) for a   *)
(*      pinning value `c = 0' or `c = 1'.  A success is the solver's decision    *)
(*      and yields the *proof* of the fact, so nothing is asserted.  A failure  *)
(*      is reported as `undetermined' and the close simply proceeds without it. *)
(*      The decision is per theorem: it is read from this goal's terms, its     *)
(*      bounds and this system's elimination, never from a per-class template.  *)
(*   4. Hand the residual -- the aggregate rows, the emitted facts and the      *)
(*      integer hypotheses -- to the linear prover.  The system it now sees has *)
(*      two or three equations, not sixty.                                     *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The old route (`BRIDGE_SPLIT_TOP_CARRY_TAC' + `ASM_INT_ARITH_TAC') is kept   *)
(* below and is no longer called; it is the IX.70 attempt, recorded in          *)
(* `research/receipts/ix70-algebraic-close.md'.                                *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_int_add_tm = `(+):int->int->int`
and bridge_int_mul_tm = `(*):int->int->int`
and bridge_int_neg_tm = `(--):int->int`
and bridge_int_of_num_tm = `int_of_num:num->int`
in
(* an integer literal, negative ones as `-- &|k|' *)
let bridge_int_lit k =
  let m = mk_comb(bridge_int_of_num_tm, mk_numeral (Num.abs_num k)) in
  if Num.lt_num k num_0 then mk_comb(bridge_int_neg_tm, m) else m
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.1 Sparse exact rational linear forms.                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_lf_coeff t xs =
  try snd (List.find (fun (u,_) -> aconv u t) xs) with Not_found -> num_0
in
(* the coefficient of an atom in a form (a form is `(sparse, constant)') *)
let bridge_lf_coeff_in t (xs,_) = bridge_lf_coeff t xs
in
let rec bridge_lf_addc xs t k =
  match xs with
  | [] -> if Num.eq_num k num_0 then [] else [(t,k)]
  | (u,k0)::rest ->
      if aconv u t then
        (let k' = Num.add_num k0 k in
         if Num.eq_num k' num_0 then rest else (u,k')::rest)
      else (u,k0) :: bridge_lf_addc rest t k
in
let bridge_lf_add (xs,c) (ys,d) =
  let xs' = List.fold_left (fun a (t,k) -> bridge_lf_addc a t k) xs ys in
  (xs', Num.add_num c d)
in
let bridge_lf_scale k (xs,c) =
  if Num.eq_num k num_0 then ([], num_0)
  else (List.map (fun (t,j) -> (t, Num.mult_num k j)) xs, Num.mult_num k c)
in
let bridge_lf_neg f = bridge_lf_scale (Num.minus_num num_1) f
in
let bridge_lf_vars (xs,_) = List.map fst xs
in
(* a numeral coefficient: `&k' is `int_of_num (&k)', and `-- &k' (the form  *)
(* `bridge_lf_term' emits for a negative coefficient) is its negation.  The   *)
(* negated-literal case is needed for the aggregate to be re-linearisable: the *)
(* canonical flat form spells `-3 * x' as `-- &3 * x', and a parser that only *)
(* knows `&k' would report the aggregate as non-linear.                    *)
let rec bridge_lf_num t =
  match t with
  | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), n) when is_numeral n -> Some(dest_numeral n)
  | Comb(Const("int_neg",_), u) ->
      (match bridge_lf_num u with
       | Some k -> Some(Num.minus_num k)
       | None -> None)
  | _ -> None
in
let rec bridge_lf_of_term tm =
  match tm with
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_add",_),a),b) ->
      (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
       | Some x, Some y -> Some(bridge_lf_add x y)
       | _ -> None)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_sub",_),a),b) ->
      (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
       | Some x, Some y -> Some(bridge_lf_add x (bridge_lf_neg y))
       | _ -> None)
  | Comb(Const("int_neg",_),a) ->
      (match bridge_lf_of_term a with Some x -> Some(bridge_lf_neg x) | None -> None)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_mul",_),a),b) ->
      (match bridge_lf_num a with
       | Some k -> (match bridge_lf_of_term b with
                    | Some y -> Some(bridge_lf_scale k y) | None -> None)
       | None ->
           (match bridge_lf_num b with
            | Some k -> (match bridge_lf_of_term a with
                         | Some x -> Some(bridge_lf_scale k x) | None -> None)
            | None -> None))
  | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_),n) when is_numeral n -> Some([], dest_numeral n)
  | _ -> Some(([(tm, num_1)], num_0))
in
(* the row of an integer equation, `lhs - rhs = 0' *)
let bridge_lf_row_of_thm th =
  let t = concl th in
  if not (is_eq t) || type_of (lhand t) <> `:int` then None else
  match bridge_lf_of_term (lhand t), bridge_lf_of_term (rand t) with
  | Some l, Some r -> Some(bridge_lf_add l (bridge_lf_neg r))
  | _ -> None
in
(* the integer hypotheses, as (theorem, linear form >= 0 / > 0, strict) *)
let bridge_lf_ineqs asl =
  List.filter_map
    (fun (_,th) ->
      let t = concl th in
      if type_of t <> `:bool` then None else
      match t with
      | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b) ->
          (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
           | Some x, Some y -> Some(th, bridge_lf_add y (bridge_lf_neg x), false)
           | _ -> None)
      | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) ->
          (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
           | Some x, Some y -> Some(th, bridge_lf_add y (bridge_lf_neg x), true)
           | _ -> None)
      | _ -> None)
    asl
in
(* build `sum k_i * x_i' as one int term *)
let bridge_lf_term (xs,c) =
  let prods = List.map (fun (t,k) ->
      if Num.eq_num k num_1 then t
      else mk_binop bridge_int_mul_tm (bridge_int_lit k) t) xs in
  let all = if Num.eq_num c num_0 then prods else prods @ [bridge_int_lit c] in
  match all with
  | [] -> bridge_int_lit num_0
  | t::ts -> List.fold_left (fun a b -> mk_binop bridge_int_add_tm a b) t ts
in
(* the equation `sum k_i * x_i + c = 0' in the shape `lhs = rhs' *)
let bridge_lf_eq (xs,c) =
  mk_eq(bridge_lf_term (xs, num_0), bridge_int_lit (Num.minus_num c))
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.2 Exact Gauss-Jordan over the integer hypotheses.                       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Rows are `(id, support, form)' with `form = 0'.  A variable is *internal*  *)
(* when it does not occur in the goal.  Internal variables are eliminated     *)
(* one at a time, from every row *and every definition already found*, so a   *)
(* definition is always expressed in the final free atoms.  The elimination   *)
(* is `k2 * row2 - k1 * row1', which keeps integer coefficients.              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_lf_in_goal keep t = List.exists (aconv t) keep
in
(* the carry atoms, first in the elimination order, so that each carry of a
   chain is a pivot in its own definition *)
let bridge_is_bitval_atom t =
  match t with
  | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("bitval",_),_)) -> true
  | _ -> false
in
let bridge_prioritise_carries vars =
  let carries, others = List.partition bridge_is_bitval_atom vars in
  carries @ others
in
let bridge_internal_vars keep forms =
  let rec go acc = function
    | [] -> List.rev acc
    | (xs,_)::rest ->
        let acc' = List.fold_left (fun a (t,_) ->
            if List.exists (aconv t) a || bridge_lf_in_goal keep t then a
            else if bridge_is_bitval_atom t then a @ [t]
            else a) acc xs in
        go acc' rest in
  go [] forms
in
let rec bridge_eliminate_from v pivot psup rows =
  (* replace each row by `kv * row - k * pivot', carrying the pivot's support *)
  match rows with
  | [] -> []
  | (j,sup,f)::rest ->
      let k = bridge_lf_coeff_in v f in
      let f' = if Num.eq_num k num_0 then f
               else bridge_lf_add (bridge_lf_scale (bridge_lf_coeff_in v pivot) f)
                      (bridge_lf_neg (bridge_lf_scale k pivot)) in
      let sup' = if Num.eq_num k num_0 then sup else sup @ psup in
      (j,sup',f') :: bridge_eliminate_from v pivot psup rest
in
let bridge_gauss_jordan keep rows =
  let vars = bridge_prioritise_carries
               (bridge_internal_vars keep (List.map (fun (_,_,f) -> f) rows)) in
  (* eliminate the new pivot `v' from an older definition, keeping integers *)
  let elim_def v psup pivot (w,dsup,f) =
    let kv = bridge_lf_coeff_in v pivot
    and k = bridge_lf_coeff_in v f in
    if Num.eq_num k num_0 then (w,dsup,f)
    else (w, dsup @ psup,
          bridge_lf_add (bridge_lf_scale kv f)
            (bridge_lf_neg (bridge_lf_scale k pivot))) in
  let rec loop vars rows defs =
    match vars with
    | [] -> (List.rev defs, rows)
    | v::vs ->
        (match List.find_opt
                 (fun (_,_,f) -> not (Num.eq_num (bridge_lf_coeff_in v f) num_0))
                 rows with
         | None -> loop vs rows defs
         | Some (i,sup,f) ->
             let others = List.filter (fun (j,_,_) -> j <> i) rows in
             let others = bridge_eliminate_from v f sup others in
             let defs' = List.map (elim_def v sup f) defs in
             loop vs others ((v, sup, f) :: defs'))
  in loop vars rows []
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.3a The interval relaxation.                                            *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* `INT_ARITH' on a *false* bound is expensive (it searches for a            *)
(* contradiction that is not there: measured Stack_overflow after ~18 s on   *)
(* `carry_s3 < 1', and one 12 G cap firing in the third bridge of           *)
(* arm/add_p25519).  So the oracle does not ask the procedure whether a       *)
(* value holds; it *computes* the rational interval first, with exact        *)
(* arithmetic, and asks only for the bounds it already knows are true.       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The engine is interval arithmetic over the linear forms, with one          *)
(* relational hypothesis used per bound.  That is what is needed: the top    *)
(* carry of an add is bounded by `M + N < B^n', a fact about a *sum* of      *)
(* atoms, not by any single atom's bound.                                    *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* Bounds are (value, strict), meaning `x > value' when strict and
   `x >= value' otherwise.  `None' has *two* meanings and they must not be
   confused (XIX.A):

   - in a *join* of constraints on the same quantity it means "no constraint"
     (=-inf for a lower bound, =+inf for an upper bound), which is the identity
     of max/min;
   - for a *sum* it means "unknown", and it must propagate.  `0 <= x <= 3' and
     an unbounded y must give an unbounded x+y, never a coincidental 0.

   No variant type: this file is also read by camlp5r.  The block below is
   extracted verbatim by tests/interval_engine_selftest.sh and checked against
   brute-force enumeration. *)
(* BEGIN BRIDGE_INTERVAL_STANDALONE *)
(* Join of two constraints on the *same* quantity: max of lower bounds, min of
   upper bounds.  Used only by bridge_direct_bounds (two hypotheses about one
   atom) and bridge_hi (two derivations of an upper bound for one form). *)
let bridge_bound_join_lo a b =
  match a,b with
  | None, x | x, None -> x
  | Some(v1,s1), Some(v2,s2) ->
      if Num.lt_num v1 v2 then Some(v1,s1)
      else if Num.lt_num v2 v1 then Some(v2,s2)
      else Some(v1, s1 || s2)
in
let bridge_bound_join_hi a b =
  match a,b with
  | None, x | x, None -> x
  | Some(v1,s1), Some(v2,s2) ->
      if Num.lt_num v2 v1 then Some(v1,s1)
      else if Num.lt_num v1 v2 then Some(v2,s2)
      else Some(v1, s1 || s2)
in
(* Addition of bounds for a *sum*: x in A and y in B give x+y in A+B, so the
   endpoints add and the strictness is inherited (x > a and y > b give
   x+y > a+b).  A missing endpoint is *unknown* and stays unknown: dropping it
   would treat an unbounded summand as 0. *)
let bridge_bound_add_lo a b =
  match a,b with
  | None, _ | _, None -> None
  | Some(v1,s1), Some(v2,s2) -> Some(Num.add_num v1 v2, s1 || s2)
in
let bridge_bound_add_hi a b =
  match a,b with
  | None, _ | _, None -> None
  | Some(v1,s1), Some(v2,s2) -> Some(Num.add_num v1 v2, s1 || s2)
in
(* contribution of one atom with coefficient k to (lo,hi): k*x is increasing
   for k > 0, decreasing for k < 0 (the two endpoints swap), and the zero
   contribution for k = 0 is the exact point 0, whatever the atom's bounds. *)
let bridge_bound_contrib k (l,h) =
  let scale b = match b with
    | None -> None
    | Some(v,s) -> Some(Num.mult_num k v, s) in
  if Num.eq_num k num_0 then (Some(num_0,false), Some(num_0,false))
  else if Num.lt_num num_0 k then (scale l, scale h)
  else (scale h, scale l)
in
(* bounds of a sum of scaled atoms plus a constant.  This is *addition* at
   every step, not a join; `lookup' supplies the one-atom table. *)
let bridge_bounds_of_terms lookup c terms =
  List.fold_left (fun (lo,hi) (t,k) ->
      let (cl,ch) = bridge_bound_contrib k (lookup t) in
      (bridge_bound_add_lo lo cl, bridge_bound_add_hi hi ch))
    ((Some (c,false)), (Some (c,false))) terms
in
(* END BRIDGE_INTERVAL_STANDALONE *)

(* direct one-atom bounds from the hypotheses: a form with one variable and a
   constant is a lower bound when its coefficient is positive, an upper bound
   when it is negative.  Two hypotheses about the *same* atom are two
   constraints on one quantity, so this is a join (max lower, min upper), and
   `None' here means "this hypothesis gives no bound", the join identity. *)
let bridge_direct_bounds ineqs =
  let add tbl t lo hi =
    let (lo0,hi0) = try List.assoc t tbl with Not_found -> (None,None) in
    (t,(bridge_bound_join_lo lo0 lo, bridge_bound_join_hi hi0 hi))
    :: List.remove_assoc t tbl in
  List.fold_left (fun tbl (_,(xs,c),strict) ->
      match xs with
      | [(x,k)] ->
          let v = (Num.div_num (Num.minus_num c) k, strict) in
          if Num.lt_num num_0 k then add tbl x (Some v) None
          else add tbl x None (Some v)
      | _ -> tbl) [] ineqs
in
let bridge_lookup_bound tbl t =
  try List.assoc t tbl with Not_found -> (None,None)
in
(* bounds of a linear form from the one-atom table.  The form is a *sum*, so
   the scaled contributions are added (bridge_bounds_of_terms); the join is
   only used for the relational bound in bridge_hi. *)
let bridge_form_bounds tbl (xs,c) =
  bridge_bounds_of_terms (bridge_lookup_bound tbl) c xs
in
(* upper bound of a form, using one relational hypothesis; `None' if none
   applies.  `t = alpha * f + rest' where `f' shares a proportional part. *)
let bridge_rel_hi tbl ineqs t =
  let (txs,_) = t in
  let try_one (_,(fxs,fc),strict) =
    let shared = List.filter (fun (x,_) ->
        List.exists (fun (y,_) -> aconv x y) txs) fxs in
    match shared with
    | [] -> None
    | (x0,_)::_ ->
        let k0 = bridge_lf_coeff x0 txs and kf = bridge_lf_coeff x0 fxs in
        if Num.eq_num kf num_0 then None else
        let alpha = Num.div_num k0 kf in
        let prop = List.for_all (fun (x,_) ->
            Num.eq_num (bridge_lf_coeff x txs)
                       (Num.mult_num alpha (bridge_lf_coeff x fxs))) shared in
        if not prop || not (Num.lt_num alpha num_0) then None else
        let f = (fxs,fc) in
        let rest = bridge_lf_add t (bridge_lf_neg (bridge_lf_scale alpha f)) in
        let (_,hi) = bridge_form_bounds tbl rest in
        (match hi with
         | Some(v,s) ->
             (* alpha < 0 and f > 0 (or >= 0): alpha*f < 0 (strict if f strict) *)
             if strict then Some (v,true) else Some (v,s)
         | None -> None) in
  List.fold_left (fun acc ineq ->
      match acc with
      | Some _ -> acc
      | None -> try_one ineq) None ineqs
in
(* two independent derivations of an *upper* bound for the same form; the
   tighter one wins, so this is a join (min), and `None' is +inf. *)
let bridge_hi tbl ineqs t =
  let (_,hi) = bridge_form_bounds tbl t in
  match bridge_rel_hi tbl ineqs t with
  | None -> hi
  | Some h -> bridge_bound_join_hi hi (Some h)
in
let bridge_lo_of_neg tbl ineqs t = 
  match bridge_hi tbl ineqs (bridge_lf_neg t) with
  | Some(v,s) -> Some(Num.minus_num v, s)
  | None -> None
in
(*                                                                           *)
(* The *linear relaxation* of the system is the equations plus the interval   *)
(* bounds read as rationals; the procedure that decides its consequences is   *)
(* the same one `INT_ARITH' uses.  It is consulted only on a *reduced*        *)
(* system (the definition of the atom, and the hypotheses all of whose atoms  *)
(* occur in that definition), so a negative answer is cheap and cannot        *)
(* wander into the 60-hypothesis search that exhausted the stack under       *)
(* IX.70.                                                                     *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_lf_atoms form = List.map fst (fst form)
in
let bridge_atom_in atoms u = List.exists (aconv u) atoms
in
(* the hypotheses whose atoms are all among `atoms' *)
let bridge_cone atoms ineqs =
  List.filter (fun (_,f,_) -> List.for_all (bridge_atom_in atoms) (bridge_lf_vars f))
    ineqs
in
let bridge_mk_imps sups goal =
  itlist (fun a b -> mk_imp(a,b)) (List.map concl sups) goal
in
(* remove the `+ &0' and `-- &1 *' artefacts the normalisation leaves behind;
   they are semantically inert but multiply the linear forms the prover
   builds. *)
let bridge_int_clean_rules =
  [INT_ADD_LID; INT_ADD_RID; INT_MUL_LID; INT_MUL_RID;
   INT_MUL_LZERO; INT_MUL_RZERO; INT_NEG_LMUL; INT_MUL_LNEG; INT_NEG_NEG;
   INT_NEG_0]
in
let bridge_clean_th th = REWRITE_RULE bridge_int_clean_rules th
in
(* A *deep* flattening conversion: every integer subterm is replaced by the
   canonical `sum k_i * atom_i + c' built from its linear form.  The IX.70
   residue is full of nested `B * (B * (B * a + b) + c) + d' coefficients, and
   the rational prover's monomial expansion of those is what exhausted the
   stack; the flat form `B^3 * a + B^2 * b + B * c + d' is decided in 0.2 s
   (probe `A_zero', `research/receipts/ix78-oracle-arithmetic-close.md').
   Each rewrite is proved by `INT_RING', so nothing is asserted. *)
let rec bridge_flat_conv tm =
  if type_of tm = `:int` then
    (match bridge_lf_of_term tm with
     | Some lf ->
         let flat = bridge_lf_term lf in
         if aconv flat tm then REFL tm
         else (try prove(mk_eq(tm, flat), CONV_TAC INT_RING)
               with _ -> REFL tm)
     | None -> REFL tm)
  else if is_comb tm then
    MK_COMB(bridge_flat_conv (rator tm), bridge_flat_conv (rand tm))
  else if is_abs tm then
    ABS (fst (dest_abs tm)) (bridge_flat_conv (snd (dest_abs tm)))
  else REFL tm
in
let bridge_flat_th th = CONV_RULE bridge_flat_conv th
in
let bridge_clean_tm tm =
  try snd (dest_eq (concl (REWRITE_CONV bridge_int_clean_rules tm)))
  with _ -> tm
in
let bridge_bitval_bool t =
  match t with
  | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("bitval",_), b)) -> Some b
  | _ -> None
in
(* The fallback close: case-split every *still undetermined* carry (the oracle
   has already decided the pinned ones), reduce `&(bitval b)' with
   BITVAL_CLAUSES, and let linear arithmetic see only the val atoms.  This is
   the IX.70 route done on the *reduced* system -- the oracle has already
   removed the carry whose integrality is load-bearing, and the residual is
   flat -- so the split is small and each branch is a pure value equation. *)
let bridge_split_close ants goal =
  let bools = List.fold_left (fun acc th ->
      List.fold_left (fun acc t ->
          match bridge_bitval_bool t with
          | Some b when not (List.exists (aconv b) acc) -> b :: acc
          | _ -> acc)
        acc (find_terms (fun _ -> true) (concl th))) [] ants in
  let bools = List.rev bools in
  let tac =
    EVERY (List.map (fun b ->
        ASM_CASES_TAC b THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[BITVAL_CLAUSES]) bools)
    THEN INT_ARITH_TAC in
  prove(bridge_mk_imps ants goal, tac)
in
let bridge_prove_from sups goal =
  let th = prove(bridge_mk_imps sups goal, INT_ARITH_TAC) in
  List.fold_left (fun acc h -> MP acc h) th sups
in
(* try `v = k' from the definition and the cone; returns the proof or None *)
let bridge_try_value def_th cone v k =
  let ants = def_th :: List.map (fun (th,_,_) -> th) cone in
  try
    let goal = mk_eq(v, bridge_int_lit k) in
    let th = prove(bridge_mk_imps ants goal, INT_ARITH_TAC) in
    Some(List.fold_left (fun acc h -> MP acc h) th ants)
  with _ -> None
in
(* facts for every carry that is the pivot of a definition.  The *decision*
   comes from the exact interval relaxation above; the procedure is asked only
   to *prove* a value the relaxation already pinned. *)
let bridge_val_gt b thr =
  match b with
  | Some(v,s) -> Num.lt_num thr v || (Num.eq_num v thr && s)
  | None -> false
in
let bridge_val_lt b thr =
  match b with
  | Some(v,s) -> Num.lt_num v thr || (Num.eq_num v thr && s)
  | None -> false
in
let bridge_val_le b thr =
  match b with Some(v,_) -> Num.le_num v thr | None -> false
in
let bridge_val_ge b thr =
  match b with Some(v,_) -> Num.le_num thr v | None -> false
in
(* `0', `1' or `None', from `k * v + rest = 0' and the interval relaxation *)
let bridge_carry_value tbl ineqs v form =
  let k = bridge_lf_coeff_in v form in
  if Num.eq_num k num_0 then None else
  let rest = bridge_lf_add form
               (bridge_lf_neg (bridge_lf_scale k ([ (v, num_1) ], num_0))) in
  let (lo_v, hi_v) = bridge_lookup_bound tbl v in
  let rest_lo = bridge_lo_of_neg tbl ineqs rest
  and rest_hi = bridge_hi tbl ineqs rest in
  let one = num_1 in
  if Num.lt_num num_0 k then
    (* v = -rest/k : v < 1 <=> rest > -k ; v > 0 <=> rest < 0 *)
    (if bridge_val_gt rest_lo (Num.minus_num k) && bridge_val_ge lo_v num_0
     then Some num_0
     else if bridge_val_lt rest_hi num_0 && bridge_val_le hi_v one
     then Some one else None)
  else
    (* v = rest/(-k) : v < 1 <=> rest < -k ; v > 0 <=> rest > 0 *)
    (if bridge_val_lt rest_hi (Num.minus_num k) && bridge_val_ge lo_v num_0
     then Some num_0
     else if bridge_val_gt rest_lo num_0 && bridge_val_le hi_v one
     then Some one else None)
in
let bridge_oracle_facts defs ineqs =
  let tbl = bridge_direct_bounds ineqs in
  let out = ref [] in
  List.iter (fun (v, sup, form) ->
      if bridge_is_bitval_atom v then begin
        let atoms = bridge_lf_atoms form in
        let cone = bridge_cone atoms ineqs in
        let decided = bridge_carry_value tbl ineqs v form in
        match decided with
        | None ->
            bridge_slice_note "ORACLE undetermined %s why=relaxation"
              (string_of_term v)
        | Some k ->
            let def_th = bridge_prove_from sup (bridge_lf_eq form) in
            (match bridge_try_value def_th cone v k with
             | Some th ->
                 bridge_slice_note "ORACLE fact %s = %s why=relaxation"
                   (string_of_term v) (Num.string_of_num k);
                 out := th :: !out
             | None ->
                 (* the relaxation's interval said so, but the procedure could
                    not prove it from the local cone; the *tactic* is the
                    arbiter, so the fact is not emitted. *)
                 bridge_slice_note
                   "ORACLE undetermined %s why=not-proved-from-cone"
                   (string_of_term v))
      end) defs;
  List.rev !out
in
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* 6c.2c The zero test: `word_join' and `word_or' agree on being zero.        *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* A complement routine tests its input for zero with an OR of its limbs,    *)
(* while the reference function's guard is an equality on the whole word     *)
(* built by `word_join'.  BITBLAST does not connect those two encodings       *)
(* (measured: `word_join a b = word 0 ==> word_or a b = word 0' comes back    *)
(* SATISFIABLE), so the link is made here, as a word identity valid for every *)
(* width and every pair of limbs.  The algebraic close needs the same link:  *)
(* the chain equations say `sum + n = p`, and the reference's guard says      *)
(* `n = 0'; without the fold the machine's `val(or n) != 0' branch is not     *)
(* refutable.  No curve constant occurs below.                               *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

let WORD_JOIN_EQ_0 = prove
 (`!x:M word y:N word.
     dimindex(:M) + dimindex(:N) = dimindex(:P)
     ==> (((word_join:M word->N word->P word) x y = word 0) <=>
          (x = word 0 /\ y = word 0))`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN DISCH_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN
   `val((word_join:M word->N word->P word) x y) =
    2 EXP dimindex(:N) * val(x:M word) + val(y:N word)`
  ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [MATCH_MP_TAC VAL_WORD_JOIN_SIMPLE THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[GSYM VAL_EQ_0] THEN
  ASM_REWRITE_TAC[] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[ADD_EQ_0; MULT_EQ_0; EXP_EQ_0; ARITH_EQ] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `~(2 EXP dimindex(:N) = 0)` (fun th -> REWRITE_TAC[th]) THENL
   [REWRITE_TAC[EXP_EQ_0; ARITH_EQ]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  CONV_TAC TAUT)
in
(* the same statement instantiated at the actual limb/result widths, so the
   width side condition is discharged here and the rewrite needs no subgoal *)
let BRIDGE_JOIN_ZERO_CONV : conv =
  let conv tm =
    let (l,r) = dest_eq tm in
    let (j,args) = strip_comb l in
    if name_of j <> "word_join" || List.length args <> 2 then
      failwith "BRIDGE_JOIN_ZERO_CONV: not a join equation" else
    let x = List.nth args 0 and y = List.nth args 1 in
    (match r with
       Comb(Const("word",_),n) when n = `0` -> ()
     | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_JOIN_ZERO_CONV: right side is not `word 0'");
    let mx = bridge_word_width (type_of x)
    and my = bridge_word_width (type_of y)
    and mp = bridge_word_width (type_of l) in
    let inst = INST_TYPE
      [bridge_finty mx, `:M`; bridge_finty my, `:N`; bridge_finty mp, `:P`]
      WORD_JOIN_EQ_0 in
    let th = SPECL [x;y] inst in
    let side = lhand(concl th) in
    let side_th = prove(side,
      CONV_TAC(LAND_CONV(BINOP_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_ADD_CONV) THENC
               RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV THENC NUM_EQ_CONV)) in
    MP th side_th in
  conv
in
(* fold both zero tests to a conjunction of limb-wise `= word 0', in the goal
   and in the hypotheses *)
let BRIDGE_ZERO_TEST_TAC : tactic = fun (asl,w) ->
  (RULE_ASSUM_TAC(REWRITE_RULE[WORD_OR_EQ_0]) THEN
   REWRITE_TAC[WORD_OR_EQ_0] THEN
   RULE_ASSUM_TAC(CONV_RULE (TOP_DEPTH_CONV BRIDGE_JOIN_ZERO_CONV)) THEN
   CONV_TAC(TOP_DEPTH_CONV BRIDGE_JOIN_ZERO_CONV) THEN
   RULE_ASSUM_TAC(REWRITE_RULE[CONJ_ACI]) THEN
   REWRITE_TAC[CONJ_ACI]) (asl,w)
in
(* The algebraic close needs the same fold *plus* the val-level OR form (the
   accumulator hands the select condition as `val(or ...) <> 0') and the
   reduction of zero tests over already-substituted `word 0' limbs, so the
   impossible select branch becomes `F'.  Separate from the SAT fold above so
   the shipped x86 neg route is byte-for-byte the tactic it had. *)
(* The algebraic close meets the machine's zero test in *integer* form
   (`&(val(word_or ...)) = &0') only after the normalisation, so the OR fold is
   done there, by a rewrite that is exact on the actual type.  Applied to the
   goal and every hypothesis; a term with no OR is untouched. *)
let INT_VAL_WORD_OR_EQ_0 = prove
 (`!x:N word y:N word.
     (int_of_num(val(word_or x y)) = &0) <=>
     (int_of_num(val x) = &0 /\ int_of_num(val y) = &0)`,
  REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_EQ; VAL_WORD_OR_EQ_0])
in
let BRIDGE_INT_OR_ZERO_CONV : conv =
  GEN_REWRITE_CONV TOP_DEPTH_CONV [INT_VAL_WORD_OR_EQ_0]
in
let BRIDGE_ZERO_FOLD_TAC : tactic = fun (asl,w) ->
  (RULE_ASSUM_TAC(REWRITE_RULE[INT_SUB_RZERO]) THEN
   REWRITE_TAC[INT_SUB_RZERO] THEN
   RULE_ASSUM_TAC(CONV_RULE BRIDGE_INT_OR_ZERO_CONV) THEN
   CONV_TAC BRIDGE_INT_OR_ZERO_CONV) (asl,w)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.3c Aggregate, don't eliminate (XIX.C1).                                 *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* IX.78 measured the exact defect: eliminating every internal carry by      *)
(* Gauss-Jordan destroys the chain aggregate because the top carry becomes a *)
(* pivot with a `B^n' coefficient (`c8'-type definitions carrying            *)
(* `2^256 * &(bitval carry_s8)'), and `INT_ARITH' then either omits the raw  *)
(* relation `M + N = W + B^n * c_n' or blows up.  The human proof never       *)
(* eliminates: `GEN_DECARRY_RULE'/`DECARRY_RULE' sum the per-limb equations  *)
(* with the digit weights, and the internal carries cancel by construction.   *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* That is done here, exactly, with integer weights.  Nothing is solved for:  *)
(* the weights ARE the digit positions, and they are recovered from the       *)
(* theorem's own equations, not from a per-curve template:                    *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   - a *limb equation* is an integer equation carrying at least one         *)
(*     `&(bitval c)' atom and at least one atom that is not a carry;          *)
(*   - two limb equations are *linked* when they share a carry atom; the link  *)
(*     points from the equation where that atom has coefficient magnitude     *)
(*     `B > 1' (the outgoing carry of a limb) to the equation where it has    *)
(*     magnitude `1' (the incoming carry of the next limb);                   *)
(*   - a chain is a connected component that is a directed path, rooted at    *)
(*     its in-degree-zero equation; its weight list is `1, B, B^2, ...';      *)
(*   - the aggregate is the weighted sum of the equations, so the internal     *)
(*     carries cancel and only the raw sum, the written sum and the top carry *)
(*     survive.                                                               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* `B', the number of limbs and the weights therefore come from the term      *)
(* structure of this theorem's hypotheses.  If the structure is not a set of  *)
(* disjoint `(outgoing B, incoming 1)' paths, no aggregate is emitted and the *)
(* close behaves exactly as it did in IX.78 -- no regression.                 *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The combination is built as a *proof*: each premise is flattened, scaled    *)
(* by `AP_TERM (( * ) w)', and the equations are added by `MK_COMB'.  The sum  *)
(* is then normalised to the canonical flat form by `INT_RING', which is a    *)
(* ring identity, not a search.  The integer weights are the certificate      *)
(* XIX.D1 asks for, and are printed in phase mode.                            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_eq_scale th k =
  if Num.eq_num k num_1 then th
  else AP_TERM (mk_comb(bridge_int_mul_tm, bridge_int_lit k)) th
in
let bridge_eq_add th1 th2 =
  MK_COMB(AP_TERM bridge_int_add_tm th1, th2)
in
(* carry atoms with a non-zero coefficient *)
let bridge_carry_coeffs form =
  List.filter (fun (t,k) -> bridge_is_bitval_atom t && not (Num.eq_num k num_0))
    (fst form)
in
let bridge_limb_equation form =
  let (xs,_) = form in
  bridge_carry_coeffs form <> [] &&
  List.exists (fun (t,_) -> not (bridge_is_bitval_atom t)) xs
in
(* one edge per carry atom shared by exactly two limb equations, from the
   larger coefficient magnitude to the smaller; any ambiguous sharing makes
   the whole structure unusable (`false') rather than guessed at. *)
let bridge_chain_edges forms =
  let n = Array.length forms in
  let occs = ref [] in
  for i = 0 to n - 1 do
    List.iter (fun (t,_) -> occs := (t,i) :: !occs) (bridge_carry_coeffs forms.(i))
  done;
  let edges = ref [] and clean = ref true in
  List.iter (fun (t,_) ->
      let occ = List.filter (fun (u,_) -> aconv u t) !occs in
      match occ with
      | [_] -> ()   (* an end-of-chain carry (top outgoing, or carry-in): no link *)
      | [(_,i); (_,j)] when i <> j ->
          (let ki = bridge_lf_coeff_in t forms.(i)
           and kj = bridge_lf_coeff_in t forms.(j) in
           let ai = Num.abs_num ki and aj = Num.abs_num kj in
           (* the signs must be opposite: that is what cancels *)
           if Num.lt_num num_0 (Num.mult_num ki kj) then clean := false
           else if Num.eq_num ai aj then clean := false
           else if Num.lt_num ai aj then
             edges := (j,i) :: !edges
           else edges := (i,j) :: !edges)
      | _ ->
          bridge_slice_note "AGGREGATE link %s occ=%d"
            (string_of_term t) (List.length occ);
          clean := false) !occs;
  let uniq = List.fold_left (fun a e -> if List.mem e a then a else e :: a) [] !edges in
  (List.rev uniq, !clean)
in
(* the ordered path through one component, or `None' *)
let bridge_chain_path comp edges =
  let out_deg i = List.length (List.filter (fun (a,_) -> a = i) edges)
  and in_deg i = List.length (List.filter (fun (_,b) -> b = i) edges) in
  let roots = List.filter (fun i -> in_deg i = 0) comp in
  match roots with
  | [r] ->
      if List.exists (fun i -> out_deg i > 1 || in_deg i > 1) comp then None
      else if List.length edges <> List.length comp - 1 then None
      else
        (let rec go acc i =
           if out_deg i = 0 then List.rev (i :: acc)
           else
             (match List.find_opt (fun (a,_) -> a = i) edges with
              | Some (_,j) -> go (i :: acc) j
              | None -> List.rev (i :: acc)) in
         Some (go [] r))
  | _ -> None
in
(* the shared carry atom of two linked equations and the limb base, or None *)
let bridge_chain_link form1 form2 =
  let shared = List.find_opt (fun (t,_) ->
      bridge_is_bitval_atom t &&
      not (Num.eq_num (bridge_lf_coeff_in t form2) num_0))
    (bridge_carry_coeffs form1) in
  match shared with
  | None -> None
  | Some (t,_) ->
      let k1 = bridge_lf_coeff_in t form1 and k2 = bridge_lf_coeff_in t form2 in
      let a1 = Num.abs_num k1 and a2 = Num.abs_num k2 in
      if Num.le_num a1 num_1 || not (Num.eq_num a2 num_1) then None
      else Some (a1)
in
(* weights `1, B, B^2, ...' for a path, or `None' if the base is not a single
   value shared by every link *)
let bridge_chain_weights forms path =
  let rec go acc prev = function
    | [] -> Some (List.rev acc)
    | i::rest ->
        (match prev with
         | None -> go ((i, num_1) :: acc) (Some i) rest
         | Some p ->
             (match bridge_chain_link forms.(p) forms.(i) with
              | None -> None
              | Some b ->
                  let w = Num.mult_num b (List.assoc p acc) in
                  go ((i, w) :: acc) (Some i) rest)) in
  go [] None path
in
(* proof of the weighted sum, normalised to the flat canonical form *)
let bridge_chain_aggregate chain =
  let scaled = List.map (fun (n,w) -> (w, bridge_flat_th n)) chain in
  match scaled with
  | [] -> None
  | (w0,th0)::rest ->
      (try
         let folded =
           List.fold_left (fun acc (w,th) ->
               bridge_eq_add acc (bridge_eq_scale th w))
             (bridge_eq_scale th0 w0) rest in
         let comb = List.fold_left (fun acc (w,th) ->
             match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
             | Some f -> bridge_lf_add acc (bridge_lf_scale w f)
             | None -> failwith "premise is not linear") ([], num_0) scaled in
         let target = bridge_lf_eq comb in
         let l' = lhand target and r' = rand target in
         let l = lhand (concl folded) and r = rand (concl folded) in
         (* folded is `l = r'.  The canonical form is obtained by *difference*:
            `INT_RING' proves `l - r = l' - r'' (a polynomial identity), and
            `l - r = 0', `l' - r' = 0' is the same equation.  No search. *)
         let sub = `(-):int->int->int` in
         let th_ring =
           prove(mk_eq(mk_binop sub l r, mk_binop sub l' r'),
                 CONV_TAC INT_RING) in
         let sub_refl =
           prove(mk_eq(mk_binop sub r r, bridge_int_lit num_0),
                 REWRITE_TAC[INT_SUB_REFL]) in
         let th_lr =
           TRANS (AP_THM (AP_TERM sub folded) r) sub_refl in
         let th_ld = TRANS (SYM th_ring) th_lr in
         let th_res =
           EQ_MP (ISPECL [l'; r'; bridge_int_lit num_0] INT_EQ_SUB_RADD) th_ld in
         Some (REWRITE_RULE[INT_ADD_LID] th_res)
       with e ->
         bridge_slice_note "AGGREGATE dropped: %s" (Printexc.to_string e);
         None)
in
(* every aggregate this theorem's equations support.  Each result is the
   proved equation; the weights and premise count are printed with it. *)
let bridge_aggregates eqs =
  let limbs = List.filter (fun (_,f) -> bridge_limb_equation f) eqs in
  let arr = Array.of_list limbs in
  let forms = Array.map snd arr in
  let n = Array.length arr in
  if n < 2 then [] else
  let (edges, clean) = bridge_chain_edges forms in
  if not clean then begin
    bridge_slice_note "AGGREGATE none: carry links are not disjoint paths";
    []
  end else
  let parent = Array.init n (fun i -> i) in
  let rec root i =
    if parent.(i) = i then i
    else (let r = root parent.(i) in parent.(i) <- r; r) in
  List.iter (fun (i,j) ->
      let ri = root i and rj = root j in
      if ri <> rj then parent.(ri) <- rj) edges;
  let nodes = List.init n (fun i -> i) in
  let rec group acc = function
    | [] -> List.rev acc
    | x::xs ->
        let r = root x in
        let same, rest = List.partition (fun y -> root y = r) xs in
        group ((x :: same) :: acc) rest in
  let comps = group [] nodes in
  List.filter_map (fun comp ->
      let cedges = List.filter (fun (i,j) -> List.mem i comp && List.mem j comp) edges in
      match bridge_chain_path comp cedges with
      | None -> None
      | Some path ->
          (match bridge_chain_weights forms path with
           | None -> None
           | Some wpath ->
               (match bridge_chain_aggregate
                        (List.map (fun (i,w) -> (fst arr.(i), w)) wpath) with
                | None -> None
                | Some th ->
                    let b = if List.length wpath > 1
                            then List.assoc (List.nth path 1) wpath else num_0 in
                    bridge_slice_note
                      "AGGREGATE limbs=%d base=%s weights=[%s] premises=%d conclusion=%s"
                      (List.length path) (Num.string_of_num b)
                      (String.concat ","
                         (List.map (fun (_,w) -> Num.string_of_num w) wpath))
                      (List.length wpath) (string_of_term (concl th));
                    Some th))) comps
in
(* An integer equation that carries no `&(bitval c)' atom is not a limb of a
   carry chain: it is a *branch fact* such as a folded zero test
   (`val(join n) = 0') or the top-bit mask relation.  Such facts are not
   premises of any aggregate, so the aggregate sum does not state them and the
   close must keep them.  The chain rows themselves stay out (that is what the
   aggregate replaces; keeping both multiplies the prover's elimination). *)
let bridge_int_eq_has_carry th =
  match concl th with
  | Comb(Comb(Const("=",_),a),_) when type_of a = `:int` ->
      (match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
       | Some f -> List.exists bridge_is_bitval_atom (bridge_lf_vars f)
       | None -> true)
  | _ -> false
in
(* the top carry of a chain is decided by its aggregate, not by eliminating   *)
(* the chain: the aggregate is `M + N = W + B^n * c', `INT_ARITH' encodes     *)
(* integer discreteness through `INT_NOT_EQ', so `c = 0' follows from         *)
(* `M + N < B^n', `W >= 0' and `0 <= c <= 1'.  The fact is *proved*, and the  *)
(* premises are the aggregate and the same integer hypotheses as before.     *)
(* The carriers are the `&(bitval c)' atoms the aggregates mention; when an   *)
(* aggregate mentions more than one, only some of them are decided by the    *)
(* global context (the rest are branch facts).                               *)
let bridge_aggregate_carriers aggregates =
  List.fold_left (fun acc th ->
      match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
      | Some f ->
          List.fold_left (fun a t ->
              if bridge_is_bitval_atom t &&
                 not (List.exists (fun (u,_) -> aconv u t) a)
              then a @ [(t, th)] else a) acc (bridge_lf_vars f)
      | None -> acc) [] aggregates
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.3b The carry-bound certificate (XXIX.B).                                *)
(*                                                                            *)
(* The aggregate is `A + K*c = 0' with `c' the top carry and `K' its          *)
(* coefficient.  The fact the close needs is `c = 0', and it follows from the *)
(* *bounds already in scope*, not from another arithmetic search:             *)
(*                                                                            *)
(*   K*c = -A.  Every atom of `A' is bounded (`&(val w) < 2^dimindex',        *)
(*   `&0 <= &(val w)', `&0 <= &(bitval b) <= &1'), and a weighted modulus     *)
(*   bound `N <= p' bounds one whole group.  If the interval bound on `K*c'   *)
(*   lies strictly on the side that rules out `c >= 1', then `c = 0':         *)
(*                                                                            *)
(*       c >= 1 ==> (K < 0  =>  K*c <= K)  and  (K > 0  =>  K*c >= K),        *)
(*                                                                            *)
(*   so an upper bound `K*c < K' (K > 0) or a lower bound `K*c > K' (K < 0)  *)
(*   closes it.  The bound is computed with exact `Num' arithmetic, so a      *)
(*   shape or value mismatch costs no inference.                              *)
(*                                                                            *)
(* Nothing here is width- or limb-specific: `B' and `n' are derived from the  *)
(* coefficient multiset of the aggregate itself (the smallest magnitude > 1   *)
(* is the limb base `B', every magnitude is a power of it, and `|K| = B^n').  *)
(* A second aggregate that shares atoms with the carrier row is used when the *)
(* bound needs it (`add'/`sub' carry a raw and a corrected aggregate); the    *)
(* elimination is an exact integer combination, so the certificate remains a  *)
(* certificate and not a solver trace.  The final proof is a kernel-checked   *)
(* `INT_ARITH' over only the equations that combination used, the bound       *)
(* hypotheses it read, and `&0 <= c'; the caller keeps the band/fact fallback *)
(* unchanged when the shape does not match or the certificate fails.          *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* a one-atom integer hypothesis, as `k*x + c REL 0' with `REL' `>=' or `>' *)
let bridge_cert_atom_ineq th =
  match concl th with
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b) when type_of a = `:int` ->
      (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
       | Some x, Some y ->
           let f = bridge_lf_add y (bridge_lf_neg x) in
           (match fst f with
            | [(u,k)] when not (Num.eq_num k num_0) -> Some (u,k,snd f,false)
            | _ -> None)
       | _ -> None)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) when type_of a = `:int` ->
      (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
       | Some x, Some y ->
           let f = bridge_lf_add y (bridge_lf_neg x) in
           (match fst f with
            | [(u,k)] when not (Num.eq_num k num_0) -> Some (u,k,snd f,true)
            | _ -> None)
       | _ -> None)
  | _ -> None
in
(* `(atom, lower bound, upper bound)' where each bound is `(value, strict, thm)'
   and means `x > value' / `x >= value' (lower) or `x < value' / `x <= value'
   (upper).  Exact division only: anything else yields no bound and the caller
   falls back. *)
let bridge_cert_bound th =
  match bridge_cert_atom_ineq th with
  | Some (u,k,c,strict) when Num.lt_num num_0 k ->
      let q = Num.div_num (Num.minus_num c) k in
      if Num.eq_num (Num.mult_num q k) (Num.minus_num c)
      then Some (u, Some ((if strict then Num.add_num q num_1 else q),
                          false, th), None)
      else None
  | Some (u,k,c,strict) ->
      let ak = Num.abs_num k in
      let q = Num.div_num c ak in
      if Num.eq_num (Num.mult_num q ak) c
      then Some (u, None, Some ((if strict then Num.sub_num q num_1 else q),
                                false, th))
      else None
  | None -> None
in
let bridge_cert_join_lo a b =
  match a,b with
  | None,x | x,None -> x
  | Some(v1,s1,_),Some(v2,s2,_) ->
      if Num.lt_num v1 v2 then a
      else if Num.lt_num v2 v1 then b
      else if s1 then a else b
in
let bridge_cert_join_hi a b =
  match a,b with
  | None,x | x,None -> x
  | Some(v1,s1,_),Some(v2,s2,_) ->
      if Num.lt_num v1 v2 then a
      else if Num.lt_num v2 v1 then b
      else if s1 then a else b
in
let bridge_cert_add tbl u lo hi =
  let (lo0,hi0) = try List.assoc u tbl with Not_found -> (None,None) in
  (u, (bridge_cert_join_lo lo0 lo, bridge_cert_join_hi hi0 hi))
  :: List.remove_assoc u tbl
in
(* the contribution of `k*x' to (lo,hi): increasing for k>0, decreasing for
   k<0, so the two endpoint bounds swap. *)
let bridge_cert_scaled k (l,h) =
  let scale bnd = match bnd with
    | None -> None
    | Some(v,s,th) -> Some(Num.mult_num k v, s, th) in
  if Num.lt_num num_0 k then (scale l, scale h) else (scale h, scale l)
in
(* bounds of `sum k_i*x_i + c', with the hypotheses that establish each
   endpoint kept apart so only the queried direction travels to the proof. *)
let bridge_cert_form_bounds tbl form =
  let (xs,c) = form in
  let (lo,lps,hi,hps) =
    List.fold_left (fun (lo,lps,hi,hps) (t,k) ->
        let (l,h) = try List.assoc t tbl with Not_found -> (None,None) in
        let (cl,ch) = bridge_cert_scaled k (l,h) in
        let addl acc bnd = match acc,bnd with
          | None,_ | _,None -> None
          | Some(v0,s0),Some(v,s,_) -> Some(Num.add_num v0 v, s0 || s) in
        let plo = match cl with Some(_,_,th) -> [th] | None -> [] in
        let phi = match ch with Some(_,_,th) -> [th] | None -> [] in
        (addl lo cl, plo @ lps, addl hi ch, phi @ hps))
      (Some(c,false), [], Some(c,false), []) xs in
  (lo,lps,hi,hps)
in
(* one relational hypothesis, rewritten as an upper bound of a *rest* form:
   `target = alpha*f + rest' with `alpha < 0' and `f >= 0' (or `> 0'), so
   `target <= rest'.  Mirrors `bridge_rel_hi'. *)
let bridge_cert_rel_hi tbl target (th,f,strict) =
  ignore th; ignore strict;
  let (txs,_) = target and (fxs,_) = f in
  let shared = List.filter (fun (x,_) ->
      List.exists (fun (y,_) -> aconv x y) txs) fxs in
  match shared with
  | [] -> None
  | (x0,_)::_ ->
      let k0 = bridge_lf_coeff x0 txs and kf = bridge_lf_coeff x0 fxs in
      if Num.eq_num kf num_0 then None else
      let alpha = Num.div_num k0 kf in
      let prop = List.for_all (fun (x,_) ->
          Num.eq_num (bridge_lf_coeff x txs)
                     (Num.mult_num alpha (bridge_lf_coeff x fxs))) shared in
      if not prop || not (Num.lt_num alpha num_0) then None else
      Some (bridge_lf_add target (bridge_lf_neg (bridge_lf_scale alpha f)))
in
(* the tightest upper bound over the per-atom table and every *combination*
   of relational hypotheses: each application bounds one weighted group
   (`N < p' then `M < p'), and the recursion is what lets `add' retire the
   top carry before the split, where the two modulus bounds are separate
   hypotheses and no single one suffices.  `(value, premises)'. *)
let rec bridge_cert_hi depth tbl rels target =
  let (_,_,hi0,pr0) = bridge_cert_form_bounds tbl target in
  let best0 = match hi0 with Some(v,_) -> Some(v,pr0) | None -> None in
  if depth <= 0 then best0 else
  List.fold_left (fun acc (th,f,strict) ->
      match bridge_cert_rel_hi tbl target (th,f,strict) with
      | None -> acc
      | Some rest ->
          let inner = bridge_cert_hi (depth - 1) tbl
              (List.filter (fun (u,_,_) ->
                   not (aconv (concl u) (concl th))) rels) rest in
          (match inner with
           | None -> acc
           | Some(v,pr) ->
               let v = if strict then Num.sub_num v num_1 else v in
               (match acc with
                | None -> Some(v, th :: pr)
                | Some(v0,_) ->
                    if Num.lt_num v v0 then Some(v, th :: pr) else acc)))
    best0 rels
in
let bridge_cert_lo depth tbl rels target =
  match bridge_cert_hi depth tbl rels (bridge_lf_neg target) with
  | None -> None
  | Some(v,pr) -> Some(Num.minus_num v, pr)
in
let bridge_cert_uniq ths =
  List.rev (List.fold_left (fun acc th ->
      if List.exists (fun u -> aconv (concl u) (concl th)) acc then acc
      else th :: acc) [] ths)
in
(* `row' = kjx * row - kx * rowj' cancels atom `x'; every weight is an
   integer, so the combination is an exact equation and not a relaxation. *)
let bridge_cert_elim (combo,row) (thj,rowj) x =
  let kx = bridge_lf_coeff_in x row and kjx = bridge_lf_coeff_in x rowj in
  if Num.eq_num kjx num_0 then None else
  let row' = bridge_lf_add (bridge_lf_scale kjx row)
                           (bridge_lf_scale (Num.minus_num kx) rowj) in
  let combo' = List.map (fun (th,w) -> (th, Num.mult_num kjx w)) combo
               @ [(thj, Num.minus_num kx)] in
  Some (combo', row')
in
(* `(B, n)' from the coefficient multiset of the carrier row, or `None' when
   the magnitudes are not the geometric limb weights (the shape does not
   match, and the caller keeps the old route). *)
let bridge_cert_shape v row =
  let k = bridge_lf_coeff_in v row in
  let mags = List.map (fun (_,c) -> Num.abs_num c) (fst row) in
  let big = List.filter (fun x -> Num.lt_num num_1 x) mags in
  match big with
  | [] -> None
  | b0::rest ->
      let b = List.fold_left (fun a x -> if Num.lt_num x a then x else a) b0 rest in
      let km = Num.abs_num k in
      let rec pow p n =
        if Num.lt_num km p then None
        else if Num.eq_num km p then Some n
        else pow (Num.mult_num p b) (n + 1) in
      (match pow b 1 with
       | None -> None
       | Some n ->
           let rec ispow x =
             if Num.eq_num x num_1 then true
             else if Num.lt_num num_1 x && Num.eq_num (Num.mod_num x b) num_0
             then ispow (Num.div_num x b)
             else false in
           if n > 1 && List.for_all ispow mags then Some (b,n) else None)
in
let bridge_carry_certificate aggregates all_hyps v =
  try
    let rows = List.filter_map (fun th ->
        match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
        | Some f -> Some (th,f) | None -> None) aggregates in
    let carriers = List.filter (fun (_,f) ->
        not (Num.eq_num (bridge_lf_coeff_in v f) num_0)) rows in
    match carriers with
    | [(th0,row0)] ->
        (match bridge_cert_shape v row0 with
         | None -> None
         | Some (base,limbs) ->
             let tbl = List.fold_left (fun tbl th ->
                 match bridge_cert_bound th with
                 | Some (u,lo,hi) -> bridge_cert_add tbl u lo hi
                 | None -> tbl) [] all_hyps in
             let rels = List.filter_map (fun th ->
                 match concl th with
