                 | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b) when type_of a = `:int` ->
                     (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
                      | Some x, Some y ->
                          let f = bridge_lf_add y (bridge_lf_neg x) in
                          if List.length (fst f) > 1
                          then Some (th,f,false) else None
                      | _ -> None)
                 | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) when type_of a = `:int` ->
                     (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
                      | Some x, Some y ->
                          let f = bridge_lf_add y (bridge_lf_neg x) in
                          if List.length (fst f) > 1
                          then Some (th,f,true) else None
                      | _ -> None)
                 | _ -> None) all_hyps in
             let nonneg =
               try match List.assoc v tbl with
                 | (Some (_,_,th), _) -> th
                 | _ -> BRIDGE_BOUND_NONNEG v
               with Not_found -> BRIDGE_BOUND_NONNEG v in
             let trial (combo,row) =
               let k = bridge_lf_coeff_in v row in
               let bn = Num.abs_num k in
               if Num.le_num bn num_1 then None else
               let a = (List.filter (fun (t,_) -> not (aconv t v)) (fst row),
                        snd row) in
               let s = bridge_lf_neg a in
               let ok =
                 if Num.lt_num k num_0 then
                   (match bridge_cert_lo 3 tbl rels s with
                    | Some(u,pr) ->
                        if Num.lt_num (Num.minus_num bn) u then Some pr else None
                    | None -> None)
                 else
                   (match bridge_cert_hi 3 tbl rels s with
                    | Some(u,pr) ->
                        if Num.lt_num u bn then Some pr else None
                    | None -> None) in
               match ok with
               | None -> None
               | Some pr -> Some (List.map fst combo, pr) in
             let rec search depth st =
               match trial st with
               | Some r -> Some r
               | None when depth = 0 -> None
               | None ->
                   let (combo,row) = st in
                   let atoms = List.filter_map (fun (t,_) ->
                       if aconv t v then None else Some t) (fst row) in
                   let others = List.filter (fun (th,_) ->
                       not (List.exists (fun u ->
                           aconv (concl u) (concl th)) (List.map fst combo))) rows in
                   let rec try_atoms = function
                     | [] -> None
                     | x::xs ->
                         let rec try_rows = function
                           | [] -> try_atoms xs
                           | (thj,rowj)::rest ->
                               (match bridge_cert_elim (combo,row) (thj,rowj) x with
                                | None -> try_rows rest
                                | Some st' ->
                                    (match search (depth - 1) st' with
                                     | Some r -> Some r
                                     | None -> try_rows rest)) in
                         try_rows others in
                   try_atoms atoms in
             (match search 2 ([th0, num_1], row0) with
              | None -> None
              | Some (eqs,pr) ->
                  let prems = bridge_cert_uniq (eqs @ pr @ [nonneg]) in
                  let goal = mk_eq(v, bridge_int_lit num_0) in
                  let th = prove(bridge_mk_imps prems goal, INT_ARITH_TAC) in
                  let th = List.fold_left (fun acc h -> MP acc h) th prems in
                  bridge_slice_note
                    "ORACLE carry-cert %s = 0 base=%s limbs=%d premises=%d"
                    (string_of_term v) (Num.string_of_num base) limbs
                    (List.length prems);
                  Some th))
    | _ -> None
  with e ->
    bridge_slice_note "ORACLE carry-cert %s failed: %s"
      (string_of_term v) (Printexc.to_string e);
    None
in
let bridge_aggregate_facts ?(band_only=false) aggregates all_hyps =
  (* a top-level disjunction cannot be an antecedent of a linear-arithmetic
     goal (the prover would have to case-split); the branch splitter has
     already produced the conjunctive branches, so one is dropped here.  The
     per-limb equations are dropped too: the aggregate already states their
     sum, and keeping both multiplies the prover's elimination steps. *)
  let is_int_eq th =
    match concl th with
    | Comb(Comb(Const("=",_),a),b) -> type_of a = `:int`
    | _ -> false in
  let conjunctive th =
    match concl th with
    | Comb(Comb(Const("\\/",_),_),_) -> false
    | _ -> true in
  let side_hyps =
    List.filter
      (fun th -> conjunctive th &&
                 (not (is_int_eq th) || not (bridge_int_eq_has_carry th)))
      all_hyps in
  (* `&(bitval b)' is a natural number, so `< &1' is `= &0'.  The `bitval'
     case split is what supplies the two possible values; the strict bound
     itself is proved by linear arithmetic from the aggregate. *)
  let lt_tm = `int_lt` in
  let carriers = bridge_aggregate_carriers aggregates in
  bridge_slice_note "ORACLE aggregate-carriers=%d [%s]"
    (List.length carriers)
    (String.concat "," (List.map (fun (v,_) -> string_of_term v) carriers));
  (* XXIII.B1: a carrier's fact is implied by the aggregate(s) that mention it;
     the rest are logically inert.  IX.86 measured 477,376 inferences on `add'
     (93.2% of the 512,129 regression) from handing one inert aggregate to this
     proof.  `sub''s correction borrow is decided by both the raw and the
     corrected aggregate, so a failed fast path retries the full list and the
     result is unchanged whenever the fast path is wrong. *)
  let aggs_mentioning v =
    List.filter (fun th ->
        match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
        | Some f -> List.exists (fun t -> aconv t v) (bridge_lf_vars f)
        | None -> false) aggregates in
  let premise_sets v =
    let local = aggs_mentioning v in
    if local = [] || List.length local >= List.length aggregates then
      [aggregates @ side_hyps]
    else [local @ side_hyps; aggregates @ side_hyps] in
  (* XXVIII.C5: a fact with the same conclusion may already be an antecedent.
     The pre-split hoist (`BRIDGE_HOIST_AGG_FACTS_TAC`) assumes the branch-
     independent facts, so every branch inherits them; re-proving one is pure
     repetition (measured: 1,511,696 inferences on `neg', XXVIII.C4).  The
     match is `aconv' on the equation `v = &0' / `v = &1' and only against a
     hypothesis already in scope, so reusing it assumes nothing new.  No match
     is the old behaviour: the per-branch proof below still runs. *)
  let assumed v =
    List.find_opt (fun th ->
        match concl th with
        | Comb(Comb(Const("=",_),a),b) when type_of a = `:int` ->
            aconv a v &&
            (aconv b (bridge_int_lit num_0) ||
             aconv b (bridge_int_lit num_1))
        | _ -> false) all_hyps in
  let prove_zero_lt v =
    let attempt premises =
      let th = prove(bridge_mk_imps premises
                       (mk_binop lt_tm v (bridge_int_lit num_1)),
                     INT_ARITH_TAC) in
      let th = List.fold_left (fun acc h -> MP acc h) th premises in
      let b = rand (rand v) in
      let th2 = prove(mk_imp (concl th, mk_eq(v, bridge_int_lit num_0)),
                      ASM_CASES_TAC b THEN
                      ASM_REWRITE_TAC[BITVAL_CLAUSES] THEN
                      CONV_TAC INT_REDUCE_CONV) in
      MP th2 th in
    let rec go = function
      | [] -> None
      | p :: rest ->
          (try Some (attempt p)
           with e ->
             bridge_slice_note "ORACLE agg-band %s failed (%d premises): %s"
               (string_of_term v) (List.length p) (Printexc.to_string e);
             go rest) in
    go (premise_sets v) in
  let prove_fact v k =
    let attempt premises =
      let th = prove(bridge_mk_imps premises (mk_eq(v, bridge_int_lit k)),
                     INT_ARITH_TAC) in
      List.fold_left (fun acc h -> MP acc h) th premises in
    let rec go = function
      | [] -> None
      | p :: rest -> (try Some (attempt p) with _ -> go rest) in
    go (premise_sets v) in
  List.filter_map (fun carrier ->
      let v = fst carrier in
      match assumed v with
      | Some th ->
          bridge_slice_note "ORACLE fact %s reused why=antecedent"
            (string_of_term v);
          Some th
      | None ->
      (match bridge_carry_certificate aggregates all_hyps v with
       | Some th ->
           bridge_slice_note "ORACLE fact %s = 0 why=carry-cert"
             (string_of_term v);
           Some th
       | None ->
      match prove_zero_lt v with
      | Some th ->
          bridge_slice_note "ORACLE fact %s = 0 why=aggregate-band"
            (string_of_term v);
          Some th
      | None ->
          (* `band_only': the pre-split hoist uses this.  A carrier the
             aggregate-band route cannot decide is left to the per-branch
             proof; the `v = 0' / `v = 1' searches are kept for the oracle
             fallback, where they are measured to be the cheap route in the
             branches that need them. *)
          if band_only then None else
          (match prove_fact v num_0 with
           | Some th ->
               bridge_slice_note "ORACLE fact %s = 0 why=aggregate"
                 (string_of_term v);
               Some th
           | None ->
               (match prove_fact v num_1 with
                | Some th ->
                    bridge_slice_note "ORACLE fact %s = 1 why=aggregate"
                      (string_of_term v);
                    Some th
                | None ->
                    bridge_slice_note "ORACLE undetermined %s why=aggregate"
                      (string_of_term v);
                    None)))) carriers
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.4 The close.                                                            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_int_hyps asl =
  List.filter (fun (_,th) ->
      let t = concl th in
      List.exists (fun u -> match u with
          | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_),_) -> true | _ -> false)
        (find_terms (fun _ -> true) t)) asl
in
(* XXVIII.C5: hoist the branch-independent part of the aggregate fact phase.

   `BRIDGE_ORACLE_TAC' builds the chain aggregate and decides each carry from
   the aggregate and the integer hypotheses in scope.  A conditional split only
   *adds* hypotheses, and the chain equations are present before the split, so a
   fact proved there from the global context holds in every branch; the
   measured cost of proving it per branch was 1,511,696 inferences on
   `arm.bignum_neg_p25519' (XXVIII.C4), the same `&(bitval carry_s12) = &0'
   ten times.

   The tactic runs at each `BRIDGE_ALGEBRA_TAC' entry, after the first
   normalisation and before `BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_KEEP_TAC'.  The entry route
   `BRIDGE_FINISH_KEEP_ALG_TAC' splits on the written-value conditions *before*
   the expansion, so the algebra tactic is entered once per pre-split goal (four
   on `neg'; the fact is therefore proved four times, not ten).  The range bounds
   that `BRIDGE_ATOM_BOUNDS_TAC' would supply run after the split, so they are
   *constructed* here as closed theorems: proving a bound on `&(val w)' or
   `&(bitval b)' needs no hypothesis.

   Each fact it proves is *assumed*, so every branch inherits it and
   `BRIDGE_ORACLE_TAC' reuses it (see `assumed' in `bridge_aggregate_facts')
   instead of proving it again.  The hoist is limited to the single-carrier case
   and to the aggregate-band route: attempting a carrier the global context
   leaves undecided costs more than the per-branch proofs it replaces (measured
   on `add' and `sub').  If no aggregate is found, nothing is decided, or
   anything raises, the goal is returned unchanged: the per-branch proof remains
   the fallback and current behaviour is preserved.  A hoisted fact is proved
   before any branch assumption exists, so reusing it assumes nothing a branch
   does not already carry, and the kernel checks every step. *)
let BRIDGE_HOIST_AGG_FACTS_TAC : tactic =
  fun (asl,w) ->
    try
      let eqs = List.filter_map (fun (_,th) ->
          match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
          | Some f -> Some (th,f) | None -> None) asl in
      let aggs = bridge_aggregates eqs in
      let carriers = bridge_aggregate_carriers aggs in
      (* Only the single-carrier (final-carry) case is hoisted.  With two
         carriers the second one is left undecided by the global context and
         the failed band/`v = k' attempts cost more than the per-branch proofs
         they replace (measured on `arm.bignum_add_p25519': +488528
         inferences).  A skip is exactly the old route. *)
      if List.length carriers <> 1 then begin
        bridge_slice_note "HOIST skip eqs=%d aggregates=%d carriers=%d"
          (List.length eqs) (List.length aggs) (List.length carriers);
        ALL_TAC (asl,w)
      end else
      let hyps =
        List.map (fun (_,th) -> bridge_flat_th th) (bridge_int_hyps asl) in
      (* XXVIII.C5 probe: the non-branch bounds.  `BRIDGE_ATOM_BOUNDS_TAC' runs
         after the split, so they are not hypotheses yet; they are closed
         theorems of the word types and are proved here, not assumed. *)
      let atoms =
        setify (List.concat
          (map (fun th -> BRIDGE_INT_ATOMS (concl th)) (aggs @ hyps))) in
      let bounds =
        List.concat (map (fun t ->
            match t with
            | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("bitval",_),_)) ->
                [BRIDGE_BOUND_BITVAL_HI t; BRIDGE_BOUND_NONNEG t]
            | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("val",_),_)) ->
                [BRIDGE_BOUND_VAL_HI (rand (rand t)); BRIDGE_BOUND_NONNEG t]
            | _ -> []) atoms) in
      let facts = bridge_aggregate_facts ~band_only:true aggs (bounds @ hyps) in
      if facts = [] then begin
        bridge_slice_note "HOIST none eqs=%d aggregates=%d hyps=%d bounds=%d"
          (List.length eqs) (List.length aggs) (List.length hyps)
          (List.length bounds);
        ALL_TAC (asl,w)
      end else begin
        bridge_slice_note "HOIST aggregates=%d hyps=%d bounds=%d facts=%d"
          (List.length aggs) (List.length hyps) (List.length bounds)
          (List.length facts);
        EVERY (map ASSUME_TAC facts) (asl,w)
      end
    with e ->
      bridge_slice_note "HOIST failed: %s" (Printexc.to_string e);
      ALL_TAC (asl,w)
in
(* A hypothesis that is only a one-sided bound on one atom (`&0 <= x',   *)
(* `x < &B', `x <= &1', or the same with the atom on the right) is not     *)
(* needed once the oracle has decided that atom; the *relational* ones     *)
(* (`p <= M + N', `M + N < &2 EXP 256', `m < p', a negated comparison) are *)
(* what distinguish the branches.  Keeping the 50-odd bounds in the final  *)
(* call is what exhausted the stack in IX.70, so they are dropped here.   *)
let bridge_lf_is_literal (xs,_) = xs = []
in
let bridge_lf_is_atomic (xs,_) =
  List.length xs = 1 &&
  (Num.eq_num (snd (List.hd xs)) num_1 ||
   Num.eq_num (snd (List.hd xs)) (Num.minus_num num_1))
in
let bridge_lf_of_concl t =
  match t with
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) ->
      (match bridge_lf_of_term a, bridge_lf_of_term b with
       | Some x, Some y -> Some(x, y)
       | _ -> None)
  | _ -> None
in
let bridge_is_direct_bound th =
  match bridge_lf_of_concl (concl th) with
  | Some (x, y) ->
      (bridge_lf_is_atomic x && bridge_lf_is_literal y) ||
      (bridge_lf_is_atomic y && bridge_lf_is_literal x)
  | None -> false
in
let bridge_close_hyps asl =
  List.filter (fun (_,th) -> not (bridge_is_direct_bound th))
    (bridge_int_hyps asl)
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 6c.9 XXVII.B11: sparse Farkas refutation of the relational slice.          *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* The arithmetic branches left after the order/identity routes are still    *)
(* *refutations*: the implicit non-negativity of every `&(val ...)' /          *)
(* `&(bitval ...)' atom (a type fact, `INT_POS', which `INT_ARITH' also uses) *)
(* is enough to make a handful of the relational hypotheses jointly          *)
(* inconsistent.  `INT_ARITH' finds this but pays a rational elimination     *)
(* over the two enormous chain aggregates; the certificate itself is a        *)
(* non-negative integer combination of at most three relational facts that    *)
(* reduces to a negative constant.  This block detects such a certificate on  *)
(* the sparse linear forms alone (`Num' arithmetic), so a no-match spends no  *)
(* kernel inference; the kernel rules run only for the support finally        *)
(* chosen.  Everything is a derived rule and the final identity is an         *)
(* `INT_RING' normalisation, so a wrong guess is a `None' that falls through   *)
(* to the existing slim/full close -- never an unsound theorem.               *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Strict comparisons are tightened to `x + &1 <= y' (`INT_LT_DISCRETE'), so  *)
(* every premise becomes `&0 <= P' for a linear term `P'.  The `&(val ...)'   *)
(* atoms are then cancelled with `&0 <= &(val ...)' (`INT_POS') scaled by the  *)
(* negated residual coefficient.  A support is accepted only when the summed  *)
(* constant `c' is negative, which refutes the branch.                        *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let bridge_int_sub_tm = `(-):int->int->int`
and bridge_int_lt_tm = `(<):int->int->bool`
and bridge_int_zero_tm = `&0:int`
in
let bridge_is_val_atom t =
  match t with
  | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("val",_), _)) -> true
  | _ -> false
in
(* a relation is `(tag, a, b)' with tag 0=`a <= b', 1=`a < b',
   2=`~(a <= b)', 3=`~(a < b)'; the positive term `P' with `&0 <= P' is
   `b - a', `b - (a + &1)', `a - (b + &1)', `a - b' respectively *)
let bridge_farkas_shape_of_thm th =
  match concl th with
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b) -> Some (0, a, b)
  | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) -> Some (1, a, b)
  | Comb(Const("~",_), p) ->
      (match p with
       | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b) -> Some (2, a, b)
       | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) -> Some (3, a, b)
       | _ -> None)
  | _ -> None
in
let bridge_int_succ a = mk_binop bridge_int_add_tm a (bridge_int_lit num_1)
in
(* the positive term `P' with `&0 <= P', built without spending an inference *)
let bridge_farkas_pos_of_shape (tag, a, b) =
  if tag = 0 then mk_binop bridge_int_sub_tm b a
  else if tag = 1 then mk_binop bridge_int_sub_tm b (bridge_int_succ a)
  else if tag = 2 then mk_binop bridge_int_sub_tm a (bridge_int_succ b)
  else mk_binop bridge_int_sub_tm a b
in
(* and the matching kernel theorem `|- &0 <= P' (built only for a chosen fact) *)
let bridge_farkas_pos_thm th (tag, a, b) =
  if tag = 0 then EQ_MP (SYM (ISPECL [b;a] INT_SUB_LE)) th
  else if tag = 1 then
    let th' = EQ_MP (ISPECL [a;b] INT_LT_DISCRETE) th in
    EQ_MP (SYM (ISPECL [b; bridge_int_succ a] INT_SUB_LE)) th'
  else if tag = 2 then
    let th' = EQ_MP (ISPECL [a;b] INT_NOT_LE) th in
    let th'' = EQ_MP (ISPECL [b;a] INT_LT_DISCRETE) th' in
    EQ_MP (SYM (ISPECL [a; bridge_int_succ b] INT_SUB_LE)) th''
  else
    let th' = EQ_MP (ISPECL [a;b] INT_NOT_LT) th in
    EQ_MP (SYM (ISPECL [a;b] INT_SUB_LE)) th'
in
let bridge_pos_of_num k =
  ISPEC (mk_numeral (Num.abs_num k)) INT_POS
in
(* scale `&0 <= P' by a positive integer `k' *)
let bridge_farkas_scale_le th k pos =
  if Num.eq_num k num_1 then (th, pos)
  else
    let ktm = bridge_int_lit k in
    let prod = mk_binop bridge_int_mul_tm ktm pos in
    (MP (ISPECL [ktm;pos] INT_LE_MUL) (CONJ (bridge_pos_of_num k) th), prod)
in
(* `&0 <= &k * atom' for a `&(val ..)' / `&(bitval ..)' atom *)
let bridge_nonneg_atom_thm k atom =
  let ktm = bridge_int_lit k in
  let posatom =
    match atom with
    | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), nm) -> ISPEC nm INT_POS
    | _ -> failwith "farkas: atom is not int_of_num" in
  let prod = mk_binop bridge_int_mul_tm ktm atom in
  (MP (ISPECL [ktm;atom] INT_LE_MUL) (CONJ (bridge_pos_of_num k) posatom), prod)
in
let bridge_add_le th1 t1 th2 t2 =
  (MP (ISPECL [t1;t2] INT_LE_ADD) (CONJ th1 th2),
   mk_binop bridge_int_add_tm t1 t2)
in
let bridge_close_hyps asl =
  List.filter (fun (_,th) -> not (bridge_is_direct_bound th))
    (bridge_int_hyps asl)
in
let BRIDGE_ORACLE_TAC : tactic =
  fun (asl,w) ->
    try
      let keep =
        match bridge_lf_of_term (lhand w), bridge_lf_of_term (rand w) with
        | Some l, Some r -> bridge_lf_atoms (bridge_lf_add l (bridge_lf_neg r))
        | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_ORACLE_TAC: goal is not linear" in
      let eqs = List.filter_map (fun (th) ->
          match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
          | Some f -> Some(th, f) | None -> None) (map snd asl) in
      let rows = List.mapi (fun i (th,f) -> (i, [th], f)) eqs in
      let (defs, resids) = bridge_gauss_jordan keep rows in
      List.iter (fun (v,_,form) ->
          bridge_slice_note "ORACLE def %s : %s"
            (string_of_term v) (string_of_term (bridge_lf_eq form))) defs;
      let ineqs = bridge_lf_ineqs asl in
      let facts = bridge_oracle_facts defs ineqs in
      (* XIX.C1: build the chain aggregates from the per-limb equations, by the
         same weighted sum the human proof performs.  This is *not* a larger
         `INT_ARITH' call; it is a constructed theorem, and its weights are the
         certificate. *)
      let aggregates = bridge_aggregates eqs in
      (* the aggregate decides the top carry; the fact is proved from these *)
      let all_hyps = List.map (fun (_,th) -> bridge_flat_th th) (bridge_int_hyps asl) in
      let agg_facts = bridge_aggregate_facts aggregates all_hyps in
      let facts = facts @ agg_facts in
      bridge_slice_note "ORACLE system defs=%d residual=%d facts=%d aggregates=%d"
        (List.length defs) (List.length resids) (List.length facts)
        (List.length aggregates);
      let facts' = facts in
      (* The close set (XIX.C1/C2): the two *constructed chain aggregates* — the
         raw one is `M + N = W + B^n * c_n', the corrected one is
         `W_cor = W + (B^n - p)' — the emitted fact, and the *bounds* (each
         `&(val w)' in [0, 2^dimindex), each `&(bitval b)' in [0,1]) together
         with the relational hypotheses.  The bounds are not decoration: the
         corrected aggregate plus `W_cor < B^n' is what turns `p <= M+N' into a
         contradiction.  The Gauss-Jordan carry definitions and the residual
         are still excluded — they carry accumulated `B^n' coefficients and are
         what drove IX.78's equality elimination into coefficient blow-up.
         Every antecedent is already in flat canonical form (the IX.78 probe:
         59 flat hypotheses close in 0.205 s, the nested form exhausted 12 GB). *)
      let is_int_eq th =
        match concl th with
        | Comb(Comb(Const("=",_),a),b) -> type_of a = `:int`
        | _ -> false in
      let is_disj th =
        match concl th with
        | Comb(Comb(Const("\\/",_),_),_) -> true
        | _ -> false in
      let side_hyps =
        List.filter (fun th -> not (is_int_eq th) && not (is_disj th)) all_hyps in
      (* non-chain integer equalities (folded zero tests, the top-bit mask
         relation) are branch facts; see `bridge_int_eq_has_carry'. *)
      let extra_eqs =
        List.filter (fun th -> is_int_eq th && not (bridge_int_eq_has_carry th))
          all_hyps in
      bridge_slice_note "ORACLE extra-eqs=%d [%s]" (List.length extra_eqs)
        (String.concat " | " (List.map (fun th ->
             let s = string_of_term (concl th) in
             if String.length s > 100 then String.sub s 0 100 ^ "..." else s)
           extra_eqs));
      let ants = aggregates @ facts' @ side_hyps @ extra_eqs in
      let w_eq = bridge_flat_conv w in
      let w' = rand (concl w_eq) in
      bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close ants=%d size=%d"
        (List.length ants)
        (List.fold_left (fun a th -> a + bridge_term_size (concl th)) 0 ants);
      (* XXIII.G: propositional-refutation fast path (IX.93).
         A branch splitter can leave both a conjunction `P' and its
         AC-equivalent negation `~Q' among the antecedents, so the branch is
         propositionally inconsistent and the whole arithmetic close is
         unnecessary.  `EQ_MP (CONJ_ACI_RULE (mk_eq(P,Q))) pth' transports `P'
         to `Q', `MP (NOT_ELIM nth)' yields `F', and `CONTR w'' closes the
         flattened goal; the final `EQ_MP (SYM w_eq)' applies it to `w'.  On
         `neg' branches this is ~500x cheaper than the full close (108
         inferences vs ~50,000; IX.93).  Try it first on every branch; a
         failed match falls through to the slim and full closes unchanged.
         Only a `Failure' from CONJ_ACI_RULE (P, Q not AC-equivalent) is an
         expected no-match; a Failure from the later steps is an implementation
         error and is re-raised (XXVI.A3). *)
      let bridge_is_conj t =
        match t with Comb(Comb(Const("/\\",_),_),_) -> true | _ -> false in
      let conj_ants =
        List.filter_map (fun th ->
            let t = concl th in
            if bridge_is_conj t then Some (th, t) else None) ants in
      let neg_ants =
        List.filter_map (fun th ->
            match concl th with
            | Comb(Const("~",_),q) when bridge_is_conj q -> Some (th, q)
            | _ -> None) ants in
      let prop_closed =
        let rec first_neg pth p ns =
          match ns with
          | [] -> None
          | (nth, q) :: rest ->
              let ac =
                (try Some (CONJ_ACI_RULE (mk_eq (p, q)))
                 with Failure _ -> None) in
              (match ac with
               | None -> first_neg pth p rest
               | Some ac ->
                   let pq = EQ_MP ac pth in
                   let fth = MP (NOT_ELIM nth) pq in
                   let gth = CONTR w' fth in
                   Some (EQ_MP (SYM w_eq) gth)) in
        let rec first_pos ps =
          match ps with
          | [] -> None
          | (pth, p) :: rest ->
              (match first_neg pth p neg_ants with
               | Some closed -> Some closed
               | None -> first_pos rest) in
        first_pos conj_ants in
      match prop_closed with
      | Some closed ->
          bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close prop-refutation ants=%d"
            (List.length ants);
          ACCEPT_TAC closed (asl,w)
      | None ->
      bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close prop-nomatch ants=%d" (List.length ants);
      (* XXIII.G: range-refutation fast path.  A branch can carry both a
         non-negativity bound `&0 <= &(val x)' and an equation that pins the
         same atom below zero, `&(val x) + &k = &0' (or `&(val x) = -- &k')
         with numeral `k > 0'.  The pair is unsatisfiable over the integers and
         the whole arithmetic close is unnecessary.  The proof is a hand chain
         of order rules, not a fresh `INT_ARITH' call: the equation is oriented
         to `v = -- &k' (`INT_EQ_SUB_LADD' plus `INT_SUB_LZERO'), rewriting the
         bound gives `&0 <= -- &k', `INT_REDUCE_CONV' proves the literal
         `-- &k < &0' (the numeral `k' is positive, so its negation is strictly
         negative), and `INT_LET_ANTISYM' closes that pair to `F'.  A failed structural match is a `None', not an
         error; anything that raises inside the proof is an implementation
         error and is re-raised (XXVI.A3). *)
      let is_zero_int t =
        match bridge_lf_num t with
        | Some k -> Num.eq_num k num_0
        | None -> false in
      let val_atom t =
        match t with
        | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_), Comb(Const("val",_), x)) -> Some x
        | _ -> None in
      let range_bounds =
        List.filter_map (fun th ->
            match concl th with
            | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_), a), b) when is_zero_int a ->
                (match val_atom b with Some x -> Some (x, th) | None -> None)
            | _ -> None) ants in
      (* Detection must not build proofs: it runs on every branch, and a
         derived theorem constructed here would be paid for even when no
         `&0 <= &(val x)' pairs with the equation.  The normalisation to
         `v = -- &k' is therefore deferred to `refute'. *)
      (* A detected equation is `(atom, k, is_add, add_atom, thm, swap)'.
         `raw = if swap then SYM thm else thm' is `u + &k = &0' when `is_add'
         and `v = -- &k' otherwise; nothing is constructed until a
         non-negativity bound on the same atom is found. *)
      let range_eqs =
        List.filter_map (fun th ->
            let t = concl th in
            if not (is_eq t) || type_of (lhand t) <> `:int` then None else
            let add_of a b swap =
              match a with
              | Comb(Comb(Const("int_add",_), u), kt) ->
                  (match val_atom u, bridge_lf_num kt with
                   | Some x, Some k when Num.lt_num num_0 k && is_zero_int b ->
                       Some (x, k, true, Some u, th, swap)
                   | _ -> None)
              | _ -> None in
            let neg_of a b swap =
              match a with
              | Comb(Const("int_neg",_), kt) ->
                  (match bridge_lf_num kt, val_atom b with
                   | Some k, Some x when Num.lt_num num_0 k ->
                       Some (x, k, false, None, th, swap)
                   | _ -> None)
              | _ -> None in
            let cands =
              [add_of (lhand t) (rand t) false;
               add_of (rand t) (lhand t) true;
               neg_of (lhand t) (rand t) true;
               neg_of (rand t) (lhand t) false] in
            List.fold_left
              (fun acc c -> match acc with Some _ -> acc | None -> c)
              None cands) ants in
      let range_closed =
        let refute bth k is_add uopt th swap =
          let k_tm = bridge_int_lit k and z = bridge_int_lit num_0 in
          let raw = if swap then SYM th else th in
          let eth =
            if is_add then
              (match uopt with
               | Some u ->
                   let h1 =
                     EQ_MP (SYM (ISPECL [u; z; k_tm] INT_EQ_SUB_LADD)) raw in
                   REWRITE_RULE [INT_SUB_LZERO] h1
               | None -> failwith "BRIDGE_ORACLE_TAC: add shape without atom")
            else raw in
          let negk = mk_comb (bridge_int_neg_tm, k_tm) in
          let hb = REWRITE_RULE [eth] bth in
          let hneg =
            EQT_ELIM (INT_REDUCE_CONV
              (mk_binop `(<):int->int->bool` negk z)) in
          (* `INT_LET_ANTISYM' is `~(x <= y /\ y < x)', a negated
             conjunction; `MP' needs an implication, so `NOT_ELIM' turns it
             into `(x <= y /\ y < x) ==> F' before the pair is applied. *)
          let fth =
            MP (NOT_ELIM (ISPECL [z; negk] INT_LET_ANTISYM))
               (CONJ hb hneg) in
          EQ_MP (SYM w_eq) (CONTR w' fth) in
        let rec go bs =
          match bs with
          | [] -> None
          | (x, bth) :: rest ->
              (match List.find_opt
                       (fun (x',_,_,_,_,_) -> aconv x x') range_eqs with
               | Some (_, k, is_add, uopt, th, swap) ->
                   Some (refute bth k is_add uopt th swap)
               | None -> go rest) in
        go range_bounds in
      match range_closed with
      | Some closed ->
          bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close range-refutation ants=%d"
            (List.length ants);
          ACCEPT_TAC closed (asl,w)
      | None ->
      bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close range-nomatch ants=%d" (List.length ants);
      (* XXVII.B9, Task 2a: order-antisymmetry refutation.

         A branch splitter can leave both `a <= b' and `b < a' (or both
         `a < b' and `b < a') among the antecedents.  Over the integers that
         pair is unsatisfiable, and the refutation is the two-premise Farkas
         combination with multipliers `(1,1)': `INT_LET_ANTISYM' is
         `~(x <= y /\ y < x)' and `INT_LT_ANTISYM' is `~(x < y /\ y < x)', so
         `NOT_ELIM' turns the chosen instance into an implication, `CONJ'
         pairs the two hypotheses, `MP' yields `F', and `CONTR w'' closes any
         goal.

         A branch condition may also arrive *negated*: `~(a <= b)' is `b < a'
         (`INT_NOT_LE') and `~(a < b)' is `b <= a' (`INT_NOT_LT').  Those are
         normalised first, so the `~(n <= m)' / `~(m < n)' pair of the `sub'
         branches 19/20 and 23/24 is the same contradiction.  Detection is pure
         `aconv' on the two sides and builds the (single) conversion only on a
         match, so a no-match costs no inferences.  On `sub' this handles
         twelve of the twenty-four branches; the arithmetic close there costs
         ~100,000 inferences for a fact this pair proves in under fifty. *)
      let order_closed () =
        (* the normalised comparison is built lazily, so a no-match spends no
           inference on the `INT_NOT_LE'/`INT_NOT_LT' conversion *)
        let normalise th =
          match concl th with
          | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b) ->
              Some (a, b, true, (fun () -> th))
          | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) ->
              Some (a, b, false, (fun () -> th))
          | Comb(Const("~",_), p) ->
              (match p with
               | Comb(Comb(Const("int_le",_),a),b) ->
                   Some (b, a, false,
                         (fun () -> EQ_MP (ISPECL [a;b] INT_NOT_LE) th))
               | Comb(Comb(Const("int_lt",_),a),b) ->
                   Some (b, a, true,
                         (fun () -> EQ_MP (ISPECL [a;b] INT_NOT_LT) th))
               | _ -> None)
          | _ -> None in
        let ords = List.filter_map normalise ants in
        let le_ants = List.filter (fun (_,_,l,_) -> l) ords
        and lt_ants = List.filter (fun (_,_,l,_) -> not l) ords in
        let close mk mg x y lemma =
          let lth = mk () and gth = mg () in
          let fth =
            MP (NOT_ELIM (ISPECL [x;y] lemma)) (CONJ lth gth) in
          EQ_MP (SYM w_eq) (CONTR w' fth) in
        let swapped_in hay (x, y) =
          List.find_opt (fun (a, b, _, _) -> aconv a y && aconv b x) hay in
        let rec le_first = function
          | [] -> None
          | (x, y, _, mk) :: rest ->
              (match swapped_in lt_ants (x, y) with
               | Some (_, _, _, mg) ->
                   Some (close mk mg x y INT_LET_ANTISYM)
               | None -> le_first rest) in
        match le_first le_ants with
        | Some closed -> Some closed
        | None ->
            let rec lt_first = function
              | [] -> None
              | (x, y, _, mk) :: rest ->
                  (match swapped_in lt_ants (x, y) with
                   | Some (_, _, _, mg) ->
                       Some (close mk mg x y INT_LT_ANTISYM)
                   | None -> lt_first rest) in
            lt_first lt_ants in
      (* XXVII.B5, Task 1: literal and polynomial-AC complements.

         The `CONJ_ACI_RULE' matcher above only sees a contradiction whose two
         sides are conjunction terms.  Two further shapes are left over from a
         branch split, and both are still purely propositional:

           (a) a *literal* complement, an antecedent `P' together with another
               `~P'.  The same `MP (NOT_ELIM nth)' chain closes it with no
               conversion at all; that is the `&0 <= &(val V)' against
               `~(&0 <= &(val V))' pair of the `neg' profile.

           (b) a *polynomial-AC* complement, `P' and `~Q' where `P' and `Q'
               differ only in the association and order of `+' and `*' inside
               their integer subterms.  The decision is `INT_POLY_CONV', the
               ring module's canonical polynomial normaliser: it is a
               *conversion*, not a search, every rewrite is a theorem, and its
               normal form is a fixed function of the polynomial (`int.ml'
               instantiates it with the total order on terms as the variable
               order).  It is applied only after the cheap structural
               prefilter below agrees, so a no-match costs no inferences.

         Both results fold into `slim_closed' below and so return through the
         slim close's `ACCEPT_TAC' line, which is the text the phase
         instrumentation brackets with `bridge:close-exit'; the bracket stays
         exactly one enter/exit pair per branch and the close cost stays its
         difference.  The `ORACLE close prop-kind=...' line names the route. *)
      let bridge_lf_sorted (xs,c) =
        let tagged = List.map (fun (t,k) -> (string_of_term t, t, k)) xs in
        let tagged = List.sort (fun (a,_,_) (b,_,_) -> compare a b) tagged in
        (List.map (fun (_,t,k) -> (t,k)) tagged, c) in
      let rec bridge_ac_norm tm =
        if type_of tm = `:int` then
          (match bridge_lf_of_term tm with
           | Some lf -> bridge_lf_term (bridge_lf_sorted lf)
           | None -> tm)
        else if is_comb tm then
          mk_comb(bridge_ac_norm (rator tm), bridge_ac_norm (rand tm))
        else if is_abs tm then
          mk_abs(fst (dest_abs tm), bridge_ac_norm (snd (dest_abs tm)))
        else tm in
      let rec bridge_ac_norm_conv tm =
        if type_of tm = `:int` then INT_POLY_CONV tm
        else if is_comb tm then
          MK_COMB(bridge_ac_norm_conv (rator tm), bridge_ac_norm_conv (rand tm))
        else if is_abs tm then
          ABS (fst (dest_abs tm)) (bridge_ac_norm_conv (snd (dest_abs tm)))
        else REFL tm in
      let rec bridge_top_head t = if is_comb t then bridge_top_head (rator t) else t in
      let prop_neg_ants =
        List.filter_map (fun th ->
            match concl th with
            | Comb(Const("~",_), q) -> Some (th, q)
            | _ -> None) ants in
      let prop_pos_ants = List.map (fun th -> (th, concl th)) ants in
      let literal_closed () =
        let rec go = function
          | [] -> None
          | (nth, q) :: rest ->
              (match List.find_opt (fun (_, p) -> aconv p q) prop_pos_ants with
               | None -> go rest
               | Some (pth, _) ->
                   bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close prop-kind=literal ants=%d"
                     (List.length ants);
                   Some (EQ_MP (SYM w_eq) (CONTR w' (MP (NOT_ELIM nth) pth)))) in
        go prop_neg_ants in
      let ac_closed () =
        if prop_neg_ants = [] then None else
        let neg_heads = List.map (fun (_, q) -> bridge_top_head q) prop_neg_ants in
        let positives =
          List.filter_map (fun (th, p) ->
              if List.exists (aconv (bridge_top_head p)) neg_heads
              then Some (th, p, bridge_ac_norm p) else None) prop_pos_ants in
        let rec go = function
          | [] -> None
          | (nth, q) :: rest ->
              let qn = bridge_ac_norm q in
              let rec pick = function
                | [] -> go rest
                | (pth, p, pn) :: ps ->
                    if aconv pn qn && aconv (bridge_top_head p) (bridge_top_head q)
                    then
                      (try
                         let pq = CONV_RULE bridge_ac_norm_conv pth
                         and nq = NOT_ELIM (CONV_RULE bridge_ac_norm_conv nth) in
                         (match concl nq with
                          | Comb(Comb(Const("==>",_), qc), _)
                            when aconv qc (concl pq) ->
                              bridge_slice_note
                                "ORACLE close prop-kind=ac ants=%d"
                                (List.length ants);
                              Some (EQ_MP (SYM w_eq) (CONTR w' (MP nq pq)))
                          | _ -> go rest)
                       with e ->
                         bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close ac-conv failed: %s"
                           (Printexc.to_string e);
                         go rest)
                    else pick ps in
              pick positives in
        go prop_neg_ants in
      (* XXVII.B5, Task 2: the linear-identity certificate.  A branch whose
         relational facts are all satisfiable can still have a goal that is an
         exact integer combination of antecedent *equations* (the `neg'
         profile's branch 3: the chain aggregate plus the decided top carry is
         the goal, word for word, once the carry is substituted).  The weights
         are found by exact rational solving over the sparse linear forms --
         one premise, then two, then a greedy elimination -- and are then
         *verified* as integers before any proof is built.  The proof is
         `bridge_eq_scale'/`bridge_eq_add' over the flattened premises, and the
         final identity `(l - r) = (lw - rw)' is a normalisation by
         `INT_POLY_CONV', so the only arithmetic inference spent is that
         normalisation.  Nothing is asserted; a certificate that does not
         verify is a `None' and falls through to the slim and full closes.  The
         search works on string-keyed linear forms (an atom is keyed by its
         printed form, so no `aconv' walks are spent per lookup) and is forced
         only after the two propositional routes miss. *)
      let linear_certificate () =
        let int_goal =
          try is_eq w && type_of (lhand w) = `:int` with _ -> false in
        if not int_goal then None else
        let key_lf (xs,c) =
          let tagged = List.map (fun (t,k) -> (string_of_term t, k)) xs in
          (List.sort (fun (a,_) (b,_) -> compare a b) tagged, c) in
        let rec k_same xs ys =
          match xs, ys with
          | [], [] -> true
          | (a,k) :: xs', (b,j) :: ys' ->
              a = b && Num.eq_num k j && k_same xs' ys'
          | _ -> false in
        let k_equal (fs,fc) (gs,gc) = Num.eq_num fc gc && k_same fs gs in
        let rec k_merge xs ys =
          match xs, ys with
          | [], z -> z
          | z, [] -> z
          | (a,k) :: xs', (b,j) :: ys' ->
              if a = b then
                (let k' = Num.add_num k j in
                 if Num.eq_num k' num_0 then k_merge xs' ys'
                 else (a,k') :: k_merge xs' ys')
              else if compare a b < 0 then (a,k) :: k_merge xs' ys
              else (b,j) :: k_merge xs ys' in
        let k_add (fs,fc) (gs,gc) = (k_merge fs gs, Num.add_num fc gc) in
        let k_scale k (fs,fc) =
          if Num.eq_num k num_0 then ([], num_0)
          else (List.map (fun (a,j) -> (a, Num.mult_num k j)) fs,
                Num.mult_num k fc) in
        let k_at (fs,c) = function
          | None -> c
          | Some a -> (try List.assoc a fs with Not_found -> num_0) in
        let k_zero (fs,c) = fs = [] && Num.eq_num c num_0 in
        let k_int k = Num.eq_num k (Num.floor_num k) in
        let k_keys f = List.map fst (fst f) in
        let goal_key =
          match bridge_lf_of_term (lhand w), bridge_lf_of_term (rand w) with
          | Some a, Some b -> key_lf (bridge_lf_add a (bridge_lf_neg b))
          | _ -> failwith "BRIDGE_ORACLE_TAC: goal is not linear" in
        let gkeys = k_keys goal_key in
        let rows =
          List.filter_map (fun th ->
              match bridge_lf_row_of_thm th with
              | Some f -> let f' = key_lf f in
                          if k_zero f' then None else Some (th, f')
              | None -> None) ants in
        (* the position in `ants', so the certificate can name its premises *)
        let index_in_ants th =
          let rec go i = function
            | [] -> -1
            | u :: rest -> if u == th then i else go (i + 1) rest in
          go 0 ants in
        (* necessary condition for `k1 * f1 + k2 * f2 = goal' with both
           weights nonzero: an atom of one premise that the goal does not have
           must be cancelled by the other premise, and the goal's atoms must be
           covered.  A string-membership test, so the quadratic search below
           only ever runs on plausible pairs. *)
        let pair_viable f1 f2 =
          let k1s = k_keys f1 and k2s = k_keys f2 in
          List.for_all (fun a -> List.mem a gkeys || List.mem a k2s) k1s &&
          List.for_all (fun a -> List.mem a gkeys || List.mem a k1s) k2s &&
          List.for_all (fun a -> List.mem a k1s || List.mem a k2s) gkeys in
        let solve_one f h =
          match fst f with
          | [] -> None
          | (a, k0) :: _ ->
              let k = Num.div_num (k_at h (Some a)) k0 in
              if Num.eq_num k num_0 || not (k_int k) then None
              else if k_equal (k_scale k f) h then Some k else None in
        (* With the one-premise case already excluded, `k1' and `k2' are
           uniquely determined as soon as one coordinate where `(f1,f2)' is
           nonzero is combined with one where the 2x2 determinant is nonzero;
           the anchor is fixed, so this is linear in the coordinates. *)
        let solve_two f1 f2 h =
          if not (pair_viable f1 f2) then None else
          let coords =
            List.map (fun (a,_) -> Some a) (fst f1) @
            List.map (fun (a,_) -> Some a) (fst f2) @ [None] in
          let rec anchor = function
            | [] -> None
            | c :: rest ->
                let a1 = k_at f1 c and b1 = k_at f2 c in
                if Num.eq_num a1 num_0 && Num.eq_num b1 num_0 then anchor rest
                else Some (c, a1, b1) in
          match anchor coords with
          | None -> None
          | Some (c, a1, b1) ->
              let h1 = k_at h c in
              let rec try_second = function
                | [] -> None
                | d :: ds ->
                    let a2 = k_at f1 d and b2 = k_at f2 d and h2 = k_at h d in
                    let det = Num.sub_num (Num.mult_num a1 b2)
                                            (Num.mult_num a2 b1) in
                    if Num.eq_num det num_0 then try_second ds else
                    let k1 = Num.div_num
                               (Num.sub_num (Num.mult_num h1 b2)
                                            (Num.mult_num h2 b1)) det
                    and k2 = Num.div_num
                               (Num.sub_num (Num.mult_num a1 h2)
                                            (Num.mult_num a2 h1)) det in
                    if not (k_int k1) || not (k_int k2) then None
                    else if k_equal
                              (k_add (k_scale k1 f1) (k_scale k2 f2)) h
                    then Some (k1, k2) else None in
              try_second coords in
        let rec first_one = function
          | [] -> None
          | (th, f) :: rest ->
              (match solve_one f goal_key with
               | Some k -> Some [(th, k)]
               | None -> first_one rest) in
        let rec first_two = function
          | [] -> None
          | (th, f) :: rest ->
              let rec inner = function
                | [] -> first_two rest
                | (u, fu) :: us ->
                    (match solve_two f fu goal_key with
                     | Some (k1, k2) -> Some [(th, k1); (u, k2)]
                     | None -> inner us) in
              (match inner rest with
               | Some ws -> Some ws
               | None -> first_two rest) in
        let greedy () =
          let rec step acc res avail depth =
            if k_zero res then Some (List.rev acc)
            else if depth <= 0 then None
            else
              let rec exact = function
                | [] -> None
                | (th, f) :: rest ->
                    (match solve_one f res with
                     | Some k -> Some [(th, k)]
                     | None -> exact rest) in
              (match exact avail with
               | Some ws -> Some (List.rev_append acc ws)
               | None ->
                   (match fst res with
                    | [] -> None
                    | (a, ka) :: _ ->
                        let rec pick = function
                          | [] -> None
                          | (th, f) :: rest ->
                              let k0 = k_at f (Some a) in
                              if Num.eq_num k0 num_0 then pick rest else
                              let k = Num.div_num ka k0 in
                              if not (k_int k) || Num.eq_num k num_0
                              then pick rest else
                              let res' = k_add res (k_scale (Num.minus_num k) f) in
                              if List.length (fst res') < List.length (fst res)
                              then Some (th, k, res') else pick rest in
                        (match pick avail with
                         | None -> None
                         | Some (th, k, res') ->
                             step ((th, k) :: acc) res'
                               (List.filter
                                  (fun (u,_) -> not (aconv (concl u) (concl th)))
                                  avail)
                               (depth - 1)))) in
          step [] goal_key rows 6 in
        (* XXVII.B9, Task 2b: mask-substitution identity search.

           The greedy above only continues while the residual's support
           *shrinks*.  A mask equation `mask + k = val' moves support from
           `mask' to `val' without shrinking it, so a certificate of the shape
           `agg0 + agg1 + B^4 * fact + B^3 * mask_eq' (the `sub' wrap branches)
           is invisible to it: `first_one' and `first_two' cannot reach four
           premises and the greedy rejects the non-shrinking step.  This
           bounded depth-first search accepts any step that cancels the
           residual's leading atom, tries every unused premise (so it
           backtracks, unlike the greedy), and keeps each premise at most once;
           depth 6 with at most five equation premises is a few dozen nodes.
           It runs only after one/two/greedy all miss, so `add' and `neg' keep
           their routes, and the candidate is still *verified* by the
           `INT_POLY_CONV' identity below before any proof is built. *)
        let search () =
          let rec step acc res avail depth =
            if k_zero res then Some (List.rev acc)
            else if depth <= 0 then None
            else
              (match fst res with
               | [] -> None
               | (a, ka) :: _ ->
                   let rec try_rows = function
                     | [] -> None
                     | (th, f) :: rest ->
                         let k0 = k_at f (Some a) in
                         if Num.eq_num k0 num_0 then try_rows rest else
                         let k = Num.div_num ka k0 in
                         if not (k_int k) || Num.eq_num k num_0
                         then try_rows rest else
                         let res' = k_add res (k_scale (Num.minus_num k) f) in
                         let avail' =
                           List.filter
                             (fun (u,_) -> not (aconv (concl u) (concl th)))
                             avail in
                         (match step ((th, k) :: acc) res' avail' (depth - 1) with
                          | Some ws -> Some ws
                          | None -> try_rows rest) in
                   try_rows avail) in
          step [] goal_key rows 6 in
        let cert =
          match first_one rows with
          | Some ws -> Some ws
          | None ->
              (match first_two rows with
               | Some ws -> Some ws
               | None ->
                   (match greedy () with
                    | Some ws -> Some ws
                    | None -> search ())) in
        match cert with
        | None -> None
        | Some weights ->
            let weights =
              List.filter (fun (_, k) -> not (Num.eq_num k num_0)) weights in
            let scaled =
              List.map (fun (th, k) -> (k, bridge_flat_th th)) weights in
            (try
               (match scaled with
                | [] -> None
                | (w0, fth0) :: frest ->
                    let folded =
                      List.fold_left (fun acc (w, th) ->
                          bridge_eq_add acc (bridge_eq_scale th w))
                        (bridge_eq_scale fth0 w0) frest in
                    let sub = `(-):int->int->int` in
                    let l = lhand (concl folded) and r = rand (concl folded) in
                    let lw = lhand w and rw = rand w in
                    let p_fold = INT_POLY_CONV (mk_binop sub l r)
                    and p_goal = INT_POLY_CONV (mk_binop sub lw rw) in
                    if not (aconv (rand (concl p_fold)) (rand (concl p_goal)))
                    then None else
                    let same_diff = TRANS p_goal (SYM p_fold) in
                    let lr_zero =
                      TRANS (AP_THM (AP_TERM sub folded) r)
                        (ISPEC r INT_SUB_REFL) in
                    let zero_th = TRANS same_diff lr_zero in
                    let eq_rule =
                      REWRITE_RULE [INT_ADD_LID]
                        (ISPECL [lw; rw; bridge_int_lit num_0]
                           INT_EQ_SUB_RADD) in
                    bridge_slice_note
                      "ORACLE close linear-cert premises=%d weights=[%s] ants=%d"
                      (List.length weights)
                      (String.concat ","
                         (List.map (fun (th, k) ->
                              Printf.sprintf "#%d:%s" (index_in_ants th)
                                (Num.string_of_num k)) weights))
                      (List.length ants);
                    Some (EQ_MP eq_rule zero_th))
             with e ->
               bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close linear-cert failed: %s"
                 (Printexc.to_string e);
               None) in
      (* XXIII.B3 probe: the close still pays to normalise every direct bound
         (`&0 <= &(val w)', `&(bitval b) < &1', ...).  Those are the antecedents
         `bridge_close_hyps' was written to drop, but the oracle path never used
         it.  Try the set without them first; the anchor line below is the exact
         full-set close and the fallback, so a wrong guess costs one failed
         attempt and cannot change the result. *)
      let slim =
        aggregates @ facts' @
        List.filter (fun th -> not (bridge_is_direct_bound th)) side_hyps @
        extra_eqs in
      (* XXVII.B11: sparse Farkas refutation of the relational slice.  The
         support search below is pure `Num' arithmetic over the sparse linear
         forms; no kernel inference is spent on a no-match. *)
      let farkas_closed () =
        try
          let facts =
            List.filter_map (fun (th) ->
                match bridge_farkas_shape_of_thm th with
                | None -> None
                | Some shape ->
                    let pos = bridge_farkas_pos_of_shape shape in
                    (match bridge_lf_of_term pos with
                     | Some lf -> Some (th, shape, pos, lf)
                     | None -> None))
              ants in
          let nf = List.length facts in
          if nf = 0 then None else
          let arr = Array.of_list facts in
          (* cancel every residual atom with a `&(val ..) >= &0' fact; its
             coefficient must be a non-positive integer *)
          let cancel r =
            let rec go acc = function
              | [] -> Some (List.rev acc)
              | (a,k) :: rest ->
                  if (bridge_is_val_atom a || bridge_is_bitval_atom a) &&
                     Num.le_num k num_0 &&
                     Num.eq_num k (Num.floor_num k)
                  then go ((a, Num.minus_num k) :: acc) rest
                  else None in
            (match go [] (fst r) with
             | Some ms -> Some (snd r, ms)
             | None -> None) in
          let combine idxs ks =
            let r = List.fold_left2 (fun acc i k ->
                let (_,_,_,lf) = arr.(i) in
                bridge_lf_add acc (bridge_lf_scale (Num.num_of_int k) lf))
                ([], num_0) idxs ks in
            cancel r in
          let rec idx_subsets k = function
            | _ when k = 0 -> [[]]
            | [] -> []
            | i :: rest ->
                List.map (fun c -> i :: c) (idx_subsets (k-1) rest) @
                idx_subsets k rest in
          let rec bridge_iota n =
            if n <= 0 then [] else bridge_iota (n-1) @ [n-1] in
          let all_subsets =
            List.concat
              (List.map (fun k -> idx_subsets k (bridge_iota nf)) [1;2;3]) in
          let result = ref None in
          let try_support idxs ks =
            match combine idxs ks with
            | Some (c, ms) when Num.lt_num c num_0 ->
                result := Some (idxs, ks, c, ms)
            | _ -> () in
          (* pass A: supports of size <= 3 with unit multipliers *)
          List.iter (fun idxs ->
              if !result = None then
                try_support idxs (List.map (fun _ -> 1) idxs)) all_subsets;
          (* pass B: small multipliers 1..3, bounded to 300 trials *)
          (if !result = None then begin
             let budget = ref 0 in
             let rec products s =
               if s = 0 then [[]]
               else List.concat (List.map (fun k ->
                     List.map (fun c -> k :: c) (products (s-1))) [1;2;3]) in
             List.iter (fun idxs ->
                 let s = List.length idxs in
                 List.iter (fun ks ->
                     if !result = None && !budget < 300 then begin
                       incr budget; try_support idxs ks end)
                   (products s)) all_subsets
           end);
          match !result with
          | None -> None
          | Some (idxs, ks, c, ms) ->
              let stage = ref "start" in
              (try
                 let parts = ref [] in
                 List.iter2 (fun i k ->
                     stage := Printf.sprintf "pos%d" i;
                     let (th, shape, pos, _) = arr.(i) in
                     let h0 = bridge_farkas_pos_thm th shape in
                     stage := Printf.sprintf "scale%d" i;
                     parts := bridge_farkas_scale_le h0 (Num.num_of_int k) pos
                              :: !parts)
                   idxs ks;
                 List.iter (fun (a,m) ->
                     stage := "nonneg";
                     parts := bridge_nonneg_atom_thm m a :: !parts) ms;
                 (match !parts with
                  | [] -> None
                  | (h0,t0) :: rest ->
                      stage := "add";
                      let (hsum, sum) =
                        List.fold_left (fun (h,t) (h',t') ->
                            bridge_add_le h t h' t') (h0,t0) rest in
                      stage := "ring";
                      let lit = bridge_int_lit c in
                      let hid = prove(mk_eq(sum, lit), CONV_TAC INT_RING) in
                      stage := "ground";
                      let hlt =
                        prove(mk_binop bridge_int_lt_tm lit bridge_int_zero_tm,
                              INT_ARITH_TAC) in
                      stage := "rewrite";
                      let hneg = REWRITE_RULE [SYM hid] hlt in
                      stage := "close";
                      let fth =
                        MP (NOT_ELIM
                              (ISPECL [bridge_int_zero_tm; sum] INT_LET_ANTISYM))
                           (CONJ hsum hneg) in
                      bridge_slice_note
                        "ORACLE close farkas support=%d const=%s"
                        (List.length idxs) (Num.string_of_num c);
                      Some (EQ_MP (SYM w_eq) (CONTR w' fth)))
               with e ->
                 bridge_slice_note
                   "ORACLE close farkas-build failed stage=%s support=[%s]: %s"
                   !stage (String.concat "," (List.map string_of_int idxs))
                   (Printexc.to_string e);
                 None)
        with e ->
          bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close farkas-error: %s"
            (Printexc.to_string e);
          None in
      let slim_closed =
        match literal_closed () with
        | Some closed -> Some closed
        | None ->
        bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close literal-nomatch ants=%d"
          (List.length ants);
        match ac_closed () with
        | Some closed -> Some closed
        | None ->
        bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close ac-nomatch ants=%d" (List.length ants);
        match order_closed () with
        | Some closed ->
            bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close order-refutation ants=%d"
              (List.length ants);
            Some closed
        | None ->
        bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close order-nomatch ants=%d"
          (List.length ants);
        match linear_certificate () with
        | Some closed -> Some closed
        | None ->
        bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close linear-nomatch ants=%d" (List.length ants);
        match farkas_closed () with
        | Some closed -> Some closed
        | None ->
        bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close farkas-nomatch ants=%d" (List.length ants);
        if List.length slim < List.length ants then
          (try
             let th = prove(bridge_mk_imps slim w', INT_ARITH_TAC) in
             bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close slim ok ants=%d (full %d)"
               (List.length slim) (List.length ants);
             Some (EQ_MP (SYM w_eq)
                     (List.fold_left (fun acc h -> MP acc h) th slim))
           with _ ->
             bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close slim failed ants=%d (full %d)"
               (List.length slim) (List.length ants);
             None)
        else None in
      match slim_closed with
      | Some closed -> ACCEPT_TAC closed (asl,w)
      | None ->
      let th = prove(bridge_mk_imps ants w', INT_ARITH_TAC) in
      let closed = List.fold_left (fun acc h -> MP acc h) th ants in
      let closed = EQ_MP (SYM w_eq) closed in
      bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close ok";
      ACCEPT_TAC closed (asl,w)
    with e ->
      bridge_slice_note "ORACLE close failed: %s" (Printexc.to_string e);
      raise e
in
(* A kept branch condition is a *disjunction* (`word_ult s x \/ word_ule p s')
   after normalisation.  Handing that to `INT_ARITH' makes it case-split
   internally, which multiplies the constraint set and exhausted the stack.
   Split it explicitly instead: one branch per disjunct, each conjunctive. *)
let bridge_is_int_disj th =
  match concl th with
  | Comb(Comb(Const("\\/",_),a),b) ->
      let has_int t = List.exists (fun u -> match u with
          | Comb(Const("int_of_num",_),_) -> true | _ -> false)
          (find_terms (fun _ -> true) t) in
      has_int a && has_int b
  | _ -> false
in
let rec BRIDGE_SPLIT_INT_DISJ_TAC (asl,w) =
  match List.find_opt (fun (_,th) -> bridge_is_int_disj th) asl with
  | None -> ALL_TAC (asl,w)
  | Some (_,th) -> (DISJ_CASES_TAC th THEN BRIDGE_SPLIT_INT_DISJ_TAC) (asl,w)
in
(* report the residual goal and hypotheses when a stage does not finish.  It
   prints only under `--mode phase' (csat_mark_enabled), so a normal answer is
   silent; a failure is still a failure. *)
let BRIDGE_ALGEBRA_TAC : tactic =
  let str t =
    let s = string_of_term t in
    if String.length s > 4000 then String.sub s 0 4000 ^ "..." else s in
  let at stage (t:tactic) : tactic =
    fun g ->
      try t g
      with e ->
        let (asl,w) = g in
        bridge_slice_note "ALG_FAIL stage=%s goal=%s" stage (str w);
        List.iteri (fun i (_,th) ->
          bridge_slice_note "ALG_HYP %d %s" (i + 1) (str (concl th))) asl;
        raise e in
  fun g ->
    (at "normalise" BRIDGE_ALG_NORM_TAC THEN
     at "hoist-facts" BRIDGE_HOIST_AGG_FACTS_TAC THEN
     at "split-conditions" BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_KEEP_TAC THEN
     at "renormalise" BRIDGE_ALG_NORM_TAC THEN
     at "zero-fold" BRIDGE_ZERO_FOLD_TAC THEN
     at "decide-bitvals" BRIDGE_DECIDE_BITVALS_TAC THEN
     at "bounds" BRIDGE_ATOM_BOUNDS_TAC THEN
     at "reduce" BRIDGE_INT_REDUCE_TAC THEN
     at "mask-split" BRIDGE_AND_MASK_FACTS_TAC THEN
     at "split-disj" BRIDGE_SPLIT_INT_DISJ_TAC THEN
     at "oracle" BRIDGE_ORACLE_TAC) g
in
(* the same route, with the residue closed algebraically and no SAT call *)
let BRIDGE_FINISH_KEEP_ALG_TAC expand : tactic =
  fun g ->
    (BRIDGE_SPLIT_CONDITIONS_KEEP_TAC THEN
     BRIDGE_ZERO_TEST_TAC THEN
     expand THEN
     RULE_ASSUM_TAC (CONV_RULE BRIDGE_TO_WORD_CONV) THEN
     CONV_TAC BRIDGE_TO_WORD_CONV THEN
     BRIDGE_ALGEBRA_TAC) g
in
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* 7. Entry points.  `pth' is the definition theorem of the modulus, so the  *)
(* numeral replaces the constant before anything is decided.                 *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

let BRIDGE_ZERO_LT_TAC p : tactic =
  SUBGOAL_THEN (mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):num->num->bool`, `0`), p))
   (fun th -> ASSUME_TAC th) THENL [ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC]
in
(* the modulus constant has to be replaced in the assumptions as well as in   *)
(* the goal: the range hypotheses are stated about the constant.            *)
let BRIDGE_REWRITE_MODULUS pth : tactic =
  RULE_ASSUM_TAC(REWRITE_RULE[pth]) THEN REWRITE_TAC[pth]
in
(* add: the spec is `(m + n) MOD p = <written value>' *)
let BRIDGE_ADD_TAC expand pth : tactic =
  ELIM_DIGIT_EQS_TAC THEN BRIDGE_REWRITE_MODULUS pth THEN
  (fun (asl,w) ->
    let (lhs,_) = dest_eq w in
    let (sum,p) = dest_binop `(MOD):num->num->num` lhs in
    let cond = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):num->num->bool`, sum), p) in
    (BRIDGE_ZERO_LT_TAC p THEN
     ASM_CASES_TAC cond THENL
      [ASM_SIMP_TAC[ADD_MOD_LT] THEN BRIDGE_FINISH_TAC expand;
       SUBGOAL_THEN (mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<=):num->num->bool`, p), sum))
         ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
       ASM_SIMP_TAC[ADD_MOD_GE] THEN CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN
       ASM_SIMP_TAC[ADD_GE_SUM] THEN BRIDGE_FINISH_TAC expand]) (asl,w))
in
(* add, through the reference function.  The split above decides `(m+n) MOD p'
   by cases on the modulus; this route carries the MOD inside ADD_REF_VAL_WORD
   instead, so the only per-curve obligation is a pure word equation

     val(ref_add (word p) x y) = val w

   with `x < p' and `y < p' among the bit-level hypotheses.  `expand' is the
   caller's bignum expansion (BIGNUM_OF_WORDLIST_CONV), applied first so the
   written value is a flat digit sum we can fold into one word. *)
let BRIDGE_ADD_REF_TAC expand pth : tactic =
  ELIM_DIGIT_EQS_TAC THEN BRIDGE_REWRITE_MODULUS pth THEN expand THEN
  (fun (asl,w) ->
    let (lhs,wv) = dest_eq w in
    let (sum,p) = dest_binop `(MOD):num->num->num` lhs in
    let (bx,by) = dest_binop `(+):num->num->num` sum in
    let (xw,thx) = BRIDGE_WORD_OF_DIGITS bx in
    let (yw,thy) = BRIDGE_WORD_OF_DIGITS by in
    let (ww,thw) = BRIDGE_WORD_OF_DIGITS wv in
    (* the bounds are ambient hypotheses, stated about the digit sums *)
    let lt tm = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):num->num->bool`, tm), p) in
    let bound tm =
      try snd(List.find (fun (_,th) -> aconv (concl th) (lt tm)) asl)
      with Not_found ->
        failwith "BRIDGE_ADD_REF_TAC: missing `x < p' hypothesis" in
    let hltx = REWRITE_RULE[GSYM thx] (bound bx)
    and hlty = REWRITE_RULE[GSYM thy] (bound by) in
    (* ADD_REF_VAL_WORD at the operand width, with the two bounds discharged *)
    let wt = bridge_finty (bridge_word_width (type_of xw)) in
    let lem = SPECL [p; xw; yw] (INST_TYPE [wt,`:W`] ADD_REF_VAL_WORD) in
    let ants = conjuncts (lhand (concl lem)) in
    if List.length ants <> 4 then
      failwith "BRIDGE_ADD_REF_TAC: unexpected antecedent shape";
    let s1 = prove(List.nth ants 0, CONV_TAC NUM_LT_CONV) in
    let s2 = prove(List.nth ants 1,
      CONV_TAC(RAND_CONV(RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV) THENC
               RAND_CONV NUM_REDUCE_CONV THENC NUM_LT_CONV)) in
    (* the two bounds stay as hypotheses of the rewrite: they are exactly the
       ambient `val x < p' / `val y < p' assumptions, and ASM_REWRITE_TAC
       below discharges the subgoals they create *)
    let rth = MP lem (end_itlist CONJ [s1; s2; hltx; hlty]) in
    let rth = SYM (REWRITE_RULE[thx; thy] rth) in
    (ASM_REWRITE_TAC[rth; SYM thw; ref_add; LET_DEF; LET_END_DEF] THEN
     BRIDGE_FINISH_KEEP_TAC expand) (asl,w))
in
(* the same route with the word residue closed by BRIDGE_ALGEBRA_TAC instead of
   by certified SAT (IX.70).  A separate entry point, so the SAT-free close is
   opt-in per theorem: every other task keeps the emitted tactic it had, and
   its inference count is unchanged.  The gate is in the emitter
   (`src/tools/emit.rs', `ALGEBRAIC_CLOSE_TASKS'), so the choice is visible in
   the emitted answer and recorded per theorem. *)
let BRIDGE_ADD_REF_ALG_TAC expand pth : tactic =
  ELIM_DIGIT_EQS_TAC THEN BRIDGE_REWRITE_MODULUS pth THEN expand THEN
  (fun (asl,w) ->
    let (lhs,wv) = dest_eq w in
    let (sum,p) = dest_binop `(MOD):num->num->num` lhs in
    let (bx,by) = dest_binop `(+):num->num->num` sum in
    let (xw,thx) = BRIDGE_WORD_OF_DIGITS bx in
    let (yw,thy) = BRIDGE_WORD_OF_DIGITS by in
    let (ww,thw) = BRIDGE_WORD_OF_DIGITS wv in
    let lt tm = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):num->num->bool`, tm), p) in
    let bound tm =
      try snd(List.find (fun (_,th) -> aconv (concl th) (lt tm)) asl)
      with Not_found ->
        failwith "BRIDGE_ADD_REF_ALG_TAC: missing `x < p' hypothesis" in
    let hltx = REWRITE_RULE[GSYM thx] (bound bx)
    and hlty = REWRITE_RULE[GSYM thy] (bound by) in
    let wt = bridge_finty (bridge_word_width (type_of xw)) in
    let lem = SPECL [p; xw; yw] (INST_TYPE [wt,`:W`] ADD_REF_VAL_WORD) in
    let ants = conjuncts (lhand (concl lem)) in
    if List.length ants <> 4 then
      failwith "BRIDGE_ADD_REF_ALG_TAC: unexpected antecedent shape";
    let s1 = prove(List.nth ants 0, CONV_TAC NUM_LT_CONV) in
    let s2 = prove(List.nth ants 1,
      CONV_TAC(RAND_CONV(RAND_CONV DIMINDEX_CONV) THENC
               RAND_CONV NUM_REDUCE_CONV THENC NUM_LT_CONV)) in
    let rth = MP lem (end_itlist CONJ [s1; s2; hltx; hlty]) in
    let rth = SYM (REWRITE_RULE[thx; thy] rth) in
    (ASM_REWRITE_TAC[rth; SYM thw; ref_add; LET_DEF; LET_END_DEF] THEN
     BRIDGE_FINISH_KEEP_ALG_TAC expand) (asl,w))
in
(* sub: the spec is `&<written value> = (&m - &n) rem &p' *)
let BRIDGE_SUB_TAC expand pth : tactic =
  ELIM_DIGIT_EQS_TAC THEN BRIDGE_REWRITE_MODULUS pth THEN
  (fun (asl,w) ->
    let (lhs,rhs) = dest_eq w in
    let (diff,p) = dest_binop `(rem):int->int->int` rhs in
    let (m,n) = dest_binop `(-):int->int->int` diff in
    let cond = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(<):num->num->bool`, rand m), rand n) in
    (BRIDGE_ZERO_LT_TAC (rand p) THEN
     ASM_CASES_TAC cond THENL
      [ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_REM_LT] THEN REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_EQ] THEN
       ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_LT_SUM] THEN BRIDGE_FINISH_TAC expand;
       ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_REM_GE] THEN REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_EQ] THEN
       ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_GE_SUM] THEN BRIDGE_FINISH_TAC expand])
    (asl,w))
in
(* neg: the spec is `&<written value> = &((p - n) MOD p)' *)
let BRIDGE_NEG_TAC expand pth : tactic =
  ELIM_DIGIT_EQS_TAC THEN BRIDGE_REWRITE_MODULUS pth THEN
  CONV_TAC REAL_TO_INT_CONV THEN
  (fun (asl,w) ->
    let (_,rhs) = dest_eq w in
    let modtm = rand rhs in
    let (diff,p) = dest_binop `(MOD):num->num->num` modtm in
    let n = rand diff in
    let cond = mk_comb(mk_comb(`(=):num->num->bool`, n), `0`) in
    (BRIDGE_ZERO_LT_TAC p THEN
     ASM_CASES_TAC cond THENL
      [ASM_SIMP_TAC[NEG_MOD_ZERO] THEN BRIDGE_FINISH_KEEP_TAC expand;
       ASM_SIMP_TAC[NEG_MOD_NZ] THEN
       (* NEG_MOD_NZ leaves `&(p - n)' with `&' applied to a *num*
          subtraction.  That atom cannot be wordified (BITBLAST leaves it
          opaque and the equation comes back SAT, measured 24.728 s), and
          INT_OF_NUM_SUB rewrites the wrong way -- its statement is
          `&n - &m = &(n - m)'.  GSYM is the direction that exposes the
          subtraction to the conversion, with `n <= p' the ambient bound. *)
       ASM_SIMP_TAC[GSYM INT_OF_NUM_SUB] THEN
       BRIDGE_FINISH_KEEP_TAC expand])
    (asl,w))
in
(* ========================================================================= *)
(* 8. Reference route for `sub` and `neg`.                                   *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Same shape as `ref_add': the whole modular specification of the operation *)
(* is one word function, and a single generic lemma carries the MOD (or the  *)
(* int `rem'), so every per-task SAT instance is a pure word equation        *)
(*                                                                           *)
(*   val(<written words>) = val(ref_sub (word p) x y)                        *)
(*   val(<written words>) = val(ref_neg (word p) x)                          *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* with `val x < p', `val y < p' (`val x <= p' for neg) among the hypotheses *)
(* and the machine's own accumulator equations (including the flag word's    *)
(* defining equation) among the assumptions.  No flag *meaning* is derived,  *)
(* so no curve-specific comparison has to be proved in real arithmetic: the  *)
(* hardware carry and the reference's word comparison are related inside the *)
(* bit-level instance.                                                       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Note on HOL Light parsing: `-` binds tighter than `+', so `a + p - b' is  *)
(* `a + (p - b)'.  Every statement below is written in that form on purpose; *)
(* SUB_REARRANGE is the bridge between it and the `(a + p) - b' form the     *)
(* subtraction lemmas produce.                                               *)
(* ========================================================================= *)

(* sub: subtract, and add pw back exactly when the subtraction borrowed.    *)
let ref_sub = new_definition
 `ref_sub (pw:W word) (x:W word) (y:W word) =
    let d = word_sub x y in
    if word_ult x y then word_add d pw else d`
in
let MOD_ADD_SELF = prove
 (`!a p:num. (a + p) MOD p = a MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_EQ THEN
  EXISTS_TAC `1` THEN REWRITE_TAC[MULT_CLAUSES])
in
let SUB_REARRANGE = prove
 (`!m n p:num. n <= p ==> (m + p) - n = m + (p - n)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN DISCH_TAC THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC)
in
(* without borrow the machine keeps x - y, which is already the residue *)
let REF_SUB_KEEP = prove
 (`!a b p:num. b <= a /\ a < p ==> a - b = (a + p - b) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + p - b) = (a - b) + p` SUBST1_TAC THENL
   [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[MOD_ADD_SELF] THEN
  CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC)
in
(* with borrow the machine writes (x - y mod 2^k) + p, which wraps to x+p-y *)
let REF_SUB_BORROW = prove
 (`!a b p t s:num.
     a < b /\ b < p /\ p < t /\ s = a + (t - b)
     ==> (s + p) MOD t = (a + p - b) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(s + p) = (a + p - b) + t` SUBST1_TAC THENL
   [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[MOD_ADD_SELF] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + p - b) < p` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `(a + p - b) < t` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  ASM_SIMP_TAC[MOD_LT])
in
(* The one lemma that carries MOD for subtraction; every width, every pw. *)
let SUB_REF_VAL = prove
 (`!(pw:W word) (x:W word) (y:W word).
       0 < val pw /\ val x < val pw /\ val y < val pw
       ==> val(ref_sub pw x y) = (val x + val pw - val y) MOD val pw`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN
   `val(pw:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\
    val(x:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\
    val(y:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W)`
    STRIP_ASSUME_TAC THENL [REWRITE_TAC[VAL_BOUND]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[ref_sub; LET_DEF; LET_END_DEF] THEN BETA_TAC THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[WORD_ULT] THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `val(x:W word) < val(y:W word)` THENL
   [ SUBGOAL_THEN `~(val(y:W word) <= val(x:W word))` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD_ADD] THEN
     MATCH_MP_TAC REF_SUB_BORROW THEN REPEAT CONJ_TAC THENL
      [ ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]; ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
        ASM_SIMP_TAC[VAL_WORD_SUB_CASES] ];
     SUBGOAL_THEN `val(y:W word) <= val(x:W word)` ASSUME_TAC THENL
      [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     ASM_SIMP_TAC[VAL_WORD_SUB_CASES] THEN
     MATCH_MP_TAC REF_SUB_KEEP THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[]])
in
let SUB_REF_VAL_WORD = prove
 (`!p (x:W word) (y:W word).
       0 < p /\ p < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\ val x < p /\ val y < p
       ==> val(ref_sub (word p : W word) x y) = (val x + p - val y) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `val(word p : W word) = p` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD] THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    ALL_TAC] THEN
  FIRST_ASSUM(fun th ->
    MATCH_MP_TAC (REWRITE_RULE[th]
      (SPECL [`(word p : W word)`; `(x:W word)`; `(y:W word)`] SUB_REF_VAL))) THEN
  ASM_REWRITE_TAC[])
in
(* neg: zero if the input is zero, pw - x otherwise. *)
let ref_neg = new_definition
 `ref_neg (pw:W word) (x:W word) =
    if x = word(0:num) then word(0:num) else word_sub pw x`
in
let NEG_REF_VAL = prove
 (`!(pw:W word) (x:W word).
       0 < val pw /\ val x <= val pw
       ==> val(ref_neg pw x) = (val pw - val x) MOD val pw`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN
   `val(pw:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\
    val(x:W word) < 2 EXP dimindex(:W)`
    STRIP_ASSUME_TAC THENL [REWRITE_TAC[VAL_BOUND]; ALL_TAC] THEN
  REWRITE_TAC[ref_neg; GSYM VAL_EQ_0] THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `val(x:W word) = 0` THENL
   [ ASM_REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD_0; SUB_0] THEN REWRITE_TAC[MOD_REFL];
     ASM_SIMP_TAC[VAL_WORD_SUB_CASES] THEN
     CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let NEG_REF_VAL_WORD = prove
 (`!p (x:W word).
       0 < p /\ p < 2 EXP dimindex(:W) /\ val x <= p
       ==> val(ref_neg (word p : W word) x) = (p - val x) MOD p`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `val(word p : W word) = p` ASSUME_TAC THENL
   [REWRITE_TAC[VAL_WORD] THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_REWRITE_TAC[];
    ALL_TAC] THEN
  FIRST_ASSUM(fun th ->
    MATCH_MP_TAC (REWRITE_RULE[th]
      (SPECL [`(word p : W word)`; `(x:W word)`] NEG_REF_VAL))) THEN
  ASM_REWRITE_TAC[])
in
(* the int `rem' specification of sub, brought to the ref_sub residue *)
let SUB_INT_REM_MOD = prove
 (`!p m n:num. 0 < p /\ m < p /\ n < p
    ==> ((&m:int) - &n) rem &p = &((m + p - n) MOD p)`,
  REPEAT GEN_TAC THEN STRIP_TAC THEN
  SUBGOAL_THEN `n <= p` ASSUME_TAC THENL [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
  ASM_CASES_TAC `m < n` THENL
   [ ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_REM_LT] THEN REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_EQ] THEN
     ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_REARRANGE] THEN
     CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC;
     ASM_SIMP_TAC[SUB_REM_GE] THEN REWRITE_TAC[INT_OF_NUM_EQ] THEN
     SUBGOAL_THEN `m + p - n = (m - n) + p` SUBST1_TAC THENL
      [ASM_ARITH_TAC; ALL_TAC] THEN
     REWRITE_TAC[MOD_ADD_SELF] THEN
     CONV_TAC SYM_CONV THEN MATCH_MP_TAC MOD_LT THEN ASM_ARITH_TAC])
in
let BRIDGE_REF2_LEMMAS =
  [MOD_ADD_SELF; SUB_REARRANGE; REF_SUB_KEEP; REF_SUB_BORROW; SUB_REF_VAL;
   SUB_REF_VAL_WORD; NEG_REF_VAL; NEG_REF_VAL_WORD; SUB_INT_REM_MOD]
in
let BRIDGE_SPEC_LEMMAS = BRIDGE_SPEC_LEMMAS @ BRIDGE_REF2_LEMMAS
in
